crit.workflow: T9 blog writing (CIS at f7d310db), plus the T9 social/LinkedIn channels that share its fixers, gates and repair loop. The path runs: T7 slate, T8 angle, input assembly (keyword, FAQ pool, place cards, seed and facts), t9_write, then about 12 deterministic fixers, the F0..F19 gates with the F9 t10_judge, a repair loop of up to 3 attempts, post-loop cuts, approved/held, and the publish gate. Every node in this graph comes from the code: services/acp_content_writing/service.py:1846-2594 (run_write_background), quality_gates.py:2783-2944 (run_quality_gates), shared/llm_client/judge.py and the live route rows in pipeline_stats.raw. The audits were read for evidence but were not used to build the graph.

node_verdicts.node: T7 slate (code + t7_debate_judge LLM + Jev topic fit)
node_verdicts.why: VERIFIED: subject supply is Route grain, and a unique (tenant,channel,route) index allows only 1-2 blogs per tenant ever. The cross-tenant duplication check (F10) runs only after a paid write: 2 of the 5 blogs in the week of 02/11 were held for it. Move a 'subject already published by another tenant / near-duplicate angle' check to slate/T8 time, before any spend. Keep the Jev topic fit.

node_verdicts.node: T8 angle generation (LLM t8_angle_gen) + deterministic angle contract + 1 retry
node_verdicts.why: The deterministic contract is good (acp_angle_gate/generate.py:234-271: foreign brand, forbidden words, thin-moment lead), so keep it. The flaw: the angle is a brief that the writer must follow, but no step checks it against the seed. The F9 verifier never sees it either (service.py:845-875 builds SOURCE without the angle), and the eval judge treats the brief as source (eval_judge.py:96). An angle can therefore commission an unsupported promise, and the writer is then punished for keeping it. Proposal: check the angle's claims against the same fact pack the writer uses, and settle the 'is the brief a source' question once. Writer cut-and-fallback issue also applies: 5 billed_unusable plus 2 truncated on sonnet-5-5 (VERIFIED, pipeline_stats.raw).

node_verdicts.node: T8 ranking (Jev + code ranking.py) + human pick
node_verdicts.why: The ranking uses measurable criteria (avoid-list hits, PAA answered, thin anchor), not LLM opinion, and the human makes the choice. This fits the 'deterministic where possible' principle.

node_verdicts.node: Upstream seed = LLM-written atoms (S1/A3) read via atom_seed_text
node_verdicts.why: VERIFIED: every fact gate (F1, F9, F17, F18) treats the seed as ground truth, but the seed is itself LLM output and its accuracy is never measured for T9. INFERRED: errors upstream pass through as 'supported'. The design needs a measured input, or at least verbatim pointers back to the raw source, of the kind quality/s1_facts.py already builds for S1 (verify_pointers).

node_verdicts.node: Place cards (LLM a3_place_card + a3_place_card_check), re-read into seed (service.py:1789-1806)
node_verdicts.why: VERIFIED: place cards supply the 'place background' that writer, repair, F9, F18 and the eval judge all disagree on (6 different widths of background). Nobody audits their accuracy for T9. Keep the separate checker on a disjoint family (CHECK_PAIRS in llm_route_chains.py). Tag card facts as a distinct allowance tier ('place background') in the fact pack, so policy can treat them differently from trip facts.

Choosing the keyword deterministically with a grounding filter (service.py:407-446) is the right design. It is upstream of F4_seo_surface (23 historical holds) but was never measured. Add it to the funnel metrics and change nothing else.

VERIFIED: the budget drops facts silently (log t9_facts_budget_dropped only), and the gates then hold a claim whose support was dropped. The eval judge also cuts the SEED at 16000 chars while the writer and labels saw it whole (aa900 RC2). Replace this node with ONE typed fact pack built by code: fact ids, kind (trip fact / place background / brand claim / brief), verbatim pointer, and an included/excluded flag. Writer, repair, every gate, the F9 verifier and the eval judge all read the same pack. grounding_text_from (service.py:870-890) already gives F1 and F9 a single builder, so extend it instead of starting over.

node_verdicts.node: FAQ question pool: real_questions + Jev place_paa + LLM t9_faq_filter
node_verdicts.why: VERIFIED contradiction: faq_filter KEEPs visas, weather, costs and travel times (faq_filter.py:90-99). drop_unanswerable_faq then deletes exactly those topics (quality_gates.py:1534-1557), and F16 holds below 3 pairs with no repair. Questions should be decided once, before writing, by one answerability function: question -> answering fact ids from the fact pack, or rejected. The LLM filter could rank inside that set, but its KEEP list must not contradict the code dropper.

node_verdicts.node: t9_write (LLM, sonnet-5-5 chain, effort medium, 12000 ceiling)
node_verdicts.why: VERIFIED: 4 of 187 blogs passed at attempt 1, so the writer contract does not encode the rules that block it. F17 part-of-day/ordinal and F18 rarity are not in the writer prompt, the CTA style it asks for is overwritten by ensure_cta, and it still gets the retired F3 structure rules. Generate the prompt's policy section from one policy file. Ask for structured output (sections, FAQ pairs carrying answer fact ids, citation tags as claim pointers, which [R:]/[F:] tags already are). VERIFIED route flaw: the empty-content max_tokens cut falls silently to sonnet-4-6 (3:3 in the ledger; token_budget.py _own_retry sets budget_retry=False, so token_floor.retry_allowed returns False). The writer route also ends at gpt-6-luna-openai, the same model that answers F9 today, so a fallback-written piece can be judged by its own model.

node_verdicts.node: SEO title/meta fit (LLM t9_repair, up to 2 calls per attempt)
node_verdicts.why: Character bands and keyword coverage are deterministic constraints, and they are handed to an LLM in 3 different bands (prompts.py:192 130-145/155, generate.py fit 120-155, gate 120-158 at quality_gates.py:90-91). The slug is cut mid-word at 60 by code (service.py:908). Have the writer or a cheap call propose 3-5 candidates. Code then selects or trims to ONE band defined once and cuts the slug at a word boundary. F4_seo_surface becomes an assert that cannot fail after the builder.

Keep it as a backstop. The primary duplicate check belongs before the paid write (see T7). An F10 hold after the write cannot be repaired by the loop anyway, because F10 is not sentence-repairable (sentence_repair.py:45-50).

node_verdicts.node: 12 deterministic fixers under step_guard (ai_tells, hygiene, ensure_cta, family caveats, 3 FAQ droppers, real_first_faq, fix_trip_facts, text_integrity, length_trim)
node_verdicts.why: Enforcing in code is right, and the step_guard / repair_contract invariant 7 revert is a strong pattern, so keep both. The flaw is that the fixers act against rules the writer was told to break or was never told about: ensure_cta replaces the 'CTA worked into the last fact' sentence (hygiene.py:2713 vs ai_tells.py:123), and the droppers delete pairs the filter kept. Every fixer must declare the contract it keeps (FAQ >= 3 or the section dropped by rule, 4,700-char floor, CTA once, slug at a word boundary), and the prompt must be generated from the same contract. Collapse them into one normalizer with post-asserts, and run it again after any post-loop edit.

Code cuts pairs, then an LLM puts pairs back, with a different pair count and a different restate rule from the writer (generate.py:466-482 vs prompts.py:59-70). Make it one route in the routing table (regenerate_section: FAQ) that reads the pre-decided answerable questions and fact ids.
It is a local, single-field repair with a deterministic split tried first, and it fits the local-repair principle. Move its routing into the shared routing table.

node_verdicts.node: Deterministic gates F1, F2, F4, F0, F6, F10, F11, F13, F16, F19 (code)
node_verdicts.why: Deterministic checks are the right instrument here. Two adjustments: (a) F1 reads digits only and its grounding includes 'Other trips' lines (VERIFIED in the blog audit), so reuse claim_rules' word-number handling; (b) derive each gate's severity from the taxonomy, because the taxonomy and the code disagree today (other.f7/c3/s5 warn vs F17/F16 block; scope.framing block vs F12 warn).

These regexes encode policy the writer was never given, and no precision or recall has been measured. A deterministic spaCy alternative exists (seed_align tier 1, $0) but is off. Run both over a labelled contradiction fixture suite, keep whichever has measured precision >= 90% per class, and make the rest warn-only.

node_verdicts.node: F9 t10_judge (LLM, 1 call per attempt, hold-capable F9_cta_fact + warn F9_brand_style)
node_verdicts.why: VERIFIED: F9 decides 34 of 99 historical holds. thresholds.yaml shows calibrated:false on 20 entries. Since 05/11 the model answering every verdict is the third rung, gpt-6-luna-openai (72/72), and the chain ends in nova-lite. Judge fallbacks are not marked: _note_fallback_write only marks role=writer (client.py:864-872). The raw reply is not stored; the ledger keeps only status and codes (quality_gates.py:1354-1358). The family check is static per route (judge_writer_family), so a writer falling to gpt-6-luna-openai is judged by the same model. The F9 prompt allows 'who founded it' background, while repair, F18 and the eval judge each draw that line differently. Replace it with a claim verifier that reads the same fact pack: extract the checkable claims, then decide supported / allowed background / unsupported per claim, where only 'promised trip activity, service, time or view not in source' can hold. Pin the model, mark any other rung as degraded, store the raw reply plus input hash, and calibrate against human labels before it may hold. The existing t10_claims / claim_rules.py is the obvious base. Keep the good part of the current F9: a flag counts only with a quoted sentence plus why_not_in_source.

It is a symptom patch for a judge that contradicts itself (in 10 of 15 reverted pieces, the judge flagged a sentence it had passed one attempt earlier). It makes outcomes depend on the path taken. A verifier with claim-level verdicts cached by (claim text, fact-pack hash, model, prompt version) replaces it in a principled way.

node_verdicts.node: seed_align tier1 (spaCy) / t10_adjudicate tier2 / t10_claims / brief_grounding / reader_checklist (dormant)
node_verdicts.why: VERIFIED: 0 calls in 30 days, yet the routes are still maintained by migrations (366). Each is a half-built verifier running parallel to F9/F17/F18. Run each in $0 shadow on a labelled corpus, then promote it with a measured number or delete its code and route. Do not keep more than one live claim verifier.

node_verdicts.node: Repair loop (3 attempts; sentence repair / truth cut / delete_flagged / keep-attempt-2 / full rewrite) + ~9 routing sets
node_verdicts.why: VERIFIED: routing lives in _ELIGIBLE_GATES, CHEAP_REPAIR_GATES, OWNED_BY_FIX_STEP, STYLE_ONLY_GATES, never_holds, TRUTH_CUT_GATES, _cut_gates_repaired and others, spread over a 750-line function. The taxonomy maps gates to classes but no routing code reads it. Replace this with one table generated from the taxonomy: error class -> repair_sentence | cut | regenerate_section | rewrite | hold | warn, with a lint that every gate id has exactly one row. Allow at most one full rewrite. Run attempt 3 only when it can change the outcome. Keep the sentence-level repair mechanics: it fixes F9 about 49% of the time, against 0/6 for a full rewrite.

It compares blocking sets of two attempts that include noisy LLM verdicts, so judge noise can revert a better text. Restrict it to deterministic gates plus claim-level verifier results with stable keys.

node_verdicts.node: Post-loop text edits (_cut_stock_lines, _enforce_authenticity cut, strip_citation_tags, t9_faq_answer_fit LLM drop)
node_verdicts.why: VERIFIED: these change the text after the last run_quality_gates call (service.py:2445-2481). Only _final_integrity re-checks, and it covers F13 residue alone. The stored text is therefore not the text that was gated, and the FAQ count and length floor are not re-asserted. Move them before the final gate pass, or re-run the deterministic gates after them. t9_faq_answer_fit is a validate stage on sonnet-5-5, the writer's own family, and it is not in CHECK_PAIRS.
Failing closed and the degraded[] registry (quality/degraded.py) are the right pattern. Extend it: an F9 verdict from a non-pinned rung, or from nova-lite, counts as degraded.

VERIFIED: held is an admin-only label and the piece publishes anyway (AA-770, standing rule 'tenant always receives content'), so the 3-attempt loop spends money on a verdict with no consequence. The stale comment at service.py:2423-2427 still says publish is gated. Two options, and the choice belongs to the tech lead: (a) keep delivery but stop spending attempt 3 when its only effect is the label; (b) a narrow publish-time block for verified product-truth classes through the existing content_compliance_flag (migration 360) mechanism. Report gate-approved and delivered separately.

node_verdicts.node: Publish gate (subject gate 409, unserved tour, compliance flag)
node_verdicts.why: These are deterministic publish-time checks with a staff release by text sha256. It is the place to attach any product-truth block decision. Reuse it rather than build a new one.

node_verdicts.node: Writing memory (release rules into t9_platform/t9_tenant/repair hints; L0 lexicon -> blocking F2)
node_verdicts.why: VERIFIED: a lexicon rule becomes a BLOCKING F2 finding and enters the prompt after one admin click following an R0 replay (l0.py header). Release rules change the writer and repair prompts (insertion.py). So prompts and gates can change without a PR, and the release fingerprint does not cover them. Put items_sha256 of active releases into the change-control fingerprint. Require a fixture replay that runs the full deterministic chain, not only the R0 stored-verdict replay.

node_verdicts.node: Writing Lab R2 eval judge + golden set
node_verdicts.why: VERIFIED: the eval judge prompt follows a different, looser policy (brief = source, reflection = voice; eval_judge.py:95-96). The golden blog set has 1 human label and 17 agent-panel labels. It evaluates first drafts only, its cost estimate is half the real cost, and it never produced a valid t9_blog run. Generate its rubric from the same policy file, add human labels with a held-out split, and run judge-only rejudges before any paid writer A/B.

VERIFIED: it covers only the t9_write route row and the eval-judge route row. Migration 381 changed t9_write effort and t10_judge silently changed its answering model, and neither change was caught. Widen it to every blog stage route, stage_model_params, mode flags, gate/prompt/policy hashes, writing-memory items_sha256 and the share of answering rungs.

node_verdicts.node: T9 social/LinkedIn branch (F14 shape/first line, F9 cut-not-hold, lead_focus)
node_verdicts.why: It shares the gates and the loop, so every fix above applies to it. Cutting a flagged F9 sentence instead of holding fits a short channel. Metrics must be keyed by channel: the blog cut rate is about 50% at the 12000 ceiling, but averaging it with LinkedIn shows 12%.

One typed, pointer-verified source per piece (seed facts, place background, brand claims, brief, FAQ answers), with included/excluded flags. Writer, fixers, gates, verifier and eval judge all read it. This applies 'facts before prose' and 'verifier sees the same source' in one node. Reuse s1_facts.verify_pointers and grounding_text_from.

node_verdicts.node: ADD: policy compiler (code, one policy.yaml -> prompt fragments, gate severities, judge rubric, label rubric)
node_verdicts.why: This removes the ~10 restatements and the 16 contradictions. A CI test checks that every prompt and rubric carries the same rule ids and hash, and a contradiction fixture suite runs through every deterministic gate and fixer.

VERIFIED: raw writer replies, FAQ-filter verdicts, repair patches and raw judge replies are not stored, and replay_aa924 replays stored F9 verdicts on final texts, so it can report green when the text has changed. Record every LLM request hash and reply per piece, then replay the whole chain (fixers, routing, gates) in CI with zero undeclared diffs. A judge rejudge stays a separate, cents-priced step.

principle_scores.principle: Single source of truth for policy
principle_scores.evidence: VERIFIED. Source fidelity is restated in the writer prompt (prompts.py:258-287), repair (generate.py:280-292), FAQ regen, faq_filter (:90-99), the F9 prose (quality_gates.py:1085-1103), claim_rules (:600-611), the F17/F18 regexes (trip_facts.py), taxonomy.yaml (:103) and eval_judge.py (:84-99). There are 3 meta bands and 6 widths of place background. What earns the 1: grounding_text_from (service.py:870) is a single source builder shared by F1, F9 and the admin rewrite.

principle_scores.principle: Facts/grounding before prose
principle_scores.evidence: The writer gets a prose seed (LLM atoms plus LLM place cards) cut by a silent facts budget (facts.py:40-76). Facts are then reconstructed by regex after the prose (F1 digits, F17/F18). There is no typed fact table for T9 like quality/s1_facts.py for S1. The claim engine (claim_rules / t10_claims) is unwired. What earns the 1.5: citation tags [R:]/[F:] exist, and choose_keyword runs a grounding filter.

principle_scores.principle: Generator and verifier separated; verifier sees the same source
principle_scores.evidence: Good: judge.py imports no writer module, the judge never sees the writer prompt, and a static judge_writer_family route check exists (llm_route_chains.py). Bad (VERIFIED): the t9_write route ends at gpt-6-luna-openai, which is the model answering t10_judge, and no per-call check exists. F9's SOURCE omits the angle brief, the PAA questions and the writing-memory rules the writer got. The eval judge sees the seed cut at 16000 chars and the output cut at 9000 chars. t9_faq_answer_fit validates writer output on the writer's own family (sonnet-5-5).

principle_scores.principle: Deterministic constraints enforced by code, not by asking an LLM
principle_scores.evidence: Mixed. Code enforces the CTA (ensure_cta), length (length_trim) and integrity (text_integrity). But SEO character bands and keyword coverage go to an LLM (up to 2 Haiku calls per attempt), FAQ counts are cut by code and then refilled by an LLM, and the slug is cut mid-word by code (service.py:908). The code enforcers also contradict the prompt (CTA, FAQ topics, F3 rhythm rules).

principle_scores.principle: Repairs local, source-aware, contract-checked after
principle_scores.evidence: Strong parts: sentence repair with ±2 neighbours and only the cited source (_repair_source), splice_checked guards (repeat/specifics/integrity/contract), step_guard on each fixer, and the repair_contract invariants. Weak parts: a full rewrite is still the attempt-2 fallback, and 20% of sentence repairs added a new blocking failure (S234). Post-loop cuts and the answer-fit drop change text after the last gate run (service.py:2445-2481) with only an F13 re-check.

principle_scores.principle: Calibrated, pinned, recorded judges with known error rates
principle_scores.evidence: VERIFIED: thresholds.yaml shows calibrated:false on 20 entries. The t10_judge route is gpt-5.6-luna@acc3 (refused) -> gpt-6-luna@acc3 (refused) -> gpt-6-luna-openai (answers 72/72) -> nova-lite, with no pin. Judge fallbacks are not marked (client.py:864-872 marks writers only). Only status and codes are logged, not the raw reply (quality_gates.py:1354-1358). The R2 eval judge has kappa between -0.07 and 0.32, with 1 human label. The 0.5 is for requiring quoted claims plus why_not_in_source.

principle_scores.principle: Every gate has measured precision/recall or is warn-only
principle_scores.evidence: The Q0 corpus covers only mechanical gates. F1, F4_seo, F9, F12, F15, F17, F18 and F19 have no measured precision or recall, yet F9/F17/F18/F4_seo/F16 can hold. Good: F12 and F9_brand_style are warn-only, and never_holds waives style gates.

principle_scores.principle: Bounded loops with a clear stop
principle_scores.evidence: Bounded: MAX_ATTEMPTS=3, attempt 3 never rewrites, and the gateway caps chain attempts (MAX_CHAIN_ATTEMPTS). Not clear: nested sub-loops (2 SEO-fit calls, FAQ regen once per writer text plus once on 'faq_fell', first-line fix, a contract retry at 2x) and 3-4 model routes give a worst case of about 38 LLM requests (INFERRED in the audit). Whether attempt 3 runs depends on sentence_repair.plan and on revert paths.

principle_scores.principle: Replayable and observable (inputs, raw replies, verdicts stored)
principle_scores.evidence: Stored: writer_input snapshot (service.py:2624), per-attempt gate_ledger in repair_log, discarded_attempts (post-fixer text), ledger rows with billed_unusable, and the R0 replay with f9_results. Not stored: raw writer replies, raw judge replies, FAQ-filter verdicts and repair patches. held_reason keeps only the first failing gate. The replay reuses stored F9 verdicts on changed text, so it can report green when it should not. Failed or processing pieces are excluded from outcome stats.

principle_scores.principle: Change control (prompt/model/effort/route changes gated by eval)
principle_scores.evidence: VERIFIED: the fingerprint covers t9_write plus the eval-judge route only (releases.py:446-476). Migration 381 (effort medium) went live with 0 measured calls. The t10_judge answering model changed with no reverify. L0 lexicon rules become blocking gates after one admin click. R2 for t9_blog never produced a valid run, and quality-paths is report-only.

principle_scores.principle: Cost proportional to value
principle_scores.evidence: 55.6% of t8-t10 spend went to pieces that ended held, and held pieces ship anyway. F10 duplicates are found after the paid write. Cut replies wasted $0.98 of $2.71 Sonnet 5.5 t9_write spend in 30 days. p95 output was 9487 tokens (mostly thinking) for an article of about 1,200 tokens. Every judge call first tries 2 acc3 rungs known to refuse.

principle_scores.principle: (added) A verdict has a product consequence
principle_scores.evidence: VERIFIED: held maps to tenant 'ready' (service.py:2778) and publishes (v1_publish.py:411-414). Phase-1 counts like '69/69 PASS' measure delivery. The loop optimises an admin label.

principle_scores.principle: (added) Inputs measured before they are trusted as truth
principle_scores.evidence: Atoms, place cards, the keyword, the PAA pool and the facts-budget drops are all treated as ground truth, and none has a T9 accuracy measurement (blog audit critic, VERIFIED).

principle_scores.principle: (added) Explicit fail semantics for outages and fallbacks
principle_scores.evidence: Good: the degraded registry, _degraded_final (judge outage = hard -> held), t9_write degrade_mode queue_retry, and budget/stage-switch waits. Bad: a fallback judge verdict (including nova-lite) counts as a full verdict, an empty-content writer cut silently downgrades the model, and t10_judge has degrade_mode null.

structural_flaws: Quality comes from verification and repair, not generation. 4 of 187 blogs passed at attempt 1, and 0 of the last 49 approved did. The writer's contract is not generated from the rules that block it (F17 timing, F18 rarity, CTA form, FAQ topics), so each new failure becomes another downstream gate or fixer. That is how one function grew to 750 lines and 26 gate ids. VERIFIED.

No single policy source. The source-fidelity policy, severity and contracts (meta band, FAQ count, CTA form, length) are restated in about 10 prompts, regexes and rubrics. taxonomy.yaml labels gates but neither drives routing nor generates prompts. A fix in one copy creates a contradiction in another (16 contradictions listed, VERIFIED).

No typed source of truth for facts. The 'source' is prose produced by upstream LLMs (atoms, place cards), cut by a silent budget, and each consumer sees a different version: the writer gets brief, PAA and memory rules; F9 gets grounding_text without the brief; the eval judge gets the seed cut at 16000 and the output cut at 9000. A verifier that does not see the generator's source cannot be calibrated against it.

Hold-capable LLM judging without an instrument record. The F9 judge is uncalibrated and unpinned. Its answering model drifts with refusals while the route row stays the same. Fallback verdicts are unmarked, and the chain ends at nova-lite. Raw replies are not stored. Same-model writer/judge pairs are possible at fallback, because the family rule is checked per route, not per call. The F9PassMemory sticky pass and the regression guard were then built to absorb this judge's noise.

The gated text is not the shipped text. Stock-line cuts, authenticity cuts, the citation strip and the LLM FAQ answer-fit drop all run after the last run_quality_gates. Only F13 residue is re-checked, so the FAQ count, length floor and CTA can break after the verdict.

Routing is spread across about 9 hand-kept sets and branches instead of one table generated from the taxonomy. Outcomes depend on the path taken (revert, truth_cut, cut_only, seo_fields, faq_fell, F14 waiver) and on judge noise. The same text can end approved or held.

The verdict has no consequence. Held pieces reach the tenant as ready and can be published, so up to 3 attempts of spend buy only an admin label, and 'PASS' metrics measure delivery. Whether held should block, or attempt 3 should go, is a product decision that has never been made explicitly against cost.

Cheap checks run after the expensive step. Cross-tenant duplication (F10), subject supply, FAQ answerability and SEO-field fitting are all checked after the paid Sonnet write, though each could be decided before it or in code.

The change surface is mostly outside eval. Route answering rung, effort, ceilings, env mode flags and writing-memory L0/release rules can each change prompts, models or blocking gates without a PR or a fingerprint change. The only paid end-to-end gate (R2 t9_blog) has never produced a valid run, and the free replay reuses stored F9 verdicts, so it can report green after a text change.

Ownership of output-token budget and retry is split. token_budget and the gateway both own retry, and an empty max_tokens cut becomes a silent model downgrade (3:3 in the ledger). Ceilings are per-call-site constants, and effort reaches the model only on the Anthropic Messages path, so the same stage behaves differently depending on which deployment answers.

Parallel half-built verifiers. t10_claims, seed_align tier 1/2, t10_adjudicate, brief grounding and the reader checklist have routes or code but 0 calls, beside the live F9 and F17/F18 regexes. A fix can land in a copy that never runs.

Measurement cannot steer the design. held_reason keeps only the first gate in a fixed order, failed/processing pieces are excluded, cut rates mix channels, raw replies are missing, and live blog volume after 19/10 is 6 pieces. Ground truth is 1 human blog label. Prompt rounds were accepted or reverted inside panel noise about 7x the decision bars.

props.quality_mechanism:
The design rests on four guarantees, each owned by one node.
(1) Same source: every consumer reads one FactPack identified by pack_sha. The writer, repair, every gate, the claim verifier, the eval judge and the label UI all record that sha, and CI fails if any of them builds its own source. A verifier can then be calibrated against exactly what the writer saw.
(2) One policy: writing_policy.yaml generates the writer rules, repair prompts, claim_rules.RulesConfig, severities, route rows and the eval/label rubric. A contract test makes a contradiction between copies a CI failure instead of a hold weeks later.
(3) Code decides, the LLM only describes: the claim verifier's LLM types each sentence and cites a line; apply_rules verifies the quote (a fabricated citation cannot pass) and applies the policy with tripwires. Its error profile is therefore a per-type confusion matrix measured on labelled claims (S232 set: 127 claims), not an opaque verdict. A class may block only when its measured precision is >= 0.9 and recall on the hard subset is >= 9/10; any other class is warn-only by construction (the policy file has no block severity without a calibration run_id). The verifier is pinned. Any other answering rung, a same-family pair or nova-lite counts as degraded, and degraded counts as unavailable, never as a pass.
(4) Delivered text is the gated text and truth-safe: normalize plus post-asserts run before the final gate, the ledger carries text_sha, and residual product-truth sentences are cut, not shipped. Since tenants always receive content, this is the consequence that protects the reader; 'held' is then an honest label about residual non-truth issues.
Stability: the claim cache plus a stop rule on the stable-key blocking set make the outcome independent of the path and of judge noise. Upstream quality lifts first-pass yield: the writer is given the same rules, the FAQ set is decided in code, duplicates are rejected before spend and the SEO fields are built by code. Repair becomes the exception, which is the main lever on cost and quality.
Change safety: every prompt, model, effort, route, flag or memory-rule change moves the fingerprint and must pass the free replay; any change that alters a request hash forces a cents rejudge before it can merge.
props.test_plan:
Proof runs in three tiers. Each tier must be green before the next one starts.
TIER 0, free (CI, about 2-5 min CPU):
(a) Pack parity: FactPack.render() is byte-equal to today's _grounding_text for every stored writer_input_snapshot. Pass: 100%.
(b) Policy contract test: every rendered prompt and rubric carries the same rule ids and policy_sha. The contradiction fixture suite (about 10 synthetic sentences per topic: background, timing, rarity, CTA, FAQ topic, numbers, scope) runs through every fixer, gate and claim_rules in deterministic-only mode (apply_rules({}, ...)). Pass: every sentence gets the policy-expected verdict.
(c) Gateway unit tests: an empty max_tokens reply on rung 0 is retried on the same model at 2x; a judge rung>0 or nova-lite reply is marked degraded; a same-family writer/judge pair is refused or degraded.
(d) Full-chain cassette replay over fixture-1.2.0 (15 blog + 15 LinkedIn) plus stored audit-tenant pieces. Pass: 0 undeclared diffs for each refactor PR, a reviewed expected_diffs.json for each behaviour PR, text_sha(final gate) == stored sha on 100%, and no approved piece flips to held without a declared reason.
(e) Route-table lint: one row per class.
(f) Tripwire and seed_align tier-1 precision on the S232 labelled claims, $0.
TIER 1, cents (judge-only, no writer):
(g) Claim-verifier calibration: run t10_claims pinned on Set A (127 labelled claims, relabelled under the settled policy) plus Set B, 2 runs. Cost per run is about $0.11 (V2a measured $0.1055 per 76 calls in S234). Pass for a class to block: real_kept >= 85% overall and >= 9/10 on the trip_promise + location + number hard subset; over_strict_cleared >= 85%; piece test-retest >= 95% (V2a was 38/38); leaks per exempt type <= 2. Record run_id in thresholds.yaml (calibrated: true). Classes that miss the bar stay warn.
(h) Eval-judge rejudge on the golden set with the rubric generated from policy and the full pack. Cost about $0.06. Pass: per-class recall >= 6/8 pass and 6/10 fail on at least 10 human labels.
(i) Shadow of the new verifier on Tier-0 stored texts, compared with the stored F9 verdicts. The disagreements are labelled by the tech lead (sample about 30).
TIER 2, paid, only after an explicit yes to the item:
(j) A 3-piece trial (about $1.2) with the full new loop on synthetic audit tenants, recording the served model x connection for each call. Abort if any stage is served off its pin.
(k) A fixed sample of 20 distinct blog inputs, old vs new writer contract, plus an A/A' repeat arm. About $8-10 per arm, $20-30 in total (INFERRED from the $0.161 per item measured in R2).
Pass for (k): first-pass yield (no blocking class at attempt 1) >= 30% (today 2%); mean LLM calls per delivered piece <= 6; residual unsupported product promise in delivered text = 0 by the verifier and <= 1/20 by human spot check; no rise in false holds on the labelled set; cost per delivered blog <= $0.25; differences judged at ±2 SE of the A/A' noise.
props.migration_path:
Each step is one PR, merged only when the Tier-0 replay is green. Refactors ship before behaviour changes.
P0 (free, parallel): the funnel query; the cassette recorder in record-only mode; trace_models bound per piece; fallback marks for judge/validate; the same-model empty-cut retry. No output change.
P1: FactPack as a pure refactor (parity test). The eval judge reads the pack with no truncation.
P2: the decision page for the tech lead (place-background width, brief as source or instruction, reflection as voice or embellishment, hypothetical warn or fail, whether a product-truth publish block goes through content_compliance_flag). Then writing_policy.yaml plus generators. The writer-prompt fragment is generated but must stay byte-equal to the current prompt until P7. The eval rubric and RulesConfig switch to it at once. Relabel at least 10-20 blog pieces and the S232 claims under the policy.
P3: Tier-1 calibration of t10_claims (cents). Pin the verifier route. Run it in shadow next to F9 on replays, then on live pieces.
P4: route_table as a pure refactor (0 diffs). Then the declared behaviour diffs: the stop rule, at most 1 rewrite, the generalised truth cut, a regression guard on stable keys only.
P5: promote the claim verifier for calibrated classes only and remove F9PassMemory. F9_brand_style and the uncalibrated classes become warn.
P6: normalize consolidation, post-loop edits moved before the final gate, the text_sha assert, the code seo_builder, the slug fix, FAQ answerable-set and answer ids (answer-fit call removed), and the T7/T8 duplicate precheck plus angle tripwires.
P7: the writer contract (structured reply, generated policy section, F17/F18 rules) through the Tier-2 paid A/B after an explicit yes.
P8: delete the dormant verifiers that were not promoted, with their routes. Widen the fingerprint and make L0 rules warn-only, if not already done in P0. Keep writing-memory releases frozen from P2 until P7 is measured.
Reused unchanged: the gateway and ledger, sentence repair plus splice_checked, step_guard and repair_contract, ensure_cta / length_trim / text_integrity, the degraded registry, the T8 contract plus Jev ranking plus human pick, choose_keyword, the publish gate, Q0 CI and the Writing Lab plumbing.
props.cost_per_item:
Today (VERIFIED from the ledger and audits): one Sonnet 5.5 blog write costs about $0.12-0.16. The upper bound per approved blog is $0.276 over the weeks of 12-19/10, with 55.6% of t8-t10 spend going to pieces that ended held. On the current route the cost is projected at $0.35-0.50 (INFERRED). The worst case is about 38 requests per piece.
Target (INFERRED):
- 1 write: about $0.12-0.15, and less if the cut waste ($0.98 of $2.71 in 30 days) ends.
- Claim extraction: about $0.0014 per call (V2a, S234), run once on the full text plus small re-checks of touched sentences. Below $0.005 per piece.
- 0 SEO-fit calls and 0 answer-fit calls. FAQ ranking: Haiku, about $0.001, or removed.
- 0-2 sentence-repair rounds: about $0.01-0.04 each.

props.quality_mechanism:
What each part guarantees:
1. Contract fields cannot fail: the CTA, slug, title/meta band + keyword, FAQ count and tag residue are produced by code and asserted after every edit, so these gate families (F4_seo, F6, F16, CTA overwrite) disappear by construction.
2. Promises are tied to the raw supplier source. Any sentence that states a trip activity, service, time, view, number or inclusion must cite TRIP or FACT ids whose pointers are proven verbatim (verify_pointers()==[]). Optional and excluded polarity, and the MISSING list, are enforced by code. Place background can cite only PLACE_BG facts about a named place, and the policy file fixes its width once.
3. Type-independent tripwires. Deterministic promise, number, scope and rarity patterns run on every sentence whatever type the writer declared, so a mis-typed 'voice' sentence still gets caught. The narrow verifier question covers the semantic residue.
4. The verifier sees exactly what supports the sentence. Entailment against the cited facts is a much narrower task than today's open F9 over a 16k seed. That makes it measurable: it is calibrated per class against human labels, pinned, recorded and cached, and it holds only for classes with measured precision of 0.9 or above. Everything else is warn-only. A fallback rung is marked degraded and cannot approve or hold on its own.
5. Results do not depend on the path taken. Unchanged sentences keep cached verdicts and only changed sentences are re-checked, so judge noise cannot flip a stable text and no sticky-pass or revert patch is needed.
6. The gated text is the shipped text: no edit happens after the final assert and 4a pass.
7. Generator and verifier are separated. The writer route is Claude-only, the verifier family is non-Claude and checked per call, and the repair model never decides its own acceptance.
8. Change control. Every prompt, model, effort, route, policy or lexicon change alters the fingerprint and must pass the zero-diff full-chain replay plus a cents-priced verifier rejudge on the labelled set before it ships.
9. First-draft quality goes up by design. The writer gets the plan, the fact ids and the generated policy section, so the rules that block a piece are in its contract. KPI: share of sentences with a hold-capable violation at S2, target 25% or less of pieces needing any repair, against today's 4/187 attempt-1 pass (VERIFIED).
props.test_plan:
All steps below run before any paid writer run.

T0, free (unit tests + CI):
- Fact-pack builder tests. Run verify_pointers on the raw source of every route behind the 187 historic blogs (read-only aggregates). Pass: 0 bad pointers; excluded[] reason present for every dropped fact; anchored-atom share reported.
- Policy-compiler hash test across all consumers.
- Contradiction fixture suite: about 10 allowed and forbidden sentences per policy topic, run through 4a and the normalizer. Pass: 100% expected outcomes.
- Normalizer fixtures: hand-written writer JSON, including broken cases (missing cites, 2 FAQ, overlong meta, accented title). Pass: 0 assert breaks after compose, with every failure going to a declared action.
- Routing-table lint: each taxonomy class has exactly one row.

T1, free (offline replay on history):
- Rebuild packs for the stored pieces (writer_input + raw_tours).
- Emulate cites for legacy texts with code lexical alignment (sentence -> best pack facts) and run 4a over the 127 S232 labelled claims, the S245 C1/C2/C3 cases and the golden blog set.
- Report per-class precision and recall of 4a alone against labels, and against today's F1/F17/F18/F9 outcomes.
- Pass: 4a precision 0.9 or above on number, polarity and scope classes. Classes below that start as warn-only.

T2, cents (verifier-only rejudge, judge-only, no writer):
- Run t10_verify twice on the same labelled set with aligned cites, on each candidate pinned non-Claude model. Expected cost about $0.10-0.40 in total, from the measured $0.06 per 18 items for GPT-6 judge-only (INFERRED scaling).
- Pass to hold: on trip_promise/number/location, real_kept 0.9 or above with 10/10 on the hard subset; over_strict_cleared 0.9 or above on place_bg and paraphrase; piece test-retest 0.95 or above; 0 leaks on the voice/place_bg narrow question for the 19 known V2a leak items.
- Add about 40 human sentence labels (we label, held-out split) before reading any number.

T3, small paid subset (needs an explicit yes, vendor API spend):
- 3-blog trial on the audit tenants, new graph behind the flag (about $0.6). Check JSON validity, cassette completeness and zero contract asserts.
- Then a fixed 20-blog sample with three arms: current graph, new graph, and new graph repeated (A/A'). Cap about $12-15.
- Pass:
  - 0 contract breaks;
  - S2 drafts needing any repair 25% or less;
  - final holds on product-truth classes 10% or less;
  - human read of 10 new-graph pieces: 0 unsupported trip promises, and verifier/human sentence agreement 0.9 or above;
  - A/A' held-rate difference inside 2 SE;
  - median LLM requests per piece 5 or fewer;
  - cost per approved blog 60% or less of the old arm.
- Only then: R2 on the Writing Lab with the policy-generated rubric.
props.migration_path:
The new graph is built beside the old one behind T9_GRAPH=v2 (per channel). The old run_write_background stays untouched until the A/B passes.

P0 ($0, shared with the other plans): gateway fixes (single truncation-retry owner, judge identity per verdict, per-call family check, raw-reply storage, nova-lite off hold-capable judge routes), the widened fingerprint and writing_policy.yaml + compiler. The tech lead settles the 3 policy questions on the decision page: background width, brief as source, reflection as voice.

P1 ($0, shadow): fact_pack built for every new T9 piece next to the old seed, with only its hash and stats stored; verify_pointers and excluded[] monitored.

P2 ($0, shadow): 4a runs on live and stored pieces with lexical-aligned cites and is compared with the F1/F9/F17/F18 outcomes. Then T0 and T1.

P3 (cents): t10_verify calibration (T2). Pin the model and set per-class hold/warn in thresholds.yaml with calibration.run_id.

P4: structured writer prompt + composer/normalizer + routing table + cassette. Full-chain replay in CI. Then the T3 trial and the 20-blog A/B.

P5: flip v2 for blog on the audit tenants, then social/LinkedIn (same pack, short JSON, cut before repair). Move the F10/angle pre-spend checks to T8. Delete F9PassMemory, the AA-528 revert, t9_faq_answer_fit, FAQ regen, the post-loop cuts and the dormant verifiers that lost in shadow, and drop their routes by migration.

P6: Writing Lab R2 on the policy-generated rubric and the same pack. From then on every prompt, model or policy change follows the order replay (free) -> rejudge (cents) -> fixed-sample paid run.

Standing rules are unchanged: tenants still receive content (held stays an admin label unless the tech lead opts into a compliance-flag block for measured product-truth classes), elephant-riding pieces are kept and go to human review, and tour country stays the source row.
props.cost_per_item:
INFERRED from the ledger numbers in the blog audit:
- Writer: 1 Sonnet 5.5 call, about $0.12-0.16 (the structured JSON adds a little output; effort stays bounded by stage_model_params).
- Verifier: 1 batched call per text version on a pinned non-Claude model, about $0.005-0.02 (the judge-only GPT-6 cost was about $0.003 per item; per-sentence output is larger).
- Repair: 0-2 Haiku rounds of about $0.003-0.01 each, on failing sentences only.
- SEO field call: rarely, about $0.003.
- Embedding: about $0.001.

Typical total is about $0.14-0.20 per blog with 2-4 requests, and the worst case is about 7 requests, against today's typical 8-12 and worst case about 38. Cost per approved blog drops from today's $0.276 (upper bound) and the $0.35-0.50 projected on the current route to about $0.16-0.22, because the attempt-3 spend and the post-write F10 losses go away. Social pieces cost about a third of that.

One-off validation cost: T0-T2 under $0.50; T3 about $13-16 in total.
risks: The writer self-types its claims and may cite facts that do not support a sentence. The verifier's entailment check exists to catch this, but citation errors add verifier load. Measure the cite-precision of the writer in T3 and add a code recite step before any repair.

Per-sentence JSON can make the prose choppier. Mitigation: cites are per sentence, not per clause; the prose field is free text; the brand-voice warn and the human read in T3 check fluency. Keep a fallback arm where the writer returns prose with inline [R:]/[F:] fact-level tags that code parses into the same structure.

The fact pack makes the raw supplier source the truth, so marketing exaggerations in supplier copy pass. This matches the current policy (source = truth) but should be stated, and the elephant-riding detector still applies over source and output.

Atoms that do not overlap their raw evidence become framing-only, which can shorten thin pieces. The length floor scales with pack richness and an under-floor piece is a warn, not a hold. Decide in the policy file whether that is acceptable for SEO.

The narrow voice/place_bg question may still leak semantic promises (V2a leaked 19 typed-exempt items). The deterministic tripwires cover the lexical part; any class that fails the T2 bar stays warn-only, with human review in the Writing Lab.

Verifier model availability: acc3 denies GPT-6 and Claude 5.x for now, so the pinned verifier is probably GPT-6 Luna via the OpenAI vendor path, or an acc2 non-Claude model if it passes calibration. The vendor_last_resort data rule must be confirmed for the payload (tour and place content only, no personal data). If the pin is unavailable, verdicts become degraded and pieces wait or are labelled; they do not silently pass.

This is a large refactor of a 750-line function that touches every channel. Mitigation: a parallel v2 graph behind a flag, shadow phases, a zero-diff replay for the shared deterministic pieces, and no deletion before the A/B passes.
Small human-label base (1 human blog label today). Per-class precision numbers have wide intervals until about 40 or more sentence labels exist, so default to warn-only until then.
Writing-memory release rules and L0 lexicon must be re-expressed as policy-file entries or normalizer rules. If they stay outside, they bypass the policy compiler again.

props.angle: EVAL-FIRST. Before deciding any node, define a measurable quality contract: a policy file with error classes and severities, a claim-level labelled corpus with a held-out split, pinned judges with known per-class error rates, and cassette replay of recorded raw replies. Then shape the graph so that every node emits a measurable output, every hold-capable gate has measured precision and recall (anything unmeasured is warn-only), and every change to prompt, model, route, effort, policy or memory has to pass the free replay and a cents rejudge first. Fewer LLM gates with known accuracy are preferred over many uncalibrated ones. Concretely: one claim verifier replaces F9, t10_claims, seed_align tier 2 and t10_adjudicate. Deterministic constraints move out of LLM calls (SEO fit, FAQ answer-fit). The writer is asked to emit claim-to-fact pointers so most fidelity checking becomes code. props.quality_mechanism:
Reliability comes from what is measured and enforced, not from more gates.

1. One policy file is compiled into the writer prompt, the repair prompt, gate config, the verifier rubric and the label rubric. Writer, verifier and labellers therefore apply the same rule, checked by a CI hash test, and a rule cannot drift between copies.
2. One typed fact pack is read by every node, so the verifier checks against exactly the source the writer had. verify_pointers ties facts back to raw text, so upstream LLM errors show up as 'derived' or pointer failures instead of silent truth.
3. Code enforces every deterministic constraint: SEO band, slug, CTA, FAQ answerability and count, length, integrity. Post-asserts plus step_guard guarantee that the stored text meets the contract. No edit happens after the last gate pass, so the gated text is the shipped text.
4. The writer emits claim-to-fact tags, so most fidelity decisions become deterministic: the tag must exist, the fact must be included, the quote must match, and the claim_rules tripwires catch a trip promise typed as something else. The single LLM verifier sees only the unsettled sentences, which makes its error surface small and measurable.
5. The verifier is a pinned instrument with per-class precision and recall measured on a human-adjudicated, held-out claim corpus. A class may hold only when measurements.yaml says enforce; every other class is warn-only. Any other rung is degraded and cannot hold. Raw replies are kept in cassettes, so every verdict can be replayed and audited.
6. The repair loop is bounded and convergent: local, source-cited patches; round 2 only on strict improvement; cut, else hold. No sticky-pass hacks are needed, because verdicts are cached per (sentence, fact pack, instrument) and cannot flip on an identical input.
7. Change control: any change to the fingerprint inputs must pass free full-chain cassette replay with zero undeclared diffs. A change to policy or the instrument must also pass the cents rejudge on the held-out split. Only writer changes need a paid run, and that runs once on a fixed sample against the calibrated instrument.
props.test_plan:
TIER 0, free, required on every PR (CI):
(a) Policy compiler hash test: every rendered artefact carries the same policy_hash and rule ids, and no stray restatements remain.
(b) The contradiction fixture suite passes on every deterministic gate and normalizer step. Fire/no-fire twins per class: precision = recall = 1.0 on synthetic cases, and every class has a twin.
(c) Route/param lints: ceiling >= token_floor; writer and judge families differ per call; judge pinned; the router table covers every gate id exactly once.
(d) Unit test: an empty max_tokens reply is retried on the same model at 2x.
(e) Full-chain cassette replay over fixture-1.2.0 (15 blog + 15 LinkedIn), the 18 golden blogs and the stored audit-tenant pieces. Pass = 0 undeclared diffs against expected_diffs.json, and 0 cassette misses treated as passes.
(f) Post-assert sweep on replay outputs: FAQ >= 3 or the section dropped by rule, CTA exactly once, meta in band, slug at a word boundary, length >= floor. Pass = 0 violations.

TIER 1, cents, required when policy, verifier prompt or instrument changes:
Judge-only rejudge of CL-1 (S232 127 claims + sampled S234 flags + golden-blog claims, relabelled under policy v1, tech-lead adjudicated subset) and of the 18 golden blogs' stored texts. Budget < $0.50 per run, no writer calls, so a budget_cap stop is impossible.
Pass on the HELD-OUT split, per hold-capable class (unsupported_trip_promise, contradicted number/name/inclusion): recall >= 0.90 and precision >= 0.90, Wilson lower bound >= 0.80, n >= 20.
Pass on false flags: over_strict false-flag rate <= 10%, against today's measured 20-21/46 = 43-46% (VERIFIED, 05-f9v2-replay.md).
Pass on stability: test-retest claim agreement >= 0.95 over 2 runs, and 0 leaks where a real violation is typed exempt (V2a had 19 leaks).
If a class fails, it stays warn-only and the verifier is fixed in prompt or policy and rejudged at cents. There is no paid rerun.
Also: a shadow run of the new verifier beside current F9 on cassettes of recent pieces, reporting the agreement matrix, at $0 from cache or cents.

TIER 2, small paid, once, needs the tech lead's explicit yes:
3-piece smoke on audit tenants (≈ $1). Pass = completes end to end, 0 post-assert violations, manifest and cassettes complete, no degraded rung.
Then a 20-blog fixed sample: arm A = current graph, arm B = target graph, and an A' repeat of B on 10 pieces to measure noise (≈ $20-30).
Pass for B: first-pass yield (no blocking class at attempt 1 under the calibrated instrument) >= 50%, against 2% today; mean attempts <= 1.5; held rate on enforce classes reported with CI; 0 contract violations in stored text; writer cut rate < 2%; $ per delivered piece <= $0.25.
B is also not worse than A, beyond the A/A' noise band, on the warn-only voice/brand panel scores.
Ship B only if every criterion holds. Afterwards every writer change is measured against this frozen sample and instrument.
props.migration_path:
Phase A (free, instruments first; no behaviour change):
- Measurement funnel SQL and admin view, used as the baseline.
- Token retry fix plus the ceiling lint.
- Judge identity recording, a degraded mark for judge/validate fallbacks, nova-lite counted as unavailable.
- Cassette recorder in the gateway.
- Fingerprint widening.
- Writer route trimmed to sonnet-5-5 -> sonnet-4-6.
- Interim F9 change: warn-only, except quoted invented trip activities, services or times. This is consistent with the standing rule that tenants always receive content.

Phase B (one decision page, then cents):
- The tech lead decides: place-background width, whether the brief is a fact source (proposed: no, only via fact ids), reflection = voice when it makes no factual predicate, which classes are hold-capable, and whether any class blocks at publish.
- Write policy.yaml v1 plus the compiler; render the eval-judge rubric and the label rubric from it.
- Relabel CL-1, get the tech-lead adjudicated subset, freeze the held-out split.
- Build t10_verify on claim_rules and run it in shadow against F9 on cassettes.
- T1 rejudge, then write measurements.yaml.

Phase C (free code behind a flag, proven by T0 replay with declared diffs):
- Fact pack N2 with verify_pointers and recorded exclusions.
- Content plan N3 with answerability.
- Normalizer N5 absorbing the post-loop edits.
- Code SEO selection and the word-boundary slug.
- Contradiction suite.
- Router table N8, F9PassMemory removed, regression guard limited to stable keys.
- Supply check N0.

Phase D (one paid gate):
- Structured writer output N4 with claim tags.
- T2 3-piece smoke, then the 20-blog A/B/A' with the tech lead's yes.
- Flip the flag only if every criterion passes.

Phase E (cleanup):
- Delete dormant verifier code and routes (t10_claims as a separate stage, seed_align tier 2, t10_adjudicate, brief_grounding, reader_checklist, t9_faq_answer_fit) and the routing sets.
- Move writing-memory activation behind the policy overlay plus the T0/T1 gate.

The T9 social/LinkedIn channel reuses N2..N9. Its N8 row for unsupported_trip_promise is 'cut' instead of 'hold', and its metrics stay separate per channel.

Shared with the tour audit (S1/T2), built once: the gateway fixes, the instrument registry, cassettes, policy.yaml (meal rule, background-number rule and meta band shared), the fingerprint and the replay runner.
risks: Label quality: CL-1 starts from agent-panel majorities, and the AA-900 skeptic found contradictory labels on rarity/era/uniqueness. Without the tech lead's adjudicated subset and the policy decisions first, calibration will measure agreement with noise. Mitigation: policy decisions before relabelling, disputed types oversampled for human adjudication.

Low live volume (6 blogs since 19/10) means production metrics cannot steer the design for weeks. Evidence must come from fixtures, cassettes and the one paid fixed sample, and the CIs will be wide (n=20 per class is a floor, not comfort).

Structured, tagged writer output may flatten voice or reduce readability. It is only measured in T2 through warn-only voice/brand scores. If B loses on voice beyond the A/A' band, fall back to free prose with post-hoc claim extraction (claim_rules extraction call) at higher verifier cost.

The writer can tag a sentence with a real but non-entailing fact id. Tag existence is not support, so code entailment rules must be conservative and send uncertain cases to the LLM verifier, otherwise false 'supported' leaks appear. This must be measured as a leak rate in T1.

Pinned instrument availability: acc3 refuses Claude 5.x/GPT-6 today, so the pin sits on gpt-6-luna-openai (vendor API). If OpenAI is down, pieces go degraded and are labelled held, not blocked. A second calibrated instrument doubles T1 cost (still cents). Removing gpt-6-luna-openai from the writer route is needed to keep judge family != writer family.
Cassette storage holds raw tenant-related text. It must live in DB/S3 under existing retention rules, never in the public repos. Only synthetic fixtures go into the repo (taxonomy.yaml rule).

Scope: phases A-C are a large refactor of a 750-line function. A big-bang rewrite would recreate the regression problem, so every step must land behind the T0 replay with declared diffs, flag by flag.
Decision latency: if the policy questions stay open, Phase B stalls, and the interim F9 warn-only setting becomes permanent by default.
The verifier cache keyed by sentence hash can hide a prompt or policy change if the key misses instrument_id or policy_hash. The key must include both, and a CI test must enforce it.

pick.workflow: T9 blog writing (CIS f7d310db), plus the T9 social/LinkedIn channels that share its fixers, gates and repair loop: T7 slate -> T8 angle -> input assembly (keyword, FAQ pool, place cards, seed/facts) -> t9_write -> 12 fixers -> F0..F19 gates + F9 t10_judge -> repair loop (MAX_ATTEMPTS=3, service.py:105) -> post-loop cuts -> approved/held -> publish gate.
pick.winner:
EVAL-FIRST is the spine: instruments, labels and measured gate modes come before any change to behaviour. Two grafts complete it. From EVOLVE comes the in-place, parity-first refactor path: no parallel v2 graph; FactPack grows out of grounding_text_from and claim_rules.number_source_lines; the V2a claim extraction stays as the verifier path for untagged text. From FACTS-FIRST come raw-source anchoring through s1_facts.build_fact_table/verify_pointers, code-composed contract fields, entailment against cited facts only, and the rule that nothing edits the text after the final gate.

Why EVAL-FIRST wins. The failure that has looped for weeks is not a missing node. Rules change without measurement: about 10 restatements of the policy, calibrated:false on 20 thresholds (VERIFIED, grep of services/quality/thresholds.yaml), 0 valid R2 t9_blog runs, and a replay that reuses stored F9 verdicts. Without a measurement contract, EVOLVE's and FACTS-FIRST's graphs would repeat the "fix N breaks fix M" cycle.

Why not FACTS-FIRST outright. It has the highest quality ceiling. But a parallel v2 graph doubles a 750-line maintenance surface during the period we most need to shrink it. Its per-sentence JSON writer is the biggest unproven bet on voice. build_fact_table is single-tour S1 SOURCE_FIELDS (s1_facts.py:510-531, VERIFIED), while a blog route spans several tours and moments, so the pack needs merging and id namespacing (INFERRED, feasible).

Why not EVOLVE outright. Its verifier is V2a extraction typing on free prose. The S234 replay (docs/audits/2026-10-13-S234-t-series-rounds/05-f9v2-replay.md, VERIFIED) shows V2a beats the current F9 on stability (test-retest 38/38 vs 35/38), on over-strict flags cleared (33/46 vs 25-26/46) and on cost ($0.1055 vs $0.2551 per 76 calls). It does NOT beat it on recall: V2a real_kept 34-36/48, while CUR run 2 reached 37/48 with 10/10 on the hard subset. V2a also has 19 exempt-typed leaks (place_background 12, opinion 7). Extraction typing alone will not reach a hold-capable bar. A narrow entailment check against facts the writer itself cited is the path that can.

Final choice for the writer contract. Use prose with inline [F:id]/[R:id] fact tags: the existing citation_tags mechanism, which is FACTS-FIRST's own fallback arm. Do not use per-sentence JSON. Code parses the tags into sentence->cites structure. Title and meta come as 3 candidates each in a small structured header. This keeps the voice risk low and still turns most fidelity checks into code.

structural_flaws: Three incompatible decision variables. The retry loop routes on quality_score (graph.py:1263-1272), publish reads score + audit_status + surviving hard codes (admin_pipeline.py:121-140), and review reads codes. The score is a saturated mean of 4 lint dimensions that start at 10 (graph.py:1223-1236; avg 9.99, p10 10.00), with no fidelity dimension. So the loop never fires on the defects that matter, and hard codes that say 'regenerate' (ITINERARY_DAY_COUNT_MISMATCH, graph.py:233-235) go to review with no regenerate. VERIFIED.

The fact sheet is built for the writer and then thrown away. Every verifier and repair re-derives its own view of the source: meal regex blocks, grounding source_text/unit_source, the judge source with agency fields. flag_fix gets none. A3 extracts 'facts' back out of Master prose. The generator and verifiers do not share one source object, so they disagree by construction. VERIFIED.

Common-mode day check. The day plan and the day-count verifier use the same parser (day_parse.source_day_markers), so a misparse is invisible to both (Japan 12->4 at score 10). The only independent oracle (duration vs markers) sits in shadow. VERIFIED.

Repair is source-blind, field-wide, and not followed by the check that triggered it. flag_fix rewrites whole fields from name/trip_type/duration only (flag_fix_node.py:605-621). _rerepair_meta asks for unsourced 'reassurance/detail'. pre_audit_checks runs only once, inside brand_audit_node, and revalidate explicitly skips it (graph.py:1397-1398), relying on a judge that is report-only. Each new detector therefore feeds a generator of new defects, and the only backstop is the generic repair_contract. This is the engine of the meal / day-loss / forbidden-word loops. VERIFIED.

No single exit contract. Six entries or exits apply different guard sets: hitl -> END, the human-edit revalidation graph, the batch-seed v1 writer graph, the resumed graph, promote, and the unedited server approve. Every new guard added at the end of build_graph (final_day_guard, degraded hold, route_guard) silently misses the other paths. VERIFIED.

Policy is encoded as prose in many copies: writer prompt, meta prompt, flag_fix prompt, audit regex, brand identity prompt, judge rubric, taxonomy, thresholds. Several copies contradict each other (meta band x4, highlights x5, meals x3, the brand identity prompt requires forbidden words). Each fix lands in one copy. VERIFIED.

Judging is inverted relative to value. An uncalibrated, unpinned LLM judge runs twice per repaired tour with no decision role (kappa 0.03, about 10% of S1 spend). The checks that do decide have no measured precision/recall: the meal regex drives 82% of audit codes and whole-itinerary rewrites, the elephant regex has known misses, and Jev 'enforce' never shows UNSUPPORTED_CLAIM. Meanwhile the approve endpoint writes blanket truth labels into Jev's calibration data. VERIFIED (Jev firing rate INFERRED).

Behaviour lives in DB rows and memory releases outside change control. Route chains, effort, token floors, provider order and writing-memory house rules or repair hints change the graph's models and prompts with no replay or eval gate. Repair and judge models can silently change family or version on fallback (flag_fix 0 rows on its configured haiku-5-5; the s1_judge split across two models). VERIFIED.

Human review is an untyped sink. Policy holds (elephant riding, kept by policy) share the manual_check channel with defects. That makes human_edit_gate unreachable for a kept ride (INFERRED deadlock), and the queue has no reason taxonomy, owner or age alert (50 ingested pending). The server approve does not enforce the contract, so review is both the safety net and the bypass. VERIFIED.

Errors propagate down the lineage as truth. A1 Master text feeds A3 atoms (Jev atom check shadow) and the T2 grounding baseline, so one A1 defect becomes a platform fact for every tenant and channel. The graph has no node that checks A1 output against the raw source for fields outside GROUNDED_FIELDS (name, trip_type, seo_title, seo_meta). VERIFIED.

HARD_CODE_REPAIR invariant plus its unit test (every hard-block code names its repair path; graph.py:217-236).

The defects and the wasted spend come from what happens after the writer: a lint score that cannot fail, a judge that decides nothing, source-blind whole-field repairs, detectors that never re-run, and six exits that each skip different guards. The smallest change set:

(2) Replace the score edge and the scattered checks with one deterministic contract_check that emits classified codes. (4) Add one read-only final_contract node that every entry and exit passes.
(5) Take s1_judge off the live path.
(6) Render policy literals from one file.
(7) Gate every prompt, route, effort, policy or memory-release change on a $0 replay of golden 1.1.0 plus the stored v2 pages.

props.quality_mechanism:
What guarantees what (target state):
1. Structural and factual-surface defects cannot reach Master on any path. These are day structure, truncated body or meta, meta band, novel numbers, inclusions the source contradicts, forbidden words and missing fields. They are decided by code in contract_check, and final_contract re-runs them on the final text at the single exit every entry passes, enforced by a topology test. The gate codes have measured precision on golden 1.1.0 (S248 table: day structure TPR 0.88 / TNR 0.86, meta cut TNR 1.00, inclusion TNR 1.00; aa645 gates about 100% on the golden pages). A code acts only when its precision is read (day_oracle discipline, D5 Wilson >= 0.70). Everything else stays REPORT, so the system does not over-hold on unmeasured rules.
2. Invented promises and meaning errors are prevented upstream. Writer v2 writes from a verbatim, code-built fact sheet with restraint rules; the blind panel measured 0.0015 vs 0.051 serious errors per sentence. Rule-7 fact lines and Optional labels are now copied by code, which removes the largest family of false and real meal/clock claims at source. Every sentence, now including the meta, title and name, is then checked per sentence by numeric code plus Jev against the same fact-sheet slice the writer saw.
3. Repairs cannot inject defects. There are no whole-field rewrites. Code fixes come first, then sentence-only LLM repair with the fact-sheet source. repair_contract's 7 invariants (days_kept, no_new_specifics, gates_kept and the rest) run after each edit, and the detectors that fired run again at final_contract. This closes the 'fixed' status that the source-blind flag_fix produced without re-checking (980 'fixed' brand statuses).
4. Loops are bounded and route on meaning. At most 3 drafts, and only for REGENERATE-class codes, with feedback built by code from the fact sheet. Grounding gets 1 repair and 1 re-check. local_fix makes at most 1 sentence-repair call and 1 meta call. Exhausting the drafts ends in final_contract, never in a bypass.
5. Judges become honest. No uncalibrated LLM verdict decides anything live. brand_fit v2 becomes a sampled, pinned, recorded Writing Lab measurement. Jev a1_claim_supported keeps its live role, and the stamp no longer pollutes its labels.
6. Regressions are caught before money is spent. Every prompt, policy, route, effort or memory-release change must pass the $0 replay, which reports per-class TPR/TNR and the publish-flip diff on stored v2 pages. It replays code gates only and does not trust stored LLM verdicts.
7. Policy cannot drift. Literals come from one policy file, and a lint test fails on any copy.
props.migration_path:
The A1 graph switches behind A1_GRAPH_V3 (worker env). T2 stays on build_graph(t2_drafts) unchanged. Each phase is one small PR with a replay result in the PR body.
- P0 ($0): writing_policy.yaml plus the lint test; the fact_sheet column migration (risky PR, independent agent review, then DB Migrate); source_snapshot persisting the fact sheet; scripts/a1_replay over golden 1.1.0 and a stored-page export; final_contract wired to every exit in REPORT mode, logging what it would decide without blocking.
- P1: contract_check and the route edge replace score routing for v2 drafts. The fact line is appended by code and rule 7 is changed. The Optional relabel is done by code. s1_judge leaves the live A1 path (sampled Writing Lab job added). A Tier 0 replay plus a 3-tour paid trial follows.
- P2: local_fix replaces flag_fix and _rerepair_meta for A1. Grounding gains the new fields and the fact-sheet unit source, and the Jev meal/clock claims move into grounding. Then the Tier 1 re-ground and the Tier 2 trial on up to 50 tours. final_contract flips from REPORT to enforce.
- P3: typed review queue (reason codes, HOLD_POLICY, contract check on approve, sentence labels instead of the truth stamp, promote and edit through final_contract, owner/age alert). The elephant detector covers all fields. The batch-seed v1 entry is retired for A1, and s1_source_facts and the nudge are deleted.
- P4: change control. The CI replay check becomes required on the paths listed. The writing-memory release fingerprint gains route, effort and provider order, and release activation is gated by the replay. The shared gateway empty-reply retry is fixed once, with the blog and T2 plans.
- P5: A3 atoms anchored to fact-sheet entries, in shadow until precision is read.
After P2 is stable, T2 adopts contract_check, local_fix and final_contract against its own source baseline in the shared plan.
props.cost_per_item:
Today: about $0.075 per tour (writer about 84%). The S1 judge adds about $0.0075 per tour ($9.66 over 30 days), and flag_fix plus meta re-repair about $0.005 ($6.87), with many outputs reverted.
Target: about $0.060-0.065 per tour. Removing the judge saves about $0.0075. local_fix is mostly deterministic, leaving about $0.001 for residual sentence repairs. Grounding the 4 new fields adds about $0.001 in Jev. The Writing Lab sampled judge costs about $0.15 a week.
Worst case is bounded by the stop rules: 3 writer drafts, 3 meta calls plus their retries, 1+1 grounding repairs, 1 local_fix sentence call and 1 meta call. That is about 12 gateway requests, against about 28 today.
Proof cost: Tier 0 $0; Tier 1 under $0.50; Tier 2 at most $8.
risks: Gate precision rests on small samples. Golden 1.1.0 has only 6 pass-labelled pages, so a code promoted to enforce may over-hold. Mitigation: final_contract ships in REPORT mode first, the stored-page flip diff is reviewed by hand, and NAME_NOT_IN_SOURCE and DAY_PLACE_MISMATCH stay REPORT (S248: TNR 0.50 for names). INFERRED.

Removing the live judge removes the only live voice signal, so voice drift could go unseen between waves. Mitigation: the weekly sampled Writing Lab judge plus the blind panel at every Tier 2. S250 showed brand_fit moving both ways while the panel and the code gates agreed, so the loss is small.

Appending the fact line by code changes the page shape compared with what the S250 panel judged (the writer wrote rule-7 lines then). The arm E result is not re-verified here (INFERRED). Tier 2 must include the panel, not just the code gates.
The fact_sheet column is a schema migration. Its builder_version must be pinned or the replay goes stale. The fact sheet's heuristic place list (capitalised tokens) can produce false name findings.
Extending Jev to seo_meta, title and name may flag marketing phrasing as unsupported (unmeasured precision). It stays REPORT unless Tier 1 reads precision >= 0.7.
The shared graph module diverges while T2 keeps the old path. Mitigation: build_a1_graph lives beside build_graph, and T2 adopts the same nodes in the shared plan.
Stored-page replay can only test code gates. LLM and Jev verdicts in stored rows must not be counted as pass evidence, or the replay goes 'green' falsely (the critic's concern about the blog replay).
When flag_fix leaves A1, T2 still uses it, so the meal and day-loss failure modes stay live on T2 until its plan lands.

Writing-memory releases already active could change the writer prompt while A1_GRAPH_V3 rolls out. The active release state was not read in this audit (INFERRED risk). Pin and record the release per wave.

props.angle: FACTS-FIRST: make the code-built S1 fact sheet the one persisted source object (a "claim contract") that the writer, every check, every repair, review and A3 all read. The LLM writes only the prose slots. Code composes every constrained field (day skeleton, fact lines, facts box, inclusions, optional labels, SEO title/meta fit, trip_type), and one deterministic final_contract decides publish/hold on every path. Core finding (VERIFIED at CIS f7d310db): the parts this design needs already exist but are not wired. build_fact_table entries carry field+quote pointers with verify_pointers (services/quality/s1_facts.py:510-550). source_fact_lines, at_a_glance and assemble_e_page compose fact lines, the facts box and inclusions in code (s1_writer_v2.py:345-528), but only the unused arm E calls them. run_checks, the fact-sheet-aware code checker suite used for the S248/S250 A/B and wave reports (s1_checks.py:403-408), is called ONLY from scripts/aa645/* and scripts/s1_step01/*, never on the live graph. The live graph gates on a saturated score (avg 9.99, p10 10.00, n=814) plus a once-only regex audit and a source-blind field rewriter. So the redesign is mostly re-wiring plus deletion, not new invention. Evidence that facts-first is safe for prose quality: in the S248 A/B on 25 golden tours, W x Sonnet 5.5 (fact sheet in, LLM writes everything) scored 0.0033 serious errors/claim and E x Sonnet 5.5 (code frame + short LLM lines) 0.0065, a gap that was not significant (p=0.128). So keep W's prose, but move only the deterministic slots to code (hybrid "W-prose + E-frame"), and prove non-inferiority on held-out golden tours before any wave.
