props.quality_mechanism:
Each guarantee is assigned to one mechanism:

(1) Structure and constrained fields are correct BY CONSTRUCTION. Day count and order, fact lines, meals, overnight, distance, At a glance, inclusions, Optional labels, trip_type, slug and the meta/title band all come from code over the FS. The LLM cannot produce a meal line, a lost day or an over-long meta, because it never writes those slots. The meta template fallback means the meta can never block a tour.

(2) Source health is checked BEFORE prose. N2 catches parser and duration mismatches and pointer failures on the source side, with an oracle independent of the day_plan parser. That removes the common-mode failure.

(3) Prose fidelity is checked per sentence against the SAME evidence the writer saw: that day's FS entries plus tour-level entries plus the background allowance for named places. Checks are layered by cost and certainty: deterministic numbers, names, inclusions and meal/time-in-prose (fail-closed), then Jev a1_claim_supported per sentence. Jev blocks only once its precision is measured on the corpus, and is otherwise recorded in shadow.

(4) Repairs cannot create new defects unseen. They are sentence-local, see only the unit's evidence quotes, pass repair_contract (no new names or numbers, day headings intact), and are followed by a full contract re-run. A code delete is the final fallback, so the loop has a hard stop: at most 2 drafts, 1 LLM repair round, then delete or review.

(5) One exit gate. Every path to Master (fresh, resumed, hitl, human edit, promote, approve) re-runs the same N9 over the persisted FS. A new detector therefore protects all paths at once, and a graph-level test enforces it.

(6) Every gate has a measured error rate or is warn-only. Each code's mode lives in writing_policy.yaml with the precision evidence id from the replay corpus. A PR that flips a code to enforce must carry that number. This extends the day_oracle discipline (day_oracle.py:48-60) to all codes.

(7) No uncalibrated LLM judge decides anything. The brand-fit judge leaves the live path. The fidelity judge in Writing Lab is pinned, from a different family than the writer, sees the FS, records its model, and is promoted only at kappa >= 0.6. Reviewer per-sentence labels, not blanket approve stamps, are the calibration truth.

(8) Change control. Prompt, policy, route, effort and writing-memory changes stamp each draft and require a replay run, so quality changes are measured instead of discovered in a wave.

(9) Lineage containment. A3 atoms and the T2 baseline come from the FS with code-checked source quotes, so one A1 prose defect cannot become a platform fact.
props.cost_per_item: Today about $0.075 per tour (writer about 84%). Target about $0.060-0.066 per tour. Removed: s1_judge about $0.011 per tour (x2 on repaired tours), the s1_flag_fix whole-field rewrites ($6.87 per 30 d) and _rerepair_meta x3. Kept: writer (about $0.063 on Sonnet 5.5, unchanged or slightly lower because W' no longer writes inclusions or fact lines), meta call (small), Jev grounding (about $0.003 per tour, now also on name/seo fields), and a sentence repair only on flagged units (cheap model, a few hundred tokens). Source-held tours cost $0 in writer spend, because N2 holds before any paid call. Redraft rate should drop below today's, because REGENERATE fires only on real structure codes and the day skeleton is code-fixed. Proof costs: tier 0 $0. Tier 1 about $0.4-1 (Jev on golden 50 plus repair on stored flagged sentences). Tier 2 about $2-3 (W' vs W on 25 held-out golden tours, panel by Claude agents at $0). Then the standard wave ladder (3 -> <=50 tours, about $0.06 each).
risks: W' (prose-only) could read worse than W because code-inserted fact lines and lists break flow. E x Sonnet scored 0.0065 vs W 0.0033 serious errors per claim in S248 (difference not significant, p=0.128). Mitigation: keep W's full narrative slots, move only the deterministic slots, and require non-inferiority on held-out golden tours before any wave.

Code composition depends on the regexes in source_fact_lines and item_lines. A source with unusual fact-line formatting yields no fact line: a silent omission, not an invention. Mitigation: an N2/N9 REPORT code for 'source has day facts but none were composed', with its hit rate read on all 943 raw_tours at tier 0.

Jev a1_claim_supported precision is unknown. UNSUPPORTED_CLAIM never appears in all-time failure codes, so its 'enforce' mode probably never fires (INFERRED). With an unread precision, the sentence-delete fallback could over-delete true sentences. Mitigation: Jev stays shadow until tier 1 reads precision >= 0.9 on golden pages. Only deterministic codes trigger repair or delete until then.

The delete fallback can thin short pages (one-sentence day bodies). Mitigation: delete only when the field keeps at least one sentence, never in name or title. Otherwise the tour goes to review with the code, and per-tour delete counts are reported in the wave report.

The persisted FS adds a schema migration and a staleness question when raw_tours changes. Mitigation: key by source_hash, rebuild on mismatch, and N9 refuses a page whose fact_sheet hash differs from the live source (it extends the existing live-source check in v1_pipeline.py:559-569).

Shared pieces (policy file, gateway retry, replay harness) are also needed by the T2/T9 redesigns. If S1 lands them alone, the copies could fork again. Mitigation: build them once as shared modules in the P0 slice that all three workflows consume.
Removing the live judge removes the only 'voice' signal on S1. Mitigation: a sampled Writing Lab judge plus REPORT style codes. Voice was never gated in practice (report-only today).

A3 moving to FS-derived atoms changes the atom vocabulary T2/T8/T9 read, and could shift tenant outputs. Mitigation: a separate slice after S1 is stable, with an atom diff replay on stored tours ($0) before switching.
props.test_plan:
Tier 0, free replay ($0, every PR touching policy, checks, compose, prompts or routes). Corpus: all 943 raw_tours, the 892 stored Master v2 pages, the 50 golden pages with 2-pass blind panel labels (S248, panel kappa 0.849 on serious-error pages), and stored W/E A/B pages (scripts/aa645 pages.json). Replay re-runs checks from stored inputs; it never reuses stored verdicts. A stored Jev verdict is used only for byte-identical units and is flagged as such, to avoid a false green.

(a) Fact-sheet health. verify_pointers == [] on 100% of sources. DAY_COUNT_VS_DURATION hit list hand-labelled by an agent panel. The code goes to enforce (SOURCE_HOLD) only with precision >= 0.9 on >= 20 hits. Japan and Rajasthan must be caught.

(b) Compose replay. Apply compose_page to the stored W pages (strip the LLM fact line, insert source_fact_lines, at_a_glance, inclusion lists, meta fit or template), then run contract_check. Pass: ITINERARY_MEAL_TIME_INVENTED on fact lines drops to 0, with 0 new day, number, name or truncation codes vs the stored page and 0 metas out of band.

(c) Contract precision and recall vs golden labels, per code. Each code is enforced only if precision >= 0.9 (>= 20 hits) or it is deterministic by definition (day count from the plan, band length). Report recall of the whole contract on serious-error pages; today the s1_judge caught 5/44.

(d) Structural tests. A graph test asserts every entry and exit (fresh, resumed, hitl, edit, promote, approve, batch) reaches publish only through N9. A policy-literal test checks that no band or word list exists outside writing_policy.yaml. The HARD_CODE_REPAIR invariant becomes 'every code has class + mode + repair path'. An elephant tour can be edited and approved with reason policy_keep (deadlock test).

Tier 1, cents rejudge (about $0.4-1). Jev a1_claim_supported on all sentences of the 50 golden W x Sonnet pages, plus name/seo fields, against the FS evidence sets. Read precision and recall vs panel sentence labels and set its mode. sentence_repair on stored flagged sentences from the 980 'fixed' and 124 manual_check tours (sample ~40). Pass: >= 80% clear after one repair with 0 repair_contract violations and 0 new codes. Record the delete-fallback rate.

Tier 2, small paid subset (about $2-3). W' + compose vs current W, both on Sonnet 5.5 with a pinned route and effort, on the 25 held-out golden tours (25:50) never used for tuning. Blind 2-pass Claude-agent panel at $0. Pre-registered pass criteria: serious errors per claim non-inferior to W (bootstrap 95% upper bound of the difference <= +0.003); 0 hard codes after N9; meal/time and meta codes <= W; figure coverage >= W - 0.03; cost per tour <= $0.07; 0 silent fallbacks.

Then the wave ladder per aa-wave-rerun: 3 tours, then <= 50, with the route_version fixed. Wave report: contract clean rate, typed review reasons, cost per stage and $/tour from llm_call_log.

Go-live criterion: >= 90% of wave tours publish on a clean contract, every held tour has a typed reason, and no tour publishes without N9.
props.migration_path:
The design has no real tenants yet, so it migrates in slices, each a PR with its own tier-0 replay. The S1 writer stays on today's live path until P4 passes, and no catalogue rerun happens before P4.

P0 (shared with T2/T9, build once): writing_policy.yaml plus a renderer and the literal test. Replay harness (scripts -> services/quality/replay, running run_checks/day_oracle/contract on a corpus). Gateway same-model retry on an empty max_tokens reply. Ledger fields: route_version, judge/repair model per verdict.

P1: FS persistence. Migration through DB Migrate (risky class: independent reviewer before merge, per dev-phase rules). The writer stores fact_sheet_id and hash. N2 fact_sheet_gate ships in shadow, then DAY_COUNT_VS_DURATION is enforced after (a).

P2: contract_check plus N9 wired on ALL entry and exit paths in shadow. They record findings beside today's gates and change no decision. hitl, edit, promote and approve call N9. Approve stops the blanket truth stamp. Read (c) on the live shadow rows plus the corpus.

P3: switch decisions. Route on classes. N9 decides publish. Enforce the codes that passed (c). Take s1_judge and the s1_brand_audit LLM path off the live path (Writing Lab sampled judge instead). POLICY_HOLD class with the human_edit_gate exemption. Retire the batch seed v1 path, s1_source_facts and the nudge.

P4: W' prompt plus compose_page plus the meta propose/fit/template path plus the sentence_repair node, replacing flag_fix and _rerepair_meta. Gate: tier 1, then tier 2 non-inferiority. Then waves 3 -> <=50 and a single clean catalogue rerun under the pinned route.

P5: A3 atoms from the FS, and the T2 grounding baseline = FS. First a $0 atom-diff replay on stored tours, then a 3-tour paid trial.

Reused as-is: build_fact_table/verify_pointers, day_plan, render_fact_sheet, source_fact_lines/at_a_glance/assemble_e_page pieces, run_checks, day_oracle, repair_contract, the grounding node pattern, forbidden strip, degraded hold, route_guard and the ledger.

props.angle: EVAL-FIRST. Write the S1 quality contract first: taxonomy classes with severities, per-class detectors with measured precision and recall, a labelled v2 corpus, and replay of recorded raw replies. Then shape the graph so a single code-computed contract result is the only decision variable. Each enforcing gate needs a measured precision (Wilson lower bound) recorded in thresholds.yaml, and anything unmeasured is warn-only. Structural facts are copied by code from one persisted SourcePack, so the writer cannot get them wrong. LLM gates are cut to one pinned, recorded sentence verifier that reads the same SourcePack as the writer. Every exit (done, exhausted, human edit, approve, promote, resume) goes through one read-only final_contract. No prompt, route, effort, policy or detector change merges without a $0 replay report, and writer or verifier changes also need a recorded eval run. Evidence base. VERIFIED by my own reads at CIS f7d310db: judge_node.py:369 (report-only), graph.py:1494-1498 (hitl goes to END), flag_fix_node.py:605-621 (source-blind context), grounding.py GROUNDED_FIELDS (subtitle/summary/highlights/itineraries only), day_oracle.py:50-60 (all codes shadow), thresholds.yaml (every row calibrated:false), services/quality/s1_checks.py (offline-only measurement module, 'measurements, not gates'), scripts/s1_step01/fixture_report.py (per-class TPR/TNR with Wilson bounds already built). The S248 confusion table (docs/audits/2026-10-23-S248-s1-step01/results.json, v1 pages, n=50) gives the starting error rates: day_structure TPR 0.875 / TNR 0.857, meta_cut TPR 0.57 / TNR 1.0, number TPR 0.42 / TNR 0.84, name TPR 0.92 / TNR 0.50, inclusion TPR 0.33 / TNR 1.0. The S246 Jev eval (docs/audits/2026-10-21-S246-jev-question-eval) found that a1_claim_supported changes the outcome in under 1% of answers, and about 50% of its number waivers are wrong. Everything else comes from the S271 tour audit and is marked as such.

props.quality_mechanism: What guarantees what. (1) By construction: the day count, day order, day headings, the per-day Distance/Overnight/Meals line, Optional labels, inclusions and country are copied by code from the SourcePack (N3). These classes stop being writer errors and become invariants that N9 asserts. A failure there is a code bug caught by Q0/L1, not a quality gamble. The common-mode parser risk (Japan 12->4) is closed by the independent duration oracle in N0: when parser and duration disagree, the tour becomes SOURCE_HOLD before any spend. (2) One source: writer, meta, repair, verifier, A2 and A3 all read the same persisted SP by sha, so 'verifier sees what generator saw' is checkable (sp_sha on every verdict). (3) One policy: every band and word list is rendered from POL, and lint fails on a stray literal, so a fix cannot land in one copy only. (4) Known error rates: a code enforces only after its precision is read on adjudicated fires and written into thresholds.yaml (calibrated:true with run_id, n, precision, recall). Unmeasured codes are warn, so false holds are bounded by a measured number, and recall gaps are published per class (for example on v1: number TPR 0.42, inclusion TPR 0.33). Those gaps are what the LLM verifier is for. (5) Fewer, calibrated LLM gates: the live graph has one LLM gate, Q-promise, with pinned model, recorded identity, family != writer, and kappa/precision measured on the L2 sentence set. If the served model drifts, the result is degraded, never a pass. The brand_fit judge, with kappa 0.03, leaves the live path. (6) Repairs cannot hide defects: repair is local (the flagged unit), reads the SP unit source, runs under repair_contract, and is followed by the same detector that fired. After the single round, whatever still fails goes to typed review with its codes. (7) No bypass: every exit, including human approve and promote, passes the same N9, and overrides are reason-coded and counted. (8) Regression net: every behaviour change replays the L1 corpus for $0 in CI, and writer/verifier changes need an L3/L4 eval run id, so the fix-loop of the last weeks becomes visible as a fire diff before merge. (9) Labels improve over time: reviewer sentence marks (not blanket truth stamps) grow L2, so detector precision and verifier kappa are re-read monthly.

One-time costs: labelling the L2 set (agent panel + adjudication, no ledger spend). Verifier calibration rejudge about $1-2 (about 600 sentences at about $0.002). Paid trials: 3 tours about $0.25, then 20 tours about $1.5. Total under $5 before any wave; a 50-tour wave about $3.5.
props.test_plan: All steps are in order, and each must pass before the next. Free replay ($0, no LLM). (a) Q0: a positive and a negative unit case for every enforce code, the POL render test and the literal-ban lint, red on base and green on branch. (b) Build the SP for all 943 active raw tours: verify_pointers == 0 on all, SOURCE_HOLD count and list, elephant source matches listed for human review (no rewrite). Pass: 0 pointer mismatches, and every hold has a reason code. (c) Run the unified contract_check and final_contract over the 892 stored v2 Master pages plus the 50 golden pages, giving fires per code. The agent panel adjudicates every fire of each candidate-enforce code (day codes, meal, Optional, meta band, inclusion, number, elephant) into TP/FP. Promotion bar per code: precision >= 0.90, Wilson-95 lower >= 0.75, >= 15 fires. Codes below the bar stay warn. Record the results in thresholds.yaml. (d) Deterministic-repair replay: apply N8a to every stored page with meal/Optional/meta findings and re-run the detectors. Pass: residual enforce findings <= 5% of repaired pages, and 0 repair_contract breaches. (e) Exit replay: run N9 on the stored A2 queue and on approved versions, and count how many approvals would now need an override. This is reported, not gated. Cents rejudge (< $2). (f) Build the L2 labelled set: 60 v2 tours stratified by country, length (> 10 days), meal-heavy, no day markers and elephant, labelled at sentence level with class codes in two independent panel passes. Repeatability must be >= 0.7 agreement, otherwise the rubric is fixed first. (g) Run the pinned verifier (Q-promise, Q-claim) on about 600 L2 sentences. Q-promise enforces only if precision >= 0.85 and kappa >= 0.6 with >= 10 positives; otherwise it stays warn and the gap is reported. The served model must equal the pinned model on 100% of rows, or the run is invalid. Small paid subset. (h) 3 tours on the new path, on the exact served route of the next wave (writer Anthropic API Sonnet 5.5, verifier OpenAI), about $0.25. Pass: day count exact 3/3, 0 enforce findings at publish, served route equal to pinned, no empty-reply fallback. (i) 20 stratified tours, about $1.5. The panel labels new pages and stored v2 pages blind as an A/B. Pass criteria: (1) 0 enforce-class defects among pages N9 calls publishable; (2) serious-defect rate per tour non-inferior to v2 (upper 95% bound of the difference <= +0.1 per tour) and day loss 0/20; (3) the L1 replay still clean; (4) cost <= $0.08/tour; (5) review share reported by reason code. Then the wave ladder of <= 50 per aa-wave-rerun.
props.migration_path:
Reuse first. s1_facts.build_fact_table, day_parse, source_fact_lines, s1_checks.run_checks, fixture_report.py (TPR/TNR + Wilson), day_oracle modes, repair_contract, grounding units, route_guard/degraded, taxonomy.yaml/registry/lint and the Q0 cases all exist and become the core. P0 ($0). Build the L1 corpus from stored v2 pages plus offline SPs. Refresh the S1 golden stratum to v2 pages and start the L2 labelling. Pull the read-only aggregates for the live v2 baseline (the tour audit's step 0).
P1. POL + render + lint + prompt hash test. Prompts change only where copies contradicted each other. The meta band is one value, decided on the decision page.
P2. Persist the SP. N0 source holds and the independent duration oracle start in warn, and become enforce after test (b).
P3. Add final_contract N9 and route all exits through it: hitl, edit, approve, promote, resume. Delete the batch-seed v1 entry. This closes the doors before any behaviour change.
P4. Unify contract_check with registry modes. Flip each code from shadow to enforce only in the PR that carries its precision read (test c).
P5. Writer W prose-only keyed by day ids, plus code assembly (fact lines, headings, Optional). Gated by tests (h) and (i), because this changes the writer.
P6. N8 repair: deterministic first, then sentence repair. Delete flag_fix whole-field and _rerepair_meta. Gated by test (d).
P7. N6 verifier split, GROUNDED_FIELDS extended, Jev number waivers removed, production family guard. Gated by test (g).
P8. s1_judge off the live path; the Writing Lab pinned judge added.
P9. Typed A2 queue + override reasons + sentence marks; remove the truth stamp.
P10. A3 from the SP.
P11. CI change control (L1 replay on paths.yaml-matched PRs, eval_run_id check for LLM changes). Writing-memory A1 releases go through the same gate.
The gateway fixes (empty-reply retry, served-model record, stage_model_params) are shared with T9/T2 and land once, before P5. In the dev phase nothing is live for tenants, so P3-P4 can ship behind the existing S1_WRITER_V2 path, and P5 onward is switched on per wave only after its gate passes.
risks: Labelling capacity: the promotion bar needs >= 15 adjudicated fires per code and a 60-tour sentence-level L2 set. If labelling slips, most codes stay warn, so review volume stays low but recall gaps stay open. Mitigation: the agent panel does first-pass labels, and humans adjudicate only disagreements.

Common-mode SourcePack: once writer and verifier share one SP, a builder bug is invisible to both. Mitigation: verify_pointers == 0, an independent duration oracle that does not use day_parse, and L1 replay of builder_version changes. Still INFERRED residual risk on unusual source formats.
Prose-only, day-keyed JSON may change writer style or flow (stilted joins between LLM prose and code fact lines). It must be measured in the blind A/B (test i), not assumed.

Q-promise may not reach kappa 0.6 on the label set. Like the T9 blog judge, the labels themselves may disagree on rarity/era/background claims. It would then stay warn, and promise-type defects would rely on review plus sampling. The background-scope decision (decision page) must be settled before labelling.
Stored v2 pages in L1 contain v2's own errors. L1 detects behaviour diffs, not truth, so it must never be read as quality evidence alone. Truth comes from L2/L4.
The next S1 wave runs on a served route no S1 tour has used (Anthropic API writer, OpenAI verifier). Test (h) must use exactly that route, or its result does not transfer.
Turning enforce codes on plus the N9 approve check will grow the A2 queue at first. The typed reasons and the age alert must ship with P3/P9, or the queue becomes a sink again.
Jev dependency: if Jev changes version (1.13 -> 1.14 already happened inside the window), Q-promise calibration is stale. The Jev version must be part of the pinned verifier identity.

Writing-memory releases and DB route rows can still change prompts or models outside git. P11 only covers what flows through PRs. Runtime admin edits need the same replay gate, or a freeze during waves.

pick.winner:
Proposal 1 (EVOLVE) is the backbone. It keeps writer v2 and its code-built fact sheet, persists the sheet, replaces score routing with one code contract, swaps flag_fix and _rerepair_meta for local source-aware repair, adds one read-only final_contract on every exit, takes s1_judge off the live path and gates change through a $0 replay.

Why it wins:
- It is the smallest change that removes the engine of the loop: a score that cannot fail, repairs that cannot see the source, detectors that never re-run, and six exits that each skip different guards.
- It does not touch the part that already works. The S250 blind panel measured 0.0015 serious errors per sentence for v2 against 0.051 for live.
- It respects the S250 freeze on new LLM gates.

Proposal 2 (FACTS-FIRST) is the strongest on convergence by construction, but it rewrites the writer's output shape (W' prose-only, with Included and At a glance composed by code). It also deletes sentences on Jev verdicts whose precision has not been measured. That adds writer-side risk before the control plane is fixed.

Proposal 3 (EVAL-FIRST) has the best test discipline, but its 11 phases and a 60-tour labelling job up front slow down closing the bypasses.

- A gateway unit test with a mocked empty max_tokens reply shows the same model retried and no silent family change.

phases.phase: P1 - Measure the gates before any of them acts (v2 truth set)
steps: Build the L2 labelled v2 set: 40-60 stored v2 tours stratified by country, length >10 days, meal-heavy, no day markers, elephant and Optional-heavy. Labels are at sentence and field level with taxonomy class codes, in two independent Claude-agent panel passes, adjudicated. Nghiệp approves the labels. This is needed because golden 1.1.0 is mostly pre-v2 failing pages (S248 README:154, 39/50 with errors), so it cannot measure v2 precision.

Run contract_check (N6) on L2, the stored v2 pages and golden 1.1.0. The panel adjudicates every fire of each candidate-enforce code: day codes, DAY_COUNT_VS_DURATION (source side), meal/clock-in-prose, Optional dropped, meta/title band, inclusion contradiction, novel number, forbidden, elephant.

Write precision, recall, n and run_id into the thresholds.yaml calibration fields (calibrated: true only when the code clears the bar). Codes below the bar stay warn/REPORT. NAME_NOT_IN_SOURCE and DAY_PLACE_MISMATCH stay REPORT (S248 name TNR 0.50).
Settle on the decision page: the background-about-places scope, whether the brief counts as source, and whether reflective sentences count as voice or as additions. These define the Q-promise labels.
phases.proof:
FREE (panel labels, no ledger spend).
- Per-code precision table with Wilson-95 bounds.
- Panel repeatability >= 0.7 agreement on L2; otherwise the rubric is fixed before any promotion.

phases.phase: P2 - Switch the decisions onto the contract (code-only control plane)
steps: Replace validate scoring and should_retry with contract_check plus the class router. REGENERATE gets 1 redraft (2 drafts total) with feedback built by code. Exhausted drafts go to N9. quality_score becomes a report column.
Turn on the N1 source_gate. SOURCE_HOLD is enforced for DAY_COUNT_VS_DURATION once its precision is >= 0.90 on >= 15 fires.
Flip N9 to enforce for the codes that passed P1. _is_publishable reads only N9.verdict.
Take s1_judge off the live A1 path, in judge and in revalidate. Delete the s1_brand_audit LLM fallback. Start the Writing Lab sampled pinned judge.

Type the review queue: reason codes from N9, an owner and an age alert. Approve re-runs N9 server side and needs a reason-coded override for enforced codes. HOLD_POLICY is approved as 'policy_keep', exempt from human_edit_gate. Edit and promote go through N9. Remove the blanket truth stamp and record reviewer-marked sentence labels. The elephant detector covers all fields and matches 'elephant ride/riding'.
Retire build_graph_from_generated for A1. Delete s1_source_facts and the itinerary nudge, with their taxonomy rows.
phases.proof:
FREE + SMALL PAID.
- Free: replay over the stored v2 pages and L2 shows enforced-gate precision >= 0.90 on the flipped pages, 0 PUBLISH pages carrying an enforced code, and the elephant deadlock test passing.
- Paid: 3 tours (sub-day, meal-coded multi-day, elephant) on the exact served route of the next wave, about $0.25, through the gateway with stage adhoc_<issue>. Pass: day count exact 3/3, 0 enforced codes at PUBLISH, served route = pinned, 0 s1_judge live calls.

phases.phase: P3 - Code-owned slots and local, source-aware repair
steps: Change writer rule 7 to 'do not write a fact line'. The N4 assemble step appends source_fact_lines verbatim and relabels Optional from FS.optional. The rest of W is unchanged (not W' prose-only).
Make the meta propose -> fit -> template path. Remove _rerepair_meta x3 (flag_fix_node.py:238, 262-277).

Replace flag_fix (A1 only) with local_fix: deterministic edits first, then grounding.repair() on enforced-flagged sentences with the FS unit quotes, then a code delete only for deterministic findings. Run repair_contract after every edit, then re-run the detectors that fired.

Extend grounding: GROUNDED_FIELDS gains name, trip_type, seo_title and seo_meta, and the unit source becomes the FS slice. Move the Jev meal/clock claims from brand_audit into grounding units. Remove Jev waivers of deterministic number findings. Add Q-promise (a1_promise_unsupported) in shadow.
phases.proof:
FREE: repair replay over every stored meal, Optional or meta-flagged v2 page. Pass: 0 days_kept breaches, 0 new names or numbers, ITINERARY_MEAL_TIME_INVENTED on fact lines = 0.

CENTS (< $2): Jev on the changed and new-field units of 50 stored pages plus about 600 L2 sentences. Read UNSUPPORTED precision and Q-promise precision/kappa. The new fields stay REPORT unless precision >= 0.85.

SMALL PAID (cap $8): 3 tours, then 25 held-out golden + 25 stratified tours (Japan, Rajasthan, source contradictions, Optional-heavy). Current graph vs the new graph on the same pinned route and effort. Blind 2-pass panel at $0, with pre-registered criteria (see targets).

phases.phase: P4 - Change control (regression net made mandatory)
steps: The CI replay check becomes required on PRs touching POL, detectors, prompt rendering, s1_writer_v2.py, taxonomy.yaml or route/effort/param migrations. It posts a per-code fire diff and blocks on unexplained new enforced fires on frozen pages.
Add a CI check that an LLM-change PR (writer, verifier, repair prompt or model) carries an eval_run_id.

The writing-memory release fingerprint (releases.py:446-481) gains route_version, effort, provider order and the Jev version. Activating an A1 house_rules or repair_hint release needs a replay pass, and also the 3-tour paid trial when it changes the writer prompt.
Freeze runtime route and admin edits during waves, or put them through the same replay.
phases.proof: FREE: a seeded-regression PR fails CI and its revert passes. Two seeds are used: widen the meta band in POL, and re-enable the LLM fact line. An audit of the last 20 LLM-change PRs shows that each carries an eval_run_id.

phases.phase: P5 - Lineage containment (A3 from the FactSheet)
steps: A3 atom candidates come from FS entries, each with a source quote. The LLM only labels and normalises. A code check verifies the quote is a substring of raw_tours. a3_atom_in_text reads the FS and stays warn.
The T2 grounding baseline becomes the FS, with Master as the style reference only.
After A1 is stable, T2 adopts contract_check, local_fix and N9 in the shared plan.
phases.proof: FREE: atom-diff replay on the stored tours reports the share of atoms with an FS id and a quote. SMALL PAID: 3 tours, about $0.05, then the wave ladder (3 -> <=50 per aa-wave-rerun) with the route pinned and a wave report giving cost per stage.

targets: Exit integrity: 100% of paths to publish or END go through final_contract (topology test). Approves and promotes that bypass it: 0.

Gate honesty: every enforced code has precision >= 0.90 and a Wilson-95 lower bound >= 0.75 on >= 15 adjudicated fires, recorded in thresholds.yaml as calibrated:true with a run_id. Everything else is warn/REPORT.
Contract cleanliness: 0 enforced-class codes on any PUBLISH page in replay and in the paid trials.

Fidelity non-inferiority (P3 Tier 2): the blind panel's serious-error rate per checkable claim is no worse than the v2 baseline of 0.0015 per sentence. The bootstrap 95% upper bound of the difference must be <= +0.003 per claim. Day loss 0/50.
Meal/time: ITINERARY_MEAL_TIME_INVENTED on code-written fact lines = 0. Invented meal or clock times in prose are caught by the prose check with measured precision >= 0.90.
Repair safety: 0 surviving repair_contract breaches (days_kept, no_new_specifics). Whole-field LLM rewrites on A1: 0.
Meta: 100% of published metas inside the single POL band (template fallback). Meta LLM calls <= 2 per tour.
Policy: 0 band or word-list literals outside writing_policy.yaml (lint).
Bounded loops: at most 2 writer drafts, 1 meta retry, 1 sentence-repair round. Gateway requests at most about 12 per tour in the worst case (about 28 today).
Review queue: the review rate excluding HOLD_POLICY is no higher than the current graph. 100% of held tours carry a typed reason code. No item older than 7 days without an owner alert.
Routing transparency: 0 silent writer or verifier fallbacks. A served model different from the pinned one gives DEGRADED, and it is recorded on 100% of drafts and verdicts.
Cost: $/tour <= $0.065 (today about $0.075). s1_judge live calls = 0. Writing Lab sampled judge about $0.15/week. Proof spend: P0-P2 $0 plus about $0.25, P3 under $2 for Jev plus at most $8 paid.
Change control: 100% of PRs on the gated paths carry a replay result. 100% of LLM-change PRs carry an eval_run_id. 0 A1 writing-memory releases activated without replay.
Calibration hygiene: 0 blanket truth stamps written. Reviewer-marked sentence labels grow L2, and gate precision is re-read monthly.
Lineage (P5): 100% of A3 atoms carry an FS entry id and a quote that is a substring of raw_tours.
grafts: From FACTS-FIRST: a source_gate (N1) before any paid call. DAY_COUNT_VS_DURATION and verify_pointers become a source-side SOURCE_HOLD, independent of day_parse. This breaks the common-mode day failure (Japan 12->4) at $0 writer spend.
From FACTS-FIRST: meta propose -> code fit -> code template(FS) fallback, so the meta can never stall a tour or invent a promise.

From FACTS-FIRST: a code-delete fallback for a sentence that still fails after one repair, but only for DETERMINISTIC findings (novel number, meal/clock in prose, forbidden), never on a Jev-only verdict, and only when the field keeps at least one sentence.
From FACTS-FIRST: cap drafts at 2. REGENERATE is narrow once the day plan is code-fixed and source faults are held at N1.
From FACTS-FIRST: N9 refuses a page whose FS hash differs from the live source. This extends the existing live-source check.
From EVAL-FIRST: close the doors first. final_contract is wired to every exit in REPORT mode before any behaviour change.
From EVAL-FIRST: a v2 labelled set (L2, 40-60 tours, sentence-level, 2-pass panel). It is required because golden 1.1.0 is mostly pre-v2 failing pages and cannot measure v2 precision.
From EVAL-FIRST: a single promotion bar for every code (precision >= 0.90, Wilson-95 lower >= 0.75, >= 15 fires), written into thresholds.yaml.

From EVAL-FIRST: remove Jev waivers of deterministic number findings (S246: about 50% of waivers wrong). Split out Q-promise (a1_promise_unsupported) in shadow. Pin the Jev version in the verifier identity.
From EVAL-FIRST: a served model different from the pinned one gives DEGRADED. Record the served model, connection and effort on every verdict. Add explicit stage_model_params.
From EVAL-FIRST: CI requires an eval_run_id on LLM-change PRs, and runtime route or memory-release edits are frozen during waves or put through the replay.
From EVAL-FIRST and FACTS-FIRST: A3 atoms from the FS, with a code-enforced quote-substring check against raw_tours. The T2 grounding baseline becomes the FS.

EVAL-FIRST (taxonomy + measured detectors + L2 labelled v2 set + recorded replies first; one calibrated verifier; 11 phases)

props.quality_mechanism:
Reliability comes from moving every pass/fail decision onto something measurable and identical across the run, replay and the admin view.
(1) One source bundle (raw facts + master base text) is read by the writer, the verifier, the repair step, Jev and the judge. Nothing is checked against a different source than the one written from, and S1 errors are surfaced as inherited_master instead of being fought in T2.
(2) One pure code verifier, t2_checks.run, decides status. It is deterministic, costs $0 and is versioned, and its precision/recall is measured on the replay corpus and the s1_step01 fixture method (Wilson bounds). Its severities come from the registry, so a policy change is one edit.
(3) Deterministic constraints (forbidden words, meta/title length, meal lines, em-dash, day structure) are enforced by code in finalize before verify. The LLM is never asked to count or to self-police them.
(4) Repairs are local spans with the source in the prompt, and repair_contract runs afterwards. A repair cannot reintroduce a fixed defect or drop a day, because the contract reverts it and verify runs again.
(5) Bounded loops: 2 repair passes, rewrite only on hard structure, and a hard budget of 3 writes / $0.25 per version that includes job retry. The stop is a code condition, never judge variance.
(6) Voice quality is a separate, source-aware, pinned, family-guarded judge that only chooses between candidates and is report-only until kappa >= 0.6 on t2@2. A noisy judge therefore can no longer choose between drafts on fidelity, or trigger spend.
(7) Every exit passes the same finalize -> verify contract, elephant tours are held by policy, and the tenant always receives the text.
(8) Each version stores a replay record, and any prompt/model/effort/route change must show a $0 replay with no new hard flips plus a cents rejudge before merge. Regressions therefore cannot return unnoticed.

Phase 0 ($0, read-only): pull aggregates for tenant_tour_versions status x qa_status x qa_repair_count x judge model, plus review_queue T2 rows by reason, as the baseline.
Phase 1 ($0): add services/quality/t2_checks.py (a composition of existing functions), the Q0 cases and the replay corpus job. Run the verifier in shadow in the current graph and T3, writing to generation_meta. No behaviour change.
Phase 2 ($0, code-only, no prompt change): extend _PT_SQL and build the support bundle (passed to T3 and the admin edit first); add the finalize node; route the hitl exit through finalize/verify; move the em-dash fix ahead of verify; drop the master-score fallback; persist the verifier vector and the replay record; add the elephant policy_hold and the budget governor; remove the nudge, the Jev tie-break, the production median-of-3, the revalidate judge call and the T3 full-graph rounds (replaced by one local repair). Prove it with scripted-LLM graph tests and a replay with no new hard flips.
Phase 3 (prompt changes, gated by Tier 2): the v2-parity T2 writer prompt with real inclusions; the local repair prompt with the support bundle; 16000 under token_budget; effort set by the A/B. Use the 3-then-20 run, and record the eval run id in the route/param migration.
Phase 4 (judge): the T2 judge v2 voice rubric, pinning, the family guard and nova-lite off the route; refresh the t2@2 golden set; kappa run. Status has come from the verifier since Phase 2; the judge only enters select_best tie-ordering once calibrated.
Phase 5 (change control): one T2 profile row replaces the env flags; manifest fix, prompt sha tests and the migration lint. Writing memory t2_block is unfrozen only when a T2 R2 is measurable.
Shared parts go to the joint plan, built once for blog, tour and T2: the gateway judge identity/fallback mark, the policy registry, the replay runner, the label set and the token-budget table.
Cost per version after the change: typical ~$0.08 (1 Sonnet 5.5 write ~$0.072 at high, less if medium wins; 0-2 Haiku span repairs ~$0.002; 1 judge ~$0.002; Jev under $0.001). Hard ceiling $0.25 per version, including job retry.
props.cost_per_item: Typical ~$0.08 per tenant version (1 t2_generate Sonnet 5.5 high ~$0.072, 0-2 local repairs at Haiku 5.5 ~$0.001 each, 1 pinned judge call ~$0.002, Jev shadow under $0.001). Hard cap $0.25 and 3 writer calls per version, including job retry. Old worst case was ~96 requests / 9 high-effort writes, ~$0.70+ and x2 on retry (I). Validation before rollout: Tier 0 $0, Tier 1 under $0.10 per rejudge, Tier 2 3+20 tours ~$2-4.
risks: Raw vs master divergence: where S1 put a claim in master that raw lacks, the verifier flags inherited_master findings that T2 cannot fix. Mitigation: union support plus the inherited_master tag (report only, sent to the A1 backlog); measure the share in the Phase 1 shadow run before it can affect status.

s1_checks was tuned on S1 pages against raw sources. On tenant text, NAME_NOT_IN_SOURCE and the lexicon may fire on brand names, tenant signature phrases or localised wording (EN-GB). Mitigation: a brand-vocabulary allowlist, plus a per-class precision floor (>= 0.8 lower bound) before a class can gate status; below the floor the class is report-only.

Removing voice-driven retries and the 'different details' reward may make tenant texts closer to master and to each other, which weakens differentiation. Mitigation: report cross-tenant/master similarity (existing Cohere embed) and voice score in the A/B; add a voice-only local repair only if the calibrated judge shows a gap.

Calibrating the judge needs human labels (>= 12 t2@2 pairs, >= 3 per label). Without them the voice judge stays report-only indefinitely. That is acceptable for fidelity, but there will be no measured brand-voice signal until the labels exist.

The v2 writer was designed for neutral A1 pages. Adding a tenant voice layer is a new prompt that must keep the brand-differentiation block (s1_writer_v2_live.py:10-11 risk T8). It is unproven until the 3-then-20 run.

Jev a1_claim_supported stays shadow on T2, so some true-negative grounding hits that it used to clear will now count as fidelity findings, and needs_review may rise until its T2 precision is measured.

The budget governor across job retries needs a counter stored on the version row. A crash between the call and the counter write could undercount by one call. This is acceptable, but it should be noted in the job's idempotency notes.

The elephant lock on ride spans depends on the detector finding the spans. A paraphrased ride sentence in master that the regex misses could still be repaired. Mitigation: a corpus test on the 892 Master pages, with the full source scanned and not only highlights.

Splitting into build_t2_graph() means A1 fixes no longer reach T2 automatically. That is intended, but shared nodes (finalize, verify, local_repair) must live in services/quality or acp_shared so both graphs import one copy.

props.angle: FACTS-FIRST: T2 is rebuilt around one code-built source bundle. Its core is a fact sheet built from the RAW supplier row with the existing S1 v2 builder, not from the Master prose, plus a claim contract. The writer, the repair step and the verifier all read that same bundle. Code composes the constrained fields (meal and overnight lines, day skeleton, inclusions, SEO length fit, dashes, forbidden words). The LLM writes only the narrative slots. One verifier checks claim by claim, and repairs are local and contract-checked. Status comes from the verifier's findings, not from a judge score. The judge is a pinned, report-only voice score from a different model family. Today T2 runs as is_tenant_rewrite branches inside the A1 LangGraph. It becomes its own small linear workflow under a per-version budget. props.quality_mechanism:
What guarantees what:
(1) Constrained facts are correct by construction. Code composes day count, day headings, Overnight/Meals lines, inclusion/exclusion lists, slug, SEO length, dashes and forbidden words from F_raw/policy. Every step's contract asserts the composed slots byte-equal, and finalize runs last. A meal, time or day-count error therefore cannot come from an LLM, and it cannot be lost during repair.
(2) Every checker reads one source. The writer, V, repair, judge and the admin edit check all take the same SourceBundle (bundle_hash on the version), so 'supported' means the same thing everywhere. Master drift is pre-flagged, so T2 cannot launder S1 inventions.
(3) Deterministic claim classes are gated by code with known recall and precision: numbers, names, day places, inclusion contradictions, day structure, meta, truncation, service-level words and meal/clock outside the slots. Recall comes from seeded mutation, precision from labelled clean sentences. A detector blocks only when its measured precision is at or above the bar; otherwise it warns. The registry flag records which.
(4) The paraphrased-promise class (activities, views, times, services) is the only residual LLM judgement. It is a claim verifier from a different family, reads the fact sheet and works per sentence. It is warn-only until precision is measured on T2 labels, and the writer prompt plus the fact-sheet-first layout are the primary defence.
(5) Repairs cannot regress. They are span-local, the source entries are in the prompt, and the repair contract (no new names/numbers absent from the bundle, no cut sentences, slots unchanged) runs, then finalize, then the full V re-run. The best-draft key is monotone on blocking findings, so a saved draft never has more blocking findings than an earlier one.
(6) There is one exit. Every path ends finalize -> V -> status -> save, so no door skips the checks (today's hitl exit and post-check em-dash edit disappear).
(7) Judge noise drives neither spend nor status. The voice judge is one pinned, family-guarded, source-aware call, report-only until kappa >= 0.6 on t2@2. Retries trigger only on deterministic findings that local repair could not fix, under VersionBudget.
(8) Change control. Prompt, policy, model, effort, route and writing-memory changes alter the fingerprint (full prompt hash, policy version, route id). CI runs the free replay of V on a frozen T2 corpus, and any LLM-side change needs the cents rejudge on t2@2 before it ships.
(9) The tenant still always receives the text. Policy holds (elephant) and needs_review stay admin-side labels plus review_queue rows with owner and reason codes.
props.cost_per_item:
Ledger baseline (VERIFIED, tour_stats.raw, 30 days): sonnet-5-5 t2_generate $2.15/30 calls, about $0.072 per write. sonnet-4-6 $10.78/238 calls, about $0.045. Haiku flag_fix about $0.002. t2_judge on gpt-5.6-luna about $0.0018 per call. Jev about $0.00005.

Target typical (INFERRED):
- 1 Sonnet write at about $0.07-0.09 (the 16000 ceiling is headroom, not spend; output is similar to today plus 3 meta candidates)
- 0-1 Haiku span repair, about $0.002
- a few residual-promise verifier calls on flagged sentences only, about $0.001-0.003
- 1 judge call, about $0.002
- Total about $0.08-0.10 per version, against about $0.072-0.15 today (1-2 writes plus 2.7 judge calls per draft plus the revalidate judge).

Target worst case under VersionBudget: 2 Sonnet writes + 3 Haiku repairs + verifier + 1 judge, about $0.18-0.22, hard cap $0.25 including job retry. Today's worst case is 9 Sonnet high-effort writes (x2 on job retry), about $0.65-1.30, plus about 96 requests.

Proof cost:
- Tier 0: $0
- Tier 1 cents rejudge: under $0.50 total
- Tier 2 paid A/B: 3-tour trial (about $0.30), then 20 tours x 2 arms (about $4), cap $5.
risks: Raw-vs-Master divergence. S1 legitimately rephrased and condensed the raw text, and the A2 review may have hand-edited the Master. A raw fact sheet may then flag Master-derived sentences as unsupported. Mitigation: master_drift pre-pass, human-edited fields as provenance=human source, and a measured drift rate on all ~892 Masters before the flip (Tier 0).

Lexical claim extraction misses paraphrased promises ('watch the sun rise over the bay'). Until the LLM claim verifier has measured precision it is warn-only, so the promise class still rests on prompt plus fact-sheet layout for a while. This must be said plainly in the Writing Lab, not reported as 'verified'.

Thin raw sources plus strict facts-first may give flat, generic copy, and tenants want brand voice. Mitigation: the background-about-named-places allowance from the policy registry, the voice judge (report), and blind pairwise preference on 10 tours in the A/B.

Composed slots may expose supplier errors (wrong meal codes in raw) verbatim. That is the correct source-of-truth behaviour, but it surfaces raw data quality, so a raw-fact conflict list (F_raw.conflicts) should go into review_queue.
Moving status off the judge changes the ai_generated vs needs_review mix in admin views. Early counts are not comparable with history, so before/after must be labelled by fingerprint.

Repair model pinning: haiku-5-5 is refused on acc3 and is served by haiku-4-5 or a different vendor. The contract protects facts, but repair quality per model must be read on the replay record. The verifier and judge family guard can leave no allowed judge reachable, which yields a null score (acceptable because the judge is report-only).
Labelling load: the golden t2@2 set and ~150 labelled sentences need agent-panel labelling plus tech-lead approval. Without them every LLM gate stays warn-only (safe but slower to tighten).
Writing-memory releases and tenant-authored rules still enter the prompt. If they are not fingerprinted and eval-gated, they bypass change control, as the blog audit also found.
Big-bang risk of rewriting T2 into its own module. Mitigation: build behind T2_PIPELINE=v2, run V in shadow on v1 outputs first, keep v1 for one release for rollback.
Elephant detector false positives or negatives on unusual wording. The registry holds the wording, and the seeded test includes both policy phrasings.
props.test_plan:
Tier 0, free, deterministic, runs in CI and on the Dev corpus with no LLM:
(a) Unit and property tests: verify_pointers(F_raw, raw) == [] on every raw row with a Master; finalize idempotent (finalize(finalize(x)) == x); slot byte-equality holds through repair_spans on synthetic LLM replies; day_body length mismatch gives a hard finding; the elephant detector fires on both 'elephant ride' and 'elephant riding' and in any field.
(b) master_drift census: run s1_checks.run_checks(raw, master) over all Masters and report the drift rate per code. Pass: rate known and reviewed; if > 15% of tours have blocking drift, tune the provenance rules before the writer work.
(c) Free replay of V on all stored tenant_tour_versions plus their raw rows (the saved texts and the existing T3 outcomes): findings distribution per code against today's T3 verdicts. It must surface the known families: meal/time, inclusion 'None' cases and the elephant tours.
(d) Seeded mutation suite: about 50 clean T2/Master texts x 8 injected classes (invented meal, excluded item claimed included, extra day, novel number, novel place name, clock time, 'luxury' service claim, elephant ride removed). Pass: recall >= 0.95 on number/day/inclusion/meal/slot classes, >= 0.8 on names and service words; false findings <= 5% of sentences on the unmutated texts.
(e) Repair replay: feed recorded and synthetic bad repair outputs (forbidden word written back, day dropped, number added) through enforce_spans plus V. Pass: 100% reverted.
This replay re-runs code on stored texts. It does not re-read stored verdicts, which avoids the 'false green' of replaying saved F9 verdicts.

Tier 1, cents, pinned rejudge:
(f) Label about 150 T2 sentences (agent panel, tech lead approves) as supported / background-OK / unsupported-promise. Measure the LLM claim verifier and the Jev a1_claim_supported precision and recall on T2 pairs (about $0.10-0.20). Blocking requires precision >= 0.85; otherwise warn-only.
(g) Build t2@2 golden (>= 12 pairs, >= 3 pass, >= 3 fail) and run the voice judge 3x pinned (about $0.05). Kappa >= 0.6 is needed before the judge may affect status, and the run-to-run spread must be recorded.

Tier 2, small paid, after Tier 0/1 pass:
3-tour trial (stop on any contract revert that loses a slot, any max_tokens, or any fallback across families), then 20 tours (mix of countries, at least 2 elephant/kept-set tours, at least 3 thin-source tours). Arms: v2 at effort medium vs v2 at effort high. Control: v1 is the stored v1 versions of the same tours re-scored by V, for $0 extra. Cap $5.
Pass criteria:
- blocking V findings per tour on v2 at most 25% of the v1 control
- 0 meal/clock/day-count findings (by construction)
- 0 slot-equality breaks
- p95 output < 70% of the ceiling and 0 empty cuts
- mean writer calls <= 1.3 per version
- cost per version <= $0.12
- the elephant tours labelled policy_hold
- voice: blind pairwise preference on 10 tours (agent panel, tech lead approves) not worse than v1; the voice judge score is reported only

The effort arm is chosen by findings and cost, not by judge score.
props.migration_path:
Step 0 (shared with the blog/S1 plan, done once): the policy registry plus lint, the gateway same-model retry on empty or max_tokens replies, the replay-record schema, and the T2 prompt-manifest fix.
Step 1: SourceBundle. Extend _PT_SQL with the raw inclusions, exclusions, price_raw and agency fields; build F_raw, master_drift, F_tenant, F_brand and the policy_mode detector. Not used by the writer yet; logged on new versions. Run the Tier 0 (b) census.
Step 2: Single verifier V in shadow. Run it after the current v1 T2 path on every new version and over the stored corpus (Tier 0 c-e). Nothing gates yet. Label sentences and build t2@2 (Tier 1).
Step 3: Low-risk changes inside v1 that need no writer change:
- status from V blocking findings
- drop the master quality_score fallback
- remove the Jev tie-break, the near-band repeat, the second judge in revalidate, and the nudge
- add the elephant policy_hold branch and VersionBudget
- persist the judge identity and full prompt hash
Step 4: The t2_v2 module behind T2_PIPELINE=v2: compose_slots, the T2 v2 writer (reusing render_fact_sheet, token_budget at 16000), finalize, the repair_spans generalisation of the T3 sentence repair, one exit and the replay record. Delete nothing yet.
Step 5: Tier 2 paid A/B (3, then 20 tours, cap $5) with v2 against stored v1. On pass, flip T2_PIPELINE=v2 as default (Dev has no real tenants, so no grace window).
Step 6: One release later, delete the is_tenant_rewrite branches in graph.py, prompts v1 T2, flag_fix on T2, revise_block, the T3 full-graph round and the related env flags (T2_JUDGE_*, T2_BEST_DRAFT, T2_TARGETED_REPAIR, T3_BACKGROUND_FACTS move into the registry). Promote verifier codes and the voice judge to blocking one by one, as each reaches its measured precision or kappa bar, each through the Tier 1 rejudge.

props.angle: EVAL-FIRST. Write the quality contract first, then build the graph to fit it. The contract has four parts: (1) the existing taxonomy (services/quality/taxonomy.yaml, qtax-v1, 17 classes with severities); (2) a span-labelled T2 corpus (t2@2) on Dev; (3) a calibration block per detector that records precision, recall and n (thresholds.yaml already has the shape `calibration: {run_id, precision, recall, n, calibrated}` and leaves it null today, VERIFIED); (4) replay records that store the raw replies. A node is allowed to gate, repair or set status only when its calibration block holds measured numbers that clear the bar. Every other node is report-only. As a result the T2 graph gets smaller. It keeps 1 writer call, 1 deterministic verifier, 1 shadow LLM fidelity verifier on the same source bundle, local span repairs triggered only by enforce-mode detectors, and 1 report-only voice scorer. It drops the source-blind brand judge as a gate, plus the nudge, the Jev tie-break, median-of-3, the judge call inside revalidate, the T3 full-graph round and the hitl bypass exit. The status the tenant never sees comes from measured detectors, not from judge noise. The tenant still always receives the text.

     Gateway: empty reply or max_tokens -> retry the SAME model once with a raised budget; a family fallback only through degrade_mode=queue_retry, never silently.

     scope.persona_promise lexicon, other.lexicon, other.length_shape (meta band), brand_claims, safety.tenant_isolation.
     Each detector has mode enforce|warn|shadow from taxonomy.yaml + calibration block. Output = finding vector [{code, class, severity, mode, field, span}].

 N7 Select (code): candidates = {initial, after each repair/rewrite}; key = (enforce_hard==0, enforce_count, warn_count, shadow_count); voice score is NOT in the key until calibrated.

props.quality_mechanism:
The guarantees fall into four groups.

(1) Fidelity is guaranteed by construction, not by persuasion. The writer, the deterministic verifier, the LLM verifier and the repair all read one SourceBundle with a code-built fact sheet (raw ∪ master), keyed by bundle_sha. No checker can disagree about what the source says, and inclusions can no longer appear as 'None'.

(2) Code owns every deterministic constraint, and the final contract always runs. Finalize runs once before every verify. Verify runs on every candidate. Every exit (normal, repaired, scoped rewrite, policy hold) goes through N4 and N9, so no door bypasses the checks: the hitl END is gone and the em-dash fix runs before the check.

(3) Only measured gates act. A detector can trigger a repair or set needs_review only when its taxonomy calibration block shows precision >= 0.90 on >= 15 labelled positives in t2@2, and CI lint refuses 'enforce' otherwise. Unmeasured detectors are warn or shadow and only report. Repairs therefore fire in proportion to proven defects, and false positives cannot drive rewrite loops. Recall per class is published, so coverage gaps are visible, not hidden.

(4) Judges are pinned, family-guarded at call time, given the same bundle, and stored with model, connection and raw reply. The holistic voice score cannot gate, select or trigger writes until kappa >= 0.6 on >= 12 t2@2 pairs. Repairs are local and contract-checked (days_kept, no_new_specifics, locked_spans_kept, gates_kept), and best-candidate selection uses deterministic cleanliness first, so a repair cannot make the saved text worse on any enforced class.

Loops are bounded twice: per node (2 repair rounds, 1 scoped rewrite) and per version (VersionBudget across graph, T3 and job retry). The stop rule is deterministic: stop when no enforce finding remains or the budget is spent.

Regressions are caught before tenants see them. Q0 pins each family red-on-base. R0 replays the stored raw replies through the current code on every deploy and diffs the finding vectors, and a flip turns verify red. R1 re-measures any verifier or voice change. R2 is required for any writer, prompt, model, effort or writing-memory change. Migration and PATCH route changes need an eval_run_id.
props.test_plan:
Stage A, free ($0, local and CI):
- A1. Q0 T2 cases (about 20, with negative twins) are red on base and green on the new N3/N4. The lint has 0 errors, with the T2 parity warnings for enforced classes turned into errors.
- A2. Offline calibration of the deterministic detectors. Run N3/N4 on the 40 t2@2 outputs (the stored generated_content of existing T2 versions; no writer call). Compute precision and recall per class against the span labels and fill the calibration blocks. Pass: every detector set to enforce has precision >= 0.90 with n_pos >= 15 (else it stays warn), and tenant_isolation, day_structure and truncated have recall >= 0.9 on their positives.
- A3. Graph-shape tests with a recorded gateway cassette. Every exit path reaches N9. VersionBudget stops at 2 writes and $0.30, including a simulated job retry. An empty reply retries the same model. The elephant fixture produces verbatim master text, policy_hold and a review_queue row with 0 LLM calls.
- A4. R0 replay job on the 40 stored versions plus the 30 sonnet-5-5 T2 versions. Run it twice, with zero diff between runs (deterministic). The rendered-prompt sha test is pinned.

Stage B, cents (≤ $0.60 total, pinned models, ledger stage adhoc_t2v2 with role judge, validate or writer):
- B1. R1 rejudge. Run t2_verify and t2_voice on t2@2 with 2 repeats each. Pass for any verifier class to be enforced: precision >= 0.90, recall reported, self-agreement >= 0.8. Pass for the voice score to enter selection: kappa >= 0.6 on >= 12 holistic pairs with >= 4 pass and >= 4 fail. Failing either keeps that part shadow or report-only, which does not block shipping.
- B2. Repair replay. Run N5 on the enforce findings of the t2@2 outputs. Pass: 0 contract violations kept, >= 80% of findings cleared, 0 new enforce findings, 0 days lost.

Stage C, paid small subset (cap $5, pinned writer route on anthropic-direct, synthetic audit tenants only, no elephant tours):
- C1. 3 tours, one per tenant. Check the flow end to end, the replay record is complete, cost per version is ≤ $0.15, and there are 0 cuts.
- C2. 20 tours as R2 against control. The control is the current pipeline's stored output for the SAME golden items and the same golden-set version, so all pairs match (this fixes AA-900 RC3). Pass:
  - enforce-hard findings per version ≤ control (non-inferior), with fact.inclusion plus fact.number strictly lower;
  - 0 struct.truncated and 0 day loss;
  - median writer calls 1, max 2;
  - median cost ≤ $0.10, max ≤ $0.30;
  - holistic labels by the agent panel on the 20 pairs show no more heavy grades than control.
A failure on any line keeps v1 live and records the run as evidence.
risks: Label cost and quality: 40 span-labelled versions by an agent panel can still carry the inconsistencies AA-900 found in T9 labels (the same claim type labelled pass in one item and fail in another). Mitigate with written class definitions from the registry, 3 labellers plus an adjudicator, inter-labeller agreement recorded per class, and no detector enforced on a class whose labeller agreement is below 0.7.

Few positives: some hard classes (tenant_isolation, misbinding) may never reach 15 positives on 40 natural versions. These stay warn-only unless synthetic injected-defect items (marked as such) are added, which measure recall, not real-world precision.

Raw ∪ master conflicts: the fact sheet joins two sources, and the master is an S1 output that can carry S1 errors. Conflicts must surface as source.contradiction findings, report-only, not as writer facts. Joining raw_tours into the tenant job widens the T2 data read path, which must stay within tenant RLS and data scope.

The deterministic inclusion and service lexicon may over-flag paraphrases (precision < 0.9) and stay warn-only. In that case, real meal and activity inventions are caught only once N4b calibrates. Until then T2 fidelity on judgement classes is reported, not enforced.

Verifier availability: a pinned non-Anthropic verifier with no fallback means outages produce 'unverified' versions and more needs_review labels. That is acceptable because tenants still receive the text, but the nightly re-verify job must exist.

Elephant default (master verbatim for the whole tour) gives the tenant no brand rewrite on those tours. A locked-span variant (rewrite everything except ride-bearing spans) is possible but needs its own contract invariant and labels. This needs a decision from the tech lead.

The single policy registry forces the pending policy calls (scope of background about named places, whether the tenant brief counts as a source, reflection lines as voice or embellishment) to be decided once. Until they are decided, the related classes cannot be calibrated.

Writing-memory rules and tenant exemplars injected into the system prompt can still change writer behaviour. They are covered only if the release id is in the prompt fingerprint and activation is gated on R2 against t2@2. Today a T2 R2 cannot pass, so a release may already be active by break-glass. Check this before P3.
Moving effort or the ceiling (16000) changes cost and latency. Effort stays pinned at today's 'high' until a 3-then-20 A/B inside Stage C decides it, so no unmeasured change rides along.

pick.winner:
EVOLVE is the backbone, with grafts from FACTS-FIRST and EVAL-FIRST. All three proposals end at almost the same graph: one source bundle, one code verifier, local contract-checked repair, one finalize step, status from the verifier, and a voice judge that only reports. They differ in how they get there. EVOLVE wins on route. It runs everything in shadow first, reuses dormant S1 v2 code, puts no human labels on the critical path for the structural fixes, and ships value in the first phase. It is weaker in three places, and the grafts fix those:
- It decides with a fuzzy 'union support' and has no rule for when a detector may enforce. EVAL-FIRST supplies the calibration rule and the lint.
- It leaves meal lines and day structure to the LLM plus a repair. FACTS-FIRST's compose_slots makes those classes correct by construction.
- It keeps T2 as a LangGraph variant. A plain linear orchestrator (FACTS-FIRST) is simpler to test and replay.
FACTS-FIRST has the best quality ceiling, but it is big-bang (two L items) and gates a full module rewrite before any measurement. EVAL-FIRST has the best governance, but it puts 40 span-labelled versions in front of most of the value and defaults elephant tours to master verbatim without asking.

scores.angle: EVOLVE (rewire T2 into one small graph reusing S1 v2 assets; shadow-first)
FACTS-FIRST (raw fact sheet + code-composed slots; LLM writes narrative slots only; linear orchestrator behind T2_PIPELINE=v2)
EVAL-FIRST (quality contract + calibration blocks first; only measured gates act; graph sized to the contract)

grafts: FACTS-FIRST -> compose_slots: code writes the day skeleton ('Day N' headings, day count), the verbatim Overnight/Meals lines (source_fact_lines, s1_writer_v2.py:345) and the inclusion/exclusion lists. The contract asserts these slots byte-equal after every step. The meal/time family (82% of brand-audit codes) is removed by construction, not by repair.

FACTS-FIRST -> facts come from the RAW row (build_fact_table + verify_pointers == []). The master is the voice/structure base only. A master_drift pre-pass (run_checks(raw, master)) marks master sentences that raw does not support as 'do not carry'; human-edited master fields count as source with provenance=human. This replaces EVOLVE's vague 'union support'. The inherited_master tag (EVOLVE) stays as the report code that feeds the A1 backlog.

FACTS-FIRST -> T2 v2 is a plain linear Python orchestrator in its own module, not is_tenant_rewrite branches in graph.py. Shared steps (finalize, verify, local_repair) live in services/quality so A1 can import the same copy later.
FACTS-FIRST -> the writer returns 3 seo_meta/title candidates; code picks the first that passes the registry band, else fit_seo_meta_final. No LLM meta re-repair loop.

FACTS-FIRST -> a seeded mutation suite (~50 clean texts x 8 injected classes) measures detector recall. The replay re-runs current code on stored texts and never re-reads stored verdicts, which avoids the 'false green' found in the blog audit.
FACTS-FIRST -> the A/B control is the stored v1 version of the same tours, re-scored by the new verifier for $0.

EVAL-FIRST -> calibration blocks in taxonomy.yaml per T2 detector (mode enforce|warn|shadow; run_id, precision, recall, n_pos, n_neg). CI lint refuses 'enforce' without measured numbers. Definitional classes (JSON shape, day count vs fact sheet, slot equality, truncation, forbidden words, meta band, tenant isolation) may enforce from day one on Q0 proof; lexical and judgement classes need precision >= 0.90 on n_pos >= 15.

EVAL-FIRST -> P0 quick wins inside v1 before any new graph: same-model retry on an empty/max_tokens reply; nova-lite off the t2_judge route; gpt-6-luna-openai off the t2_generate chain (degrade_mode=queue_retry); family_rule.trace_models bound in the job; manifest fix; full-prompt hash; master-score fallback dropped; hitl bypass closed; T3 full-graph round off.
EVAL-FIRST -> a job retry resumes from the stored best candidate instead of rewriting. VersionBudget is persisted on the version row.

EVAL-FIRST -> an LLM claim verifier for the residual promise class (activity/view/time/service): non-Anthropic, sees the same bundle, closed class list, per-sentence claims with quote spans, built from the AA-900 lessons (explicit background allowance, field names, CUT_MARK). It stays in SHADOW until it is calibrated per class. If unavailable the result is 'unverified', with no fallback rung.
EVAL-FIRST -> nightly ledger watchdog ($0 SQL): cut rate > 2%, answering model differs from the pin, fallback share > 10%, more than one prompt sha or effort per day, versions stuck 'unverified'.

EVAL-FIRST -> a migration lint requires '-- eval: <run_id>' or '-- break-glass: <reason>' on t2_* llm_role_config / llm_stage_params rows. The T2 files go into services/quality/paths.yaml as a required check.
EVAL-FIRST -> per-class labeller agreement is recorded. No class is enforced where agreement is below 0.7.
EVOLVE -> Phase 1 shadow run of the new verifier inside the current pipeline, writing its findings vector into generation_meta, so base and new are compared on the same versions.
EVOLVE -> a scripted fake-LLM graph-shape test proves that every exit passes finalize -> verify -> select -> save and that the writer-call cap holds across a job retry.

pick.verdict_on_current_design:
RESTRUCTURE. Do not polish it, and do not rebuild from zero. The current graph is not sound, for three VERIFIED reasons:
(1) The only score gate is a source-blind, uncalibrated LLM brand judge. In 30 days it was answered by 4 models with 118 refusals, and it rewards 'different details'. It drives retries, the best-draft choice and status, so the number of rounds follows judge variance. Its voice feedback is also merged into the fact-fix revision, which is the T2 form of 'fixes loop forever'.
(2) The writer, T3 and Jev all ground on lossy master prose with 'Inclusions: None'. No fact sheet exists, so the core fidelity classes (promised activities, meals, times, views, services) have no detector.
(3) Two verifier stacks run with different sources and exits. Loops nest to ~96 requests and 9 high-effort writes. One exit (hitl, graph.py:1487-1492) skips the audit, and the em-dash edit runs after the last check. Because the tenant always receives the text, all of that spend only changes an admin label.

The node inventory, though, is largely reusable: the job wrapper, the brand and SEO loaders, the deterministic fits, forbidden handling, the T3 sentence repair, repair_contract, the ledger, best-draft-wins, and the dormant S1 v2 fact table and checks. What must change is the topology and the decision signal. Status, retry and selection move onto a measured deterministic verifier that reads the same bundle as the writer. Repairs become span-local and contract-checked. Every exit passes one finalize -> verify contract. A per-version budget replaces the nested loops. Without the change-control half (calibration modes, replay, migration lint, frozen writing memory) any new graph would drift the same way, so that half is part of the restructure, not optional.

Overall verdict: the release plumbing (evidence checked twice, in the API and the DB, one human click, rollback, post-activation check, ledger-backed caps) is sound and must be kept. The measuring part of the graph (ground truth -> judge -> calibration -> control pairing -> paired criterion) is wrong by design, so R2 cannot produce a valid verdict for any writer: 3 of 3 t9_blog runs were invalid, $5.04 was spent, and no a1 or t2 run exists. 1. The instrument moves. The judge is whichever model on the 4-rung route answers. Its identity is left out of judge_version (eval_judge.py:169-180, VERIFIED). One vote per item, no test-retest check.
2. The instrument answers a different question from the policy. The rubric's rule 2 (eval_judge.py:90-92) has no Part A (background about named places is allowed). Verdict and score are copied straight from the LLM with no code rule (parse_verdict eval_judge.py:303-325).
3. Ground truth is weak. 17 of 18 blog labels are agent_panel labels, and the only human label is a test stub (t9b-002 'ZZ S239 test label'). The calibration set and the gating set are the same 18 items.

   - Release-0 controls come from pre-v2 or older golden versions. The item_id changes with every golden version, so 0 of 15 candidates were paired in both S271 runs (r2.py:310-316, VERIFIED from calib.raw).
   - With paired == 0, criterion_met (eval_checks.py:473-483) can never pass.
5. Spend is not gated by calibration. The writer loop at r2.py:490 starts even when judge_counts is false. tune_decision then returns 'informative' only after the whole tune phase has been paid for.
6. Change control covers only writing-memory Releases:
   - Prompt, route, effort and token changes arrive by migration or env with no eval.
   - current_fingerprint (releases.py:446-462) misses effort, max_tokens, gate code, the t9_repair, t10_* and t9_faq_* routes, and the model that actually answered.
   - reverify_reasons (releases.py:465-476) never emits prompt_version_mismatch, although REVERIFY_REASONS lists it (releases.py:45). Only release0.py:147 sets it by hand (VERIFIED).

That fits a regression probe but not a calibration set, because the judge's base rate is distorted. Keep failure-biased items as a 'hard' stratum. Add a random stratified 'representative' stratum of recent outputs from the CURRENT writer (v2, Sonnet 5.5). Today's a1 controls predate v2 (fixture-1.2.0 version_num 1 x41, created 20/10, VERIFIED via the tour audit).

The labels contradict each other on the same defect type: 004 PASS 'approximated elsewhere' vs 019 FAIL 'replicate elsewhere'; 017 PASS 'millennia' vs 020 FAIL 'barely changed in centuries' (VERIFIED by critic vote 1). The --approved-by stamp is not a human judgement. The item verdict is then derived by code from the claim labels under the single policy file.

The importer is $0, DRY RUN by default and versioned, which is good. The flaw is that each version re-creates items with new item_ids, which breaks control pairing across versions. Key items by a stable sample_id plus content hash. Store fixtures in one private, versioned place (Dev DB, or a private bucket with a manifest hash) and not in a session scratch folder.

The a1 controls are pre-v2 pages labelled heavy, so 'non_inferior' against them is a meaningless bar. Re-freeze: a1@2 from the v2 panel50 pages, t2@2 with at least 12 pairs and at least 3 per label, before any a1/t2 R2.

A $0 counterfactual over stored text, with counts and ids only, tied to rule_sha. Correct for a lexicon rule whose effect is deterministic (a phrase drops to 0 and no new blocking gate fires). Keep it as the evidence for L0.

It passes the stored F9 verdicts through (run_quality_gates f9_results=..., replay.py:16-19 docstring) and skips F10, so it can never detect a change in the F9 judge: false green for judge changes. Gate inputs are rebuilt in a second copy of run_write_background (PieceReplay, plus scripts/aa729/score.t9_gate_replay) with no parity test (VERIFIED, blog audit). Make one input builder shared with production and assert parity. Label the stored-verdict mode 'deterministic-only' in the result so nobody reads it as a judge check.

An active lexicon rule changes the T9 system prompt (the Never use line) and adds a BLOCKING F2_lexicon finding on R0 + one click (l0.py:1-24, D11). There is no R2 and no shadow, and no PR. The design limits are good: it only adds a word, the fact gates outrank it, and rollback is one click. But a new blocking gate with no measured precision on stored texts is a precision-unknown hold source. Make the L0 F2_lexicon finding warn-only/sentence-repair (never a hold), require R0 l0_ok on at least 20 texts, and add the active L0 set's hash to the writer fingerprint and to writer_input stamps (already partly in writer_input.writing_rules).

The drafter is gated in code: clusters are counted at $0, there are support thresholds, lint forbids content additions and PREDICT needs 2 or more held-out edits, auto-mining is off by default, and there is a $1/run and $25/month cap. Its output only reaches writers through a Release, which needs an R2 pass. Not on the critical path today, so leave it.
