node_verdicts.why: The constants are hand-set: t9_blog 0.08 against a real ~$0.16 per item at effort high, and a judge estimate of 0.01 against a real 0.002-0.003 (VERIFIED: calib.raw candidate cost_usd 2.400/15). So the DRY RUN said $2.48 fits a $2.5 cap, and both runs stopped at budget_cap on item 16/23 and came out invalid. Derive the estimate from the ledger (median cost per real_stage x model over the last N calls, x1.3) instead of constants.

It enforces judge family != writer family at both route level and call level, and a same-family verdict becomes an error row. Gap to close when pinning: it checks only the writer's primary family, and a --judge-model pin would bypass the route-based check (critic vote 3, VERIFIED). Extend it to every model the writer route can fall to, plus the pinned judge.

node_verdicts.node: Eval judge prompt + rubric (eval_judge.py:84-99, 141-166; taxonomy.yaml fact.embellish)
node_verdicts.why: Rule 2 says 'fails even when one phrase would fix it'. fact.embellish covers 'any invented description, superlative, rarity or editorial claim'. And 'a fact class applies when the OUTPUT states something the SOURCE does not support' (VERIFIED). Read together, every evaluative phrase becomes a fail: 91% of the 47 claims on PASS items are false positives (judge lens 2). The rubric does not encode Part A of the source-fidelity policy, and it is stricter than T10 F2_superlatives (quality_gates.py:388-391). Two judges from different vendors agreed 17/18 with each other, and both failed all pass labels, so the prompt is the cause, not the model. Replace the holistic verdict with: (1) the LLM extracts claims, each mapped to the policy taxonomy (trip-promise / checkable world claim / background on a named place / voice), with source quotes; (2) a code rule from the single policy file maps claim classes to item verdict and severity. Score is dropped (AUC 0.53 vs labels).

node_verdicts.node: Eval judge input builder (judge_source_text, build_user_prompt, eval_writers.output_text)
node_verdicts.why: Three defects, all VERIFIED: (1) the SEED cap is 16000, below the longest seed of 19420, so 11 false claims come from facts the judge never saw; (2) OUTPUT is sliced at 9000 with no CUT_MARK (eval_judge.py:56, :287), so false struct.truncated claims appear and SEO title, meta and slug go unseen; (3) output fields are flattened with no field names (eval_checks.py:32-47). The panel reads panel_source_text uncut, which is a second builder, so labeller and judge read different evidence by design. Use one builder for writer, labeller and judge: labelled fields, no silent cuts, and refuse to judge when the input exceeds the cap instead of cutting it.

node_verdicts.node: Eval judge model selection (stage writing_memory_eval route, eval_judge.py:339-353)
node_verdicts.why: There is no model of its own: the route has 4 rungs, the acc3 rungs are deferred, so gpt-6-luna-openai answers, and when its replies were cut nova-lite answered instead. Two runs on the same day had different judges under one id, t9_blog:judge-73e641a99aca (VERIFIED). Pin one judge per run (model_key already exists: client.py:1276) and put the model and connection into judge_version and prompt_version. Refuse to start, at $0, when the pinned model is unavailable, instead of falling back. Pick the model by measured per-class recall on R1, not by availability. The S257 evidence: gpt-5.6-luna 0.562, gpt-6-luna 0.054.

Running calibration on every run, with per-label minimums and per-stratum kappa, is good and should be kept. Flaws: one vote per item at temperature 0 on reasoning models, with no test-retest; the calibration items are the same items the rubric is tuned on and the gate is measured on (circular, and critic vote 3 flags a winner's-curse risk); kappa alone hides class recall. Move it out as a separate R1 calibration run with a pinned judge, 3 votes, a split between rubric-dev items and gate items, and a gate on pass-recall AND fail-recall (each >= 0.75) plus kappa. R2 then refers to a calibration run id for the same judge_version+model and does not recompute it.

judge_counts=false does not stop the run: the writer loop pays for probe and the whole tune phase before tune_decision returns 'informative' (eval_checks.py:486-491). 858c8bf6 spent $2.37 on the writer after kappa 0.0 was known (VERIFIED). Make an uncalibrated judge a $0 refusal before any writer call (a hard precondition: a valid R1 calibration id).

control_run = the active release's eval_run_id, which for release 0 is the baseline_import of an OLDER golden version. With item_ids changing per version, control_sources returns {}, and 0/15 candidates were paired in both runs, so criterion_met can never pass (VERIFIED symptom, INFERRED exact cause). The control is also the wrong artefact: a stale repaired final against a fresh first draft. Replace with same-writer, same-path controls: the control arm is generated by the CURRENT production config (A) on the same inputs and through the same path as the candidate (B), written twice (A, A') to measure noise. Fall back to a stored control only when its config fingerprint equals the current one.

node_verdicts.node: Candidate writer path (eval_writers.regenerate; T9 first draft only)
node_verdicts.why: For T9 the candidate is generate.write_content only. T10 gates, t9_repair, the FAQ filter and answer-fit, and the post-gate cut/trim do not run (eval_writers.py:9-13, VERIFIED), yet these are where the holds and fixes happen. The comparison therefore measures neither what ships nor the change under test. Make the full T9 loop runnable in a dry mode that writes no piece row (inject a store), and evaluate the final text plus the hold/approve outcome.

node_verdicts.node: Deterministic checks in R2 (qa_artefacts, isolation_probe, injection_violations)
node_verdicts.why: These are code, cheap, with clear semantics, and they map to hard stops 2 and 3 and to trap defence, which always count. Keep them as is.

It stops the run on ANY new hard fact class against the control, and the judge is told to report classes 'also when pass'. A noisy class therefore ends a paid run with an attachable fail. Replay shows F4 (counting only on a candidate fail) still leaves the first stop unchanged (critic vote 2, VERIFIED). Require a hard-stop-1 class to be confirmed: the claim quote is checked against the source by code (does the quoted phrase exist in the output, and is the cited fact absent from the source) or by a second judge vote, and only claims of the policy class 'trip promise / checkable claim' count.

Binary per-item new_fail/fixed on about 14 tune and 4-6 holdout pairs, with NOISE_K=1 hard-coded 'until a tier has >= 20 items' (config.py:63). One judge flip decides the run. S258 measured panel SD 1.07-1.60 per piece against effects of about 0.15. Replace it with claim-count or severity deltas per item, with A/A' noise bars (±2 SE), and a pre-registered decision (what fail means: revert or not) before the run. Never stopping early on success and the holdout-only-after-tune ordering are right and should be kept.

Ledger-backed caps are right and should be kept. Flaw: after() at r2.py:384-386 marks a run that has finished every item as budget_cap/invalid if the final item overshoots, so a whole paid run is thrown away by $0.01. Check the cap before the last item only, and let a finished run keep its verdict while recording an overspend flag.

Good: output, sha, verdict, codes, up to 8 claims, judge_model, judge_version and cost per row, plus every call in llm_call_log under the eval label. Missing for replay: the exact judge input (it had to be rebuilt in scratch scripts), the raw judge reply (only parsed claims, capped at 8, which creates the 'all claims >= 8' artefact), and writer config (effort, max_tokens, answering model, fallback_used). Store the input hash plus the raw reply as a cassette, so any new verdict rule can be re-scored at $0.
A cheap test of the stop mechanics that never becomes evidence (release_id check, CIS 292 trigger). Keep it. It needs the pairing fix to work (it errors with no control).
It checks the hard stops (QA trace, tenant leak) on real inputs, golden items excluded, caps in place. It does not claim to measure quality, and that is correct. Keep it.

node_verdicts.node: Release evidence gate (releases.evidence_problem + CIS 287 CHECK/trigger + human approve/activate)
node_verdicts.why: The strongest part of the graph: evidence is checked twice (API and DB), a seeded or code-train run can never be evidence, there is one human click, rollback, and a monthly train. Keep it unchanged. It only becomes useful once R2 can actually produce a pass.

current_fingerprint covers only the golden set, the writer route, the writing_memory_eval route and TAXONOMY_VERSION. It misses stage_model_params (effort, max_tokens: migration 381 flagged nothing), the gate/prompt module hashes, the t9_repair, t10_judge, t10_claims, t10_adjudicate, t9_faq_* and t8 routes, and the mode flags. reverify_reasons never computes prompt_version_mismatch, although it is a declared reason (VERIFIED). Widen the fingerprint to the full config that produced an output, and use that same object as R2's run fingerprint and as the stamp on every production write.

node_verdicts.node: Post-activation check + weekly KPI soft stops + disagreement queue
node_verdicts.why: $0, automatic rollback, Wilson bounds, minimum samples. The disagreement queue (R2 control vs label, gates vs labels) is the natural human-label intake. Route it into the claim-level label store proposed above. With no tenants yet, the KPI side has no data (INFERRED), so it is harmless.

node_verdicts.node: Change-eval path for prompt/model/route/effort (eval-runbook.md, adhoc_aa900, route_evidence)
node_verdicts.why: It is manual, runs after deploy, and the runbook is marked UNTESTED (runbook:18-21). route_evidence applies only to the admin PATCH, so migrations 327, 333, 344, 366, 376 and 381 changed writer and judge chains and effort with no eval (VERIFIED, tour audit). Q2 has no tooling. judge_compare refuses the live *-openai judge (judge_compare.py:62-77). Replace with a tiered gate driven by the widened fingerprint: L0 $0 replay in CI for any mapped path; R1 judge-only with a pinned judge for judge or validate-role changes; R2 full-loop paired A/A'/B only for writer prompt/model/effort. The migration lint requires an eval run id or a break-glass reason.

principle_scores.principle: Single source of truth for policy
principle_scores.evidence: Good: labels.RUBRIC is kept equal to eval_judge.LABEL_RUBRIC by a test. Bad: (1) the source-fidelity policy (background about named places allowed) is not in the rubric (eval_judge.py:84-99); (2) the taxonomy.yaml fact.embellish definition is stricter than T10 F2_superlatives (quality_gates.py:388-391, a style issue that never holds); (3) the judge reads the writer's SCOPE text ('must not ... name any place outside these moments') as policy and fails on background places; (4) labels made before the S256 rules were never relabelled. VERIFIED.

principle_scores.principle: Facts / grounding before prose
principle_scores.evidence: The judge rediscovers facts from prose: the FACTS section is empty on 15/18 blog items, place facts sit inside the SEED prose, and the SEED is clipped at 16k (eval_judge.py:63). No structured fact list or claim-to-source mapping exists before judging. Labels are item-level verdicts, not claim-level. VERIFIED.

principle_scores.principle: Generator and verifier separated; verifier sees the same source
principle_scores.evidence: The family rule is enforced at route and call level (r2.py:835-857, _judge_family). But the judge's source is clipped while the writer and panel saw it whole (panel_source_text is uncut; two builders), the output is cut silently at 9000 chars with unlabelled fields (eval_judge.py:56, :287; eval_checks.py:32-47), and labeller and judge read different evidence. VERIFIED.

principle_scores.principle: Deterministic constraints enforced by code, not by asking an LLM
principle_scores.evidence: QA traces, tenant isolation and injection are code (eval_checks.py:86-243), which is good. But field length, slug cut and truncation are left to the LLM judge (struct.truncated in JUDGE_CLASSES), and the whole pass/fail is the LLM's own verdict field with no code rule (parse_verdict eval_judge.py:303-325). The slug cut itself is a code bug the judge then 'finds' (service.py:908). VERIFIED.

principle_scores.principle: Measure what ships: full chain incl. repairs, local source-aware repairs with a contract check
principle_scores.evidence: T9 R2 regenerates the first draft only. T10, t9_repair, the FAQ filter and answer-fit, and cut/trim are not run (eval_writers.py:9-13, r2.py:345 't9_first_draft_only'). The control is a repaired final. The comparison is confounded by design. VERIFIED.

principle_scores.principle: Calibrated, pinned, recorded judges with known error rates
principle_scores.evidence: Calibration runs every run with per-label minimums and strata, and judge_model is stored per row. But it never passed: -0.073, 0.316, 0.137, 0.000 against 0.6. The model is not pinned (4-rung route), and the model is not in judge_version (both S271 runs are judge-73e641a99aca with nova-lite vs gpt-6-luna-openai). There is one vote, no test-retest, and the calibration set equals the gate set and the rubric-tuning set. The production t10_judge also answers on uncalibrated gpt-6-luna-openai. VERIFIED.

principle_scores.principle: Every gate has measured precision/recall or is warn-only
principle_scores.evidence: The kappa gate is measured. Hard stop 1 (any new hard class, eval_checks.py:458-462), NOISE_K=1, the futility rule and the L0 F2_lexicon blocking finding have no measured precision. Hard stop 1 would fire on judge noise (critic vote 2 replay). VERIFIED.

principle_scores.principle: Bounded loops with a clear stop
principle_scores.evidence: Caps come from the ledger, plus probe -> tune -> holdout, futility, never stopping early on success, and an error-share stop: all good. But there is no stop after a failed calibration (r2.py:490), the stale cost estimate guarantees budget_cap, and after() invalidates a finished run on overshoot. VERIFIED.

principle_scores.principle: Replayable and observable (inputs, raw replies, verdicts stored)
principle_scores.evidence: Rows keep output, sha, verdict, codes, claims (8 at most), judge_model and cost, and llm_call_log binding is complete. R0 replay is $0. But the judge input and raw reply are not stored (the S271 analysis had to rebuild them in scratch), the R0 baseline reuses stored F9 verdicts (false green for judge changes), and the active fixture 1.3.0 lives in a gitignored session folder. VERIFIED.

principle_scores.principle: Change control (prompt/model/effort/route changes gated by eval)
principle_scores.evidence: Release activation is enforced twice (API + DB), which is excellent. Everything else bypasses it: route and effort migrations (327/333/344/366/376/381) carry no eval, route_evidence applies to the PATCH only, the runbook is after-deploy and UNTESTED, Q2 has no tooling, the fingerprint misses effort, max_tokens, gate code and most T8-T10 routes, and reverify never computes prompt_version_mismatch (releases.py:465-476). Judge prompt edits are not gated by a calibration. VERIFIED.

principle_scores.principle: Cost proportional to value
principle_scores.evidence: $5.04 over 3 t9_blog runs and 0 valid verdicts. $2.37 of writer spend after kappa 0.0 was known. Per-item estimate 0.08 against a real 0.16. A judge-only calibration (about $0.04-0.06) would have answered the question first. VERIFIED.

principle_scores.principle: Stable identity of eval items and controls across versions (added)
principle_scores.evidence: Each golden version re-creates item_ids, and the release-0 control points at an older version's baseline, so 0/15 candidates were paired in both S271 runs and criterion_met is impossible (r2.py:310-316, eval_checks.py:477). VERIFIED symptom, INFERRED exact cause.

principle_scores.principle: Statistical power and noise-aware decisions (added)
principle_scores.evidence: Binary per-item paired criterion on about 14 tune and about 4-6 holdout pairs, NOISE_K=1, no A/A' noise measurement. S258 panel SD 1.07-1.60 against ±0.15 bars, and a minimum detectable effect of about 0.7-0.9 on 24 blogs. Critic vote 2 estimates P(pass | calibrated judge) at about 3-30%. VERIFIED/INFERRED.

principle_scores.principle: Ground-truth quality (added)
principle_scores.evidence: 1 human label in the blog golden set, and it is a test stub. 1 human label on live blog pieces in 60 days. All 50 a1 labels are agent_panel. Panel vs human about kappa 0.40. The labels contradict each other on identical defect types (004 vs 019, 017 vs 020, 011 vs 012). VERIFIED.

structural_flaws: The measuring instrument is not fixed. The eval judge is whichever rung of the 4-model writing_memory_eval route answers (acc3 refused, then gpt-6-luna-openai, then nova-lite when cut). Neither the model nor the connection is part of judge_version or prompt_version (eval_judge.py:169-180, r2.py:243-251), and nothing refuses a mixed-judge run. Before/after numbers and calibration history are therefore not comparable. VERIFIED.

Verdict authority sits in an LLM's holistic judgement under a rubric that diverges from the product policy. The rubric's rule 2 plus the fact.embellish definition turn any evaluative phrase into a fail. The source-fidelity Part A (background on named places) is missing. No code rule maps claims to the verdict. Fixing this has been attempted by editing prompt prose four times (S255, S256, S258, S271) instead of moving the decision into code. VERIFIED.

Policy exists in 5 or more divergent copies that the harness compares against each other: writer prompt, taxonomy.yaml definitions, LABEL_RUBRIC/labels.RUBRIC, T10 gates (F2_superlatives style-only), the writer SCOPE text read by the judge, and the S223 fidelity memory note. A label made under one copy is measured by a judge reading another. VERIFIED.

Ground truth is agent-made, tiny, failure-biased, contradictory and item-level. 1 human label on blog, and it is a test stub. 17/18 agent_panel. Selection uses tags held/known_failure. Identical defect types are labelled pass and fail on different items. RELABEL_SOURCES blocks fixing the stub. Labels at item level cannot be reused when the policy changes, so every policy decision invalidates the set. VERIFIED.

Calibration is circular and unpowered. The same 18 items are used to tune the rubric, to calibrate, and as the R2 gate. One vote per item, no test-retest, and kappa alone with no per-class recall bar. One item flip moves kappa across 0.6 (sim3: best subset flips at t9b-004/018). VERIFIED.

Spend is ordered before evidence. Calibration does not gate writer spend (r2.py:490 runs after judge_counts=false). The cheap judge-only harness (judge_compare) cannot test the live judge (acc3-only, refuses *-openai). Q2 (judge re-score before merge) has no tooling. R1 (re-score old outputs) does not exist. So the only tier that runs is the most expensive one. VERIFIED.

The comparison does not measure the change under test or what ships. T9 candidates are first drafts with no T10, repair or FAQ steps, against repaired final controls. Release-0 controls are stale pre-v2/pre-AA-790 outputs, and release 0 has carried reverify=true since 27/10 with no regenerated controls. a1 controls are 44/50 heavy-fail pre-v2 pages. VERIFIED.

Control identity is unstable. Item ids change with each golden version, and control_run follows the active release's eval run (an older baseline), so 0 candidates are paired and criterion_met can never be true. The run would have ended invalid or fail even with a perfect judge. VERIFIED symptom.

The decision rule is noise-dominated. Hard stop 1 fires on any new hard class from a judge told to report classes 'also when pass'. The paired binary criterion uses about 14 + 4-6 items with NOISE_K=1. There is no A/A' noise arm and no pre-registered meaning of 'fail'; the runbook maps fail to 'revert or run again', which invites reruns. VERIFIED/INFERRED.

Change control covers only writing-memory Releases, not the configuration that actually changes behaviour. Prompt, model, route, effort, max_tokens, thinking and mode-flag changes ship via migrations and env with no eval (327/333/344/366/376/381). current_fingerprint sees only 2 routes plus the golden set and taxonomy, and reverify_reasons never emits prompt_version_mismatch. Stored outputs before 31/10 carry no prompt_version or effort. VERIFIED.

Coverage collapses outside t9 blog/social. t2 has 8 usable pairs, under MIN_KAPPA_PAIRS, so it can never count. a1 controls are stale. No a1/t2 R2 run exists. route_evidence for these writers can only ever be break-glass. VERIFIED.

'Green' replays are partly fake. The R0 baseline and the proposed reruns pass through stored F9 verdicts, so a judge change cannot show. Gate inputs are rebuilt by two or more copies of run_write_background with no parity test. VERIFIED.

The judge sees different evidence from the labeller by construction. judge_source_text clips (SEED 16k) while panel_source_text is uncut; output is silently cut at 9k with unlabelled fields. About 22 of 119 claims come from input defects. VERIFIED.

The learning loop can change prompt and gate through data. An active L0 lexicon rule adds a 'Never use' prompt line and a blocking F2_lexicon finding with R0 plus one click (no R2, no shadow, no PR). Human-gated and narrow, but it creates a hold source with unmeasured precision, outside the writer fingerprint. INFERRED that no rule is active today (not checked live).

Eval data and cost models live outside review. The active fixture 1.3.0 sits in gitignored .tmp-session, while older fixtures sit in the public root repo. Cost estimates are hand-set constants (0.08 vs a real 0.16), so budget_cap/invalid is guaranteed, and after() invalidates finished runs on overshoot. VERIFIED.
must_keep: Release activation evidence checked twice: releases.evidence_problem (API 409) + CIS 287 CHECK/trigger (DB); one human click; nothing auto-activates; seeded-fault or code-train runs can never be evidence (release_id check, CIS 292).
Release 0 as a proven no-op (wm20 byte-identical replay over >= 20 inputs + test_aa919_release0_replay / test_aa920_injection).

Rollback paths: one-click rollback, post_activation check with automatic pointer rollback, weekly KPI soft stops with Wilson bounds and minimum samples, the keep override, the disagreement queue as human-label intake.

Calibration runs on every run, with MIN_KAPPA_PAIRS, MIN_KAPPA_PER_LABEL and per-stratum kappa reporting (eval_checks.judge_counts, kappa_by_stratum). Keep the 0.6 bar or tighten it with per-class recall; never loosen it to make a run pass.
Both arms judged by the same judge in the same run (rejudge), the never-early-stop-on-success rule, and holdout spent only after tune passes.
Deterministic hard stops in code: qa_artefacts (hard stop 3), isolation_probe (hard stop 2), injection traps; shadow restricted to these checks on real inputs.
Judge family != writer family, enforced at route level before spend and at call level per verdict (family_rule, r2.check_judge_family, _judge_family).

Ledger-backed spend: every call via LLMClient and bind_eval_stage under the eval label with quality_signal.eval_run, the per-run cap read from llm_call_log, the $25 month cap over MEMORY_STAGES, and lost-row detection in eval_run_report.
The judge must quote the OUTPUT phrase behind each class (unsupported_claims); claims are stored per row. This is the raw material for claim-level labels and a code verdict rule.
labels.RUBRIC == eval_judge.LABEL_RUBRIC enforced by a test (the pattern to extend into one policy file); the panel pack hides pipeline verdicts (PANEL_HIDDEN_KEYS/TAGS).
judge_version hashing of system prompt + input layout (extend it with the model; do not drop it).
R0 $0 rule replay with rule_sha staleness, and the L0 constraints (adds a word only, fact gates outrank it, skips brand/CTA/trip name, one-click rollback).

Golden-set import discipline: DRY RUN by default, versioned, one active set per name, the CIS 284 trigger keeping controls honest (no human-edited output as a writer control), and text_guard blocking golden text from the public CIS repo.
Writes stamped with the release fingerprint (items_sha256) on generated_content / tenant_tour_versions.generation_meta / content_piece.writer_input; extend the stamp, keep the mechanism.
Mining guardrails: thresholds counted in code before any paid call, lint (only constrain, PREDICT >= 2 held-out edits), auto-mining off by default, monthly release train.

props.angle:
EVOLVE. Keep the release plumbing, the deterministic checks, the ledger caps, R0, shadow, the family rule and the disagreement queue. Rebuild only the measuring chain: policy, evidence view, judge, verdict, calibration, controls and decision rule. Do it by turning on machinery that already exists but sits unused:
- run_kind 'r1' is already allowed by the CHECK at infra/AA-CIS-Infra/db/migrations/cis/284_eval_golden_set.sql:445, but no code uses it.
- judge_output(model_key=...) already gives a pinned call with no fallback (eval_judge.py:330-353). Only judge_compare uses it.
- calibration.report() already computes confusion, per-class recall, LOO range and AUC (calibration.py:86-128), but only scripts read it.
- ctl_mode 'regenerate' and _control_regenerate already exist for reverify (r2.py:500ff).
- The judge already returns quoted unsupported_claims (eval_judge.py:160-163, _claims :290-300), but they are stored as evidence only.
- The disagreement queue (disagreements.py) already acts as a human-label intake.

The main change in the graph: the LLM stops being the verdict authority. It extracts claims. A code rule driven by the policy file gives the verdict. A judge-only R1 tier with a pinned judge becomes a hard $0-refusal precondition before any writer spend. A useful consequence: release 0 is an empty release, so its first R2 is an A/A' noise run by construction. That makes it the cheapest honest first paid run.

props.quality_mechanism:
Each link in the chain has one owner and one guarantee:
1. Policy. policy.yaml is the only definition of what fails. The rubric, the labels and verdict_rule are generated from it and carry its sha, so a label and a verdict made under different policies cannot be compared without a $0 re-derivation (refused otherwise).
2. Evidence. evidence_view is one builder, and its sha is stored on every label and judge call. Labeller and judge therefore provably read the same bytes, and an over-cap input is excluded instead of clipped.
3. Ground truth. Claim labels are adjudicated by a human on at least 10 items per writer stratum. Item verdicts are derived by code, so contradictions like 004 vs 019 become visible as two claim labels with the same class and different decisions. They are fixed once, and the change propagates.
4. Instrument. The JudgeSpec is pinned and fingerprinted, with no fallback. A calibration_record proves its pass recall and fail recall (each >= 0.75), its kappa (>= 0.6) and its vote stability (>= 0.85) on a gate split disjoint from the rubric_dev split. R2 cannot start without one, and the drift check refuses a judge that moved since its record.
5. Verdict. The LLM only extracts and quotes. confirm_claim verifies in code that the quote exists in the output and that the fact is absent from the source. verdict_rule decides. A noisy, unconfirmed or voice-class claim cannot fail an item or trigger hard stop 1.
6. Comparison. A, A' and B are produced on the same inputs, through the same path, under the same fingerprint-checked config, so the effect is measured against measured noise (A-A'). The decision rule and the action on fail are recorded before the first call, which ends the 'run again' loop.
7. Replay. Every judge call is a cassette, so any later change to policy or verdict rule is re-scored over all history at $0 before any paid run.
8. Change control. The widened fingerprint stamps every production write, and the CI lint ties each kind of change to its cheapest valid tier (R0 / R1 / R2). The release evidence gate (API plus DB) stays the final lock.
Together, a pass means: the instrument is known-accurate, the evidence was the same, the comparison was fair and powered, and the decision was set before the data. Today none of these holds.

props.cost_per_item:
All costs come from the S271 ledger and calib.raw. Nothing in this design was run.
- R0 and cassette re-score: $0.
- R1 judge-only: about $0.002-0.003 per call, so 3 votes is about $0.008 per item and a 17-item calibration is about $0.15.
- R2 drift check: about $0.02 per run.
- R2 first-draft arm: about $0.12-0.16 per write at Sonnet 5.5 effort high (S271: $0.161 per item), plus 3 judge votes (about $0.008), so about $0.14 per arm-item. A + B on 12 items plus a cached A' on 6 items comes to about $4.
- Full-loop T9 arm (phase 2): about $0.28-0.50 per item (INFERRED from the $0.276 upper bound per approved blog and the 55% held share), so a full-loop R2 must stay near 8-10 items per arm to fit the $10 run cap.
risks: Claim-extraction recall. With an LLM that only extracts, a missed claim becomes a false pass. This is controlled by the recall_fail >= 0.75 bar in R1 and by human claim labels, but with 10-12 fail items the bar has wide error (one item is about 8-10 points).

Small-sample circularity remains. Disjoint rubric_dev and gate splits from about 30 blog items still leave a gate split of 12-15. Each R1 pass is weak evidence until the representative stratum grows through the disagreement queue.

policy.yaml is blocked on product decisions: the width of place background, whether the brief counts as source, and whether reflection counts as voice. Until the tech lead decides, P1 cannot freeze, and any rubric written before that will drift again.

Human adjudication time (at least 10 items per writer, about 30 min/week) is the real bottleneck. If it slips, R1 stays agent-labelled, and its record must be marked agent_ground_truth (informative only).

A/A' doubles writer spend on the noise subset. If the noise cache is keyed too loosely (the fingerprint misses a param), a stale noise estimate could pass a real regression. The widened fingerprint must land first (P4 before P5).
The PieceStore refactor (P6) touches the production T9 path. A parity bug would change live behaviour. The 20-piece byte-equal replay gate is mandatory, and full-loop eval waits for it.

The pinned judge is on the OpenAI-direct connection, which has a $10/month hard stop shared with production t10_judge. R1 or R2 can starve production or be starved by it mid-run. The R2 precondition should check OpenAI headroom.

When the acc3 deferral lifts, a better judge model becomes available. It needs its own R1 record. Switching is a judge change and must go through R1 plus the CI token, never silently through the route.

The token-overlap test in confirm_claim can wrongly treat a paraphrased source fact as absent, or a common word as present. Its own precision must be measured on the 119 S271 claims (FREE-2) before hard stop 1 depends on it.
Moving fixtures into the DB removes git history from eval data. The manifest sha in the repo, together with the importer's versioning, must stay the audit trail.

props.angle:
FACTS-FIRST applied to the Writing Lab evaluation and test harness. The harness should stop asking an LLM "is this output good?" and stop treating its holistic verdict as the decision. Every item gets one source-derived, hashed FactSheet (FS), built by code ($0). The writer, every repair, the labeller and the verifier all read that same FS. The LLM does one narrow job: for each output sentence it gives a claim type, the FS line it cites and a quote. A single policy file then decides the verdict in code. Deterministic constraints are checked by code only: meta band, slug, CTA, FAQ count, meals, day count, novel numbers and names, optional-as-included, truncation.

The main benefits:
- Ground truth moves to claim level, so labels survive policy changes: item verdicts are re-derived from claim labels at $0.
- Calibration counts claims (hundreds per writer), not items. This removes the t2 limit of 8 pairs and the one-flip-moves-kappa fragility.
- Each policy decision becomes a $0 replay over stored extraction replies (cassettes) instead of a paid rerun.

Most building blocks already exist, so this reuses them rather than starting over:
- claim_rules.py (F9 v2). Typed, numbered source lines S/L/P/O/F/B/A/T; the extraction prompt; apply_rules, verify_quote and tripwires. It was built in S234 and never wired in. Its paid replay at $0.40 gave V2a 38/38 test-retest, real_kept 75% and over_strict_cleared 72% (docs/audits/2026-10-13-S234-t-series-rounds/05-f9v2-replay.md; claim_rules.py:22-24, :373, :401, :660, :708, :755). VERIFIED.
- s1_facts.build_fact_table plus verify_pointers. A verbatim fact table with pointer proof, already read by S1 writer v2 and brand_fit_v2 (quality/s1_facts.py:510, :545). VERIFIED.
- For the deterministic contract checks: trip_facts (optional-as-fixed, date spans), offered.py (the single included/offered decision), grounding.find_novel_numeric_claims, repair_contract (no_new_specifics, no_truncation, gates_kept) and citation_tags. VERIFIED.
- 127 three-lens claim-level labels from S232 (docs/audits/2026-10-12-S232-t9-social-audit/08-claim-labels.json). The S271 analysis also classified 47 plus 119 judge claims. VERIFIED.

The redesign keeps all the release plumbing in must_keep and replaces only the measuring chain: ground truth, then instrument, then calibration, then control pairing, then decision rule.

props.quality_mechanism:
Output quality becomes reliable because each guarantee has an owner that does not drift.

1. One FactSheet per input, with pointers back to the source (verify_pointers == [] in CI). Writer, repair, labeller and verifier provably see identical evidence: a parity test asserts that all four renders share one fs_sha. So a claim is either backed by a numbered FS line or it is not, and "the judge never saw it" stops being a class of error.

2. One policy file decides what counts as a violation, and it is applied in code. The LLM only types a sentence and cites a line. Code verifies the quote against the FS line (verify_quote), re-types disguised trip promises (tripwires), and maps type × support kind to a verdict. A rubric-wording change can no longer flip the meaning of 'background about a named place'. It becomes a policy_sha change, replayed at $0 over cassettes before merge.

3. Deterministic constraints are guaranteed by code (E1), never sampled from an LLM: numbers and names absent from the FS, optional-as-included, offered status, date spans, meta/slug/CTA/FAQ/meal/day contracts, truncation, QA traces, isolation, injection. A seeded-fault set proves 100% catch.

4. The instrument has a known error rate. A pinned judge_id gets a calibration_record on a sealed GATE split, with per-class recall and precision, false-block rate and test-retest. R2 refuses to spend without one. Claim-level units give hundreds of calibration points, so a single item flip cannot cross the bar.

5. Ground truth is claim-level and adjudicated by the tech lead, so it survives policy changes: item labels are re-derived.

6. Comparisons measure what ships. A, A' and B all run the full loop on the same inputs under recorded fingerprints. A' gives a measured noise floor, the decision rule is pre-registered, and hard stops need code confirmation. A pass therefore means a real improvement, beyond judge noise and the A/A' floor, on the final text.

7. Every behaviour-changing knob is in the fingerprint and gated by the cheapest sufficient tier (T0 free, then T1 cents, then T2 paid). No route, effort or prompt change ships unmeasured. The release gate (API + DB, human click, rollback) stays as the final lock.
props.test_plan:
Phase 1, free ($0, CI and local, no LLM). Pass criteria:
(a) FS parity: for every golden item (t9_blog 18+3, t9_social 13, a1 50, t2 8), the writer prompt input, the repair input, the panel pack and the judge input embed the same fs_sha. verify_pointers == [] on every A1/T2 FS, and no section is clipped.
(b) Policy consumers: a test fails if prompts, claim_rules, quality_gates F9 v2, eval derivation or taxonomy read a different policy_sha.
(c) Seeded-fault set, built by code from stored outputs: inject an invented number, a name not in the FS, optional-as-included, a cut meta/slug, a wrong CTA, a dropped FAQ pair and a present-tense ended role. E1 must catch 100% of them, with 0 findings on the unmodified originals.
(d) Pairing: re-run control selection over stored calib.raw rows with sample_id keys. Expect 15/15 paired, not 0/15.
(e) Fingerprint: replay migrations 366 and 381 against the widened fingerprint. Both must produce a reverify reason; prompt_version_mismatch must appear on a prompt sha change.
(f) Spend guard: an R2 with no calibration_record makes 0 gateway calls (ledger delta 0). An estimate from the S271 ledger predicts within ±20% of the $2.46 runs.
(g) Cassette replay: E3 over stored replies is byte-deterministic. Rerun the S234 V2a replies, if still in .tmp-session/s234, under the new policy file and report real_kept and over_strict_cleared against the 127 labels as the $0 baseline. Not yet confirmed that the replies are still there.

Phase 2, cents (T1/R1). Two pinned non-Anthropic candidates, for example gpt-6-luna-openai and one Amazon/OpenAI alternative, each run on the sealed GATE split (blog ≥20 items, ≥300 claims), 2 votes, about $0.0014-0.003 per call, cap $1 total. Pass for a judge_id:
- blocking-claim recall ≥0.90 on trip_promise/number/location/service_promise
- false-block rate ≤0.10 on adjudicated background_allowed and voice claims
- sentence-type test-retest ≥0.90
- derived item kappa ≥0.6 with ≥3 items per label
- 0 exempt-typed leaks of adjudicated real violations (S234 V2a had place_background 12 and opinion 7; tripwires plus the policy must close these on replay first)
Pick the model by measured per-class recall, not availability.

Phase 3, small paid subset (T2/R2). Only with a valid calibration_record and the full-loop dry mode merged. T9 blog, 12 representative items, cap $10, estimate from the ledger.
- Run 1 is an A/A' null test: the harness must declare 'no change'. That is its false-alarm check; if it flags a difference, the harness is broken and B is not run.
- Run 2 is B, for example effort medium vs high (open since mig 381) or a writing-memory release.
Pass for the harness: 12/12 paired, not invalid, every row has a cassette, the cost estimate is within ±20%, and the decision follows the pre-registered rule. a1/t2 follow the same ladder after re-freeze. No catalogue-wide runs.

props.cost_per_item:
Per eval item:

| Step | Cost per item |
|---|---|
| E1 contract checks | $0 (code) |
| E2 extraction, 1 vote | about $0.0014-0.003 (S234 V2a: $0.10 over 76 calls; S271 judge $0.002-0.003 per call) |
| E4 second vote | only on unconfirmed blocking claims, typically 0-2 claims, under $0.001 |
| Cassette replay | $0 |
| R1 calibration (≥20 blog items, 2 votes, 2 candidate models) | about $0.25-0.50 per model, under $1 total |
| R2 writer arm (T9 blog full loop) | about $0.16-0.30 (first draft at high effort $0.16 measured; repairs and FAQ add some, INFERRED) |

For R2, an A/A'/B run on 12 items is about 36 writer passes plus judging, roughly $6-10. Once A and A' are cached per fingerprint, each further B costs about $2-4. That compares with today's $5.04 for 0 valid verdicts.
risks: Extraction typing can still leak. In S234, V2a typed 12 real violations as place_background and 7 as opinion. Mitigations: tripwires plus quote verification, the per-class leak bar in R1, and a policy that blocks place_background claims whose quote does not verify against a P/L line. If the leaks persist, E4 must cover those types too, which costs more.

Labels still start from agent proposals. If the tech lead's adjudication is skipped or rubber-stamped, ground truth stays weak. The 20% random audit and the recorded panel-vs-adjudicator agreement per class make that visible but do not prevent it.

The FS builder could omit something the writer really used, such as route text or brand lines, and so create false 'unsupported' claims. The parity test and verify_pointers cover the render, not completeness. A coverage check is needed: every writer-input section must map to an FS kind.
Goodhart risk: a blocking-claim count rewards bland text. Add a warn-only voice/usefulness metric, plus a small human preference check (5 pairs) on any B that wins, before a release is approved.

Pinned judge availability: acc3 refuses GPT-6 and Claude 5.x, so the pinned E2 model is likely gpt-6-luna-openai on the vendor API. The vendor_last_resort data rule must permit eval data (synthetic audit tenants). Verify this before Phase 3.

The full-loop dry mode duplicates production wiring. Without one shared input builder and an injected store it becomes a third copy of run_write_background (S218 lesson). It must be the production function with a store seam, not a re-implementation.
The policy decisions (background scope, brief as source, reflection) are open. Phases 1-5 depend on the tech lead's answers. A wrong policy is measured precisely but is still wrong.

Moving constrained fields to code composition (meta, slug, CTA, FAQ count) belongs to the writer workflows. Until those ship, E1 reports contract violations the writer cannot avoid, which inflates blocking counts equally in A and B. That is acceptable for paired deltas, but misleading as an absolute quality number.
The migration lint may slow urgent route fixes. A break-glass reason is allowed but must be recorded and followed by a T1/T2 run within the same session.

props.angle: EVAL-FIRST. The current harness puts an uncalibrated, unpinned LLM in charge of the verdict and then spends writer money to find that out. The fix is to turn that order around. (1) Write down a quality contract: one policy file with claim classes, severities and a verdict rule run by code. (2) Build a labelled corpus at claim level with stable item identity. (3) Build one judge instrument: pinned, run with 3 votes, storing every raw reply as a cassette, and calibrated with per-class precision and recall. (4) Only after that, run paid writer comparisons. Each tier has to pass at $0 or a few cents before the next one may spend. The LLM's only job is to extract and classify claims and quote them; code confirms the quotes, applies the policy and decides. The same instrument and corpus calibrate every LLM gate in production (T10 F9, S1 judge), so a gate with no measured precision and recall runs warn-only. Code verified at CIS f7d310db.

props.quality_mechanism:
The design has four guarantees, and each one is enforced by code.

(1) Policy consistency. One policy.yaml renders the writer, repair, panel, judge and F9 rubrics. A test fails if any consumer embeds a stale rendering. Item verdicts come from code (verdict_rule), so the writer's allowance ("background about named places is fine") and the judge's rule cannot diverge again.

(2) Known instrument error. A judge_id is fixed by its prompt, layout, model, connection, effort, tokens and number of votes, and it cannot fall back to another model. It counts only after R1 has measured per-class precision and recall, pass-recall and fail-recall, mutant recall and test-retest agreement. That measurement uses claim labels it never saw while its rubric was being written. Holding the GATE split separate stops rubric tuning from inflating the result.

(3) Valid comparisons. The arms are paired on (sample_id, input_sha256). The control is the current production config (its config_fp must match), and every arm runs the full shipping path. A'-A gives a noise bar. The pre-registered SWC delta rule turns per-item claim counts into a decision with stated power. Hard stops are deterministic, or code-confirmed when they come from claims.

(4) No unmeasured change reaches production. Every write carries config_fp and the answered model. Each change class maps to a required tier: R0 at $0, R1 for cents, R2 only for writer changes. A migration or PATCH without a matching eval run id is refused unless a break-glass reason is recorded.

Spend order is enforced by preconditions: R2 refuses at $0 unless a calibrated judge_id and a ledger-based estimate within the cap exist. A failed instrument therefore costs cents, not dollars. Cassettes let any later rule or policy change be re-scored for free, so the harness gets cheaper as it is used.

What is kept unchanged: the release evidence gate (API plus DB trigger, one human click), release 0 as a proven no-op, shadow, post-activation rollback, the ledger caps, the family rule, the deterministic hard stops, and mining guardrails.
props.test_plan:
Stage A: free replay ($0, CI or SELECT only). Pass criteria:
(a) Unit tests of verdict_rule on every synthetic_examples positive/negative pair in policy.yaml, and on hand-written PLACE_BACKGROUND and VOICE cases, which must pass. 100% required.
(b) A render-hash test: every prompt and rubric consumer embeds the current policy_version.
(c) A parity test: build_eval_view equals production gate inputs on 20 stored pieces. Byte-equal fields required.
(d) A pairing dry run of R2 against golden 1.3.0, with no model calls: paired == number of items.
(e) A cassette replay of the stored claims from runs 858c8bf6 and 08c34cb4 (they are in calib.raw) under the new verdict rule, plus code quote confirmation. Expect fewer claims on the PASS labels (the earlier analysis estimated 79-91% of them were false positives) and item kappa > 0.3. This shows the code rule beats the LLM verdict before any spend.
(f) A config_fp diff test: replaying migrations 381/382 as fixtures must flag effort, max_tokens and the route as reverify reasons.
(g) A seed-fault run proves the stop mechanics with no evidence written.

Stage B: rejudge for cents. R1 on CAL plus about 20 MUTANTS, 3 votes, pinned. Candidate judges: gpt-6-luna-openai, gpt-5.6-luna when acc3 serves it again, and nova-pro as the non-OpenAI fallback. All of them differ in family from Anthropic writers. Cost: about 40 items x 3 votes x $0.003, so about $0.35 per model and at most about $1.1 in total. Pass criteria: kappa >= 0.6, pass-recall >= 0.75, fail-recall >= 0.75, mutant recall >= 0.9 with zero claim-count rise on clean originals, hard-class precision >= 0.7, and vote agreement >= 0.8. Then a single GATE-split confirmation (about $0.15) must land within 0.1 of the CAL kappa. Run the same R1 on the production F9 judge to give it a precision number, or demote it to warn-only.

Stage C: small paid subset.
C1. A null-change R2-gate on t9_blog, where B = the current production config and A = stored finals with a matching config_fp ($0). B covers 8 GATE items and A' covers 4, at about $0.30 per full-loop item, so about $4 including judging. The run must end 'non_inferior' with paired == n, stop_reason completed, 0 HS1, and cost within ±25% of the ledger estimate. This proves the instrument does not false-fail.
C2. Only after C1 passes: the real candidate on 15 GATE items plus 8 A' items, about $7-8, under the $10 cap.
C3. a1 and t2 R2 runs only after their golden v2 re-freeze and an R1 for those strata.
All runs stay within the $25 month cap and every call goes through the gateway ledger.
props.migration_path:
The order keeps every step useful on its own. Spend happens only after the $0 steps pass.

P0 ($0, about 1 PR, fixes in the current graph):
- Pair controls on sample_id+input_sha256 (r2.py:726).
- Refuse before writer spend when the judge does not count (r2.py:490).
- Build cost estimates from the ledger.
- after() keeps the verdict of a finished run.
- Pin the judge model through model_key and add it to judge_version.
- Add the CUT_MARK, field labels and refuse-over-cap behaviour to the judge input.
- Store raw replies and all claims (cassette table migration, CIS-owned).
- Compute prompt_version_mismatch.
After P0 the existing R2 can at least produce a valid, if noisy, verdict.

P1 ($0 plus tech-lead time):
- policy.yaml with claim classes and verdict_rule; switch parse_verdict to claims-only.
- Render the rubrics and add the hash test.
- Claim label store and adjudication UI. Reuse the Writing Lab disagreement queue, seeded from the stored claims of 858c8bf6/08c34cb4 plus a panel pass.
- Golden v2 re-freeze: a representative stratum from stored v2 production outputs, mutants, fixed splits, and a private fixture store.
- Decisions the tech lead must take, via the shared decision page: the scope of PLACE_BACKGROUND, whether the brief counts as a source, and whether reflection counts as VOICE.

P2 (about $1-2): the R1 job, the judge_compare rewrite, calibrating the candidate eval judges and the production F9 judge, and writing the calibration rows into policy/thresholds. F9 is demoted to warn-only if it fails.

P3 ($0):
- Widen config_fp and stamp it on writes with the answered model and fallback_used.
- Change-control lint on migrations and PATCH, with R0a/R0b in CI and the R1-before-merge runner.
- Make L0 warn-only and add its hash to the fingerprint.
- Rebuild release 0's controls as arm A, which clears reverify.

P4 (about $4 then about $8): the full-loop dry mode for T9, then the null-change R2-gate (C1), then the first real candidate (C2). After that, A1/T2 dry mode plus golden v2 for a1/t2, then their R1 and R2.

Shared with the blog and tour plans (fix once): the gateway pin and the no-silent-fallback rule, policy.yaml, build_eval_view, cassettes, config_fp, and the claim label store.
props.cost_per_item:
- R0 tiers: $0.
- R1: about $0.003 per judge call (calib.raw shows $0.002-0.003), so about $0.01 per item with 3 votes. A 40-item calibration with mutants costs about $0.35 per judge model.
- R2-gate t9_blog: the full production loop is about $0.25-0.40 per item (INFERRED: the first draft measures about $0.16 at effort high; repair, FAQ and F9 add more), plus about $0.02 for judging.
- Arm A from stored finals with a matching config_fp: $0.
- Typical decisive run, 15 B + 8 A' items: about $7-8, against today's $5.04 for 0 valid verdicts.
- Null-change self-test: about $4.
- a1: about $0.15+ per item for the writer, plus about $0.50 DFS per tour if prefetch is not cached. Cache it in the golden input to keep it at $0.
- Mutants: judge cost only, about $0.01 each.
risks: Labelling load on the tech lead. Claim-level adjudication of the disputed spans plus 20 random spans per stratum is still a few hours per writer. If it slips, ground truth stays agent-made. Mitigation: mutants give exact labels for fail-recall, and adjudication covers disputed spans only.

Judge choice is narrow. acc3 denies Claude 5.x and GPT-6, and the judge must not share the writer's Anthropic family, so in practice the candidates are OpenAI-direct or Nova. If none passes R1, every LLM gate becomes warn-only and holds fall to deterministic gates. That is honest, but quality checks get thinner until a judge passes.

Claim extraction measures commission defects well and omission or framing defects (scope.framing, missing day, weak structure) poorly. Those must stay in code (day_oracle, repair_contract) or remain informative. Otherwise SWC under-counts them.

Statistical power is still modest. With 15 GATE items and an A' noise bar, only effects of about 1 confirmed claim per item can be detected. Small regressions pass as non-inferior. Accept this explicitly in the pre-registered decision, or grow the GATE split over time from the disagreement queue.

The full-loop dry mode for T9/A1 needs a store-injection refactor of run_write_background and the S1 graph. If the dry path drifts from production, the eval measures a third thing. A parity test on 20 stored pieces is mandatory.

Bootstrapping: rendering the rubrics from policy.yaml changes the writer and F9 prompts, which is itself a writer change. Accept the first rendering through the C1 null-change run as the new baseline config_fp, not as a free pass.
A wider config_fp can make reverify noisy, because many keys now change. Map each key to its required tier so a gate-code change asks only for R0b, not R2.
Using the same claim schema for the eval judge and production F9 risks shared blind spots. Keep the models different and audit regularly through mutants and human-adjudicated disagreements.
Running R1 before merge against a dev-<sha> image needs an ECS one-off task path. That is infra work, and feasibility is INFERRED.
Some figures here are INFERRED, not measured: the full-loop cost per item and the expected kappa gain from code verdicts. Stage A(e) and C1 exist to measure them before any larger spend.

The measuring chain (policy -> ground truth -> judge -> verdict -> calibration -> controls -> decision rule) is wrong by design. That is why R2 cannot produce a valid verdict for any writer, and why every policy tweak restarts the loop:
- The policy exists in 5 or more divergent copies.
- An unpinned 4-rung judge decides the verdict holistically under a rubric that lacks Part A.
- Labels are item-level and agent-made; the only human label is a test stub.
- Calibration is one vote on the same 18 items that tune the rubric and gate the release.
- Writer money is spent after calibration has already failed (r2.py:478-492, VERIFIED).
- Pairing is keyed on per-version item_ids, so 0 pairs and an impossible pass (r2.py:326 and :726-738, VERIFIED).
- First drafts are compared against stale repaired finals.
- One judge flip decides the run.
- Change control covers only Releases, while migrations 327/333/344/366/376/381 changed routes and effort unmeasured.

Patching prompt prose again (as in S255, S256, S258, S271) will not converge. The decision has to move from LLM prose into code under one policy file, with a pinned, calibrated extractor.

arch.target_architecture_md:
# Target architecture: one writing-quality system for S1, T2, T9 and the Writing Lab

Status: proposal for the tech lead, S271, 06/11/2026. It is based on four design reviews (blog, S1, T2, eval) and spot checks at CIS f7d310db.
Verdict for all four workflows: **RESTRUCTURE in place**. This means no parallel v2 graph, except T2: T2 is a set of `is_tenant_rewrite` branches inside the A1 graph and gets its own small linear orchestrator.
What is reused unchanged:
- the gateway and ledger
- writer v2 (S1)
- the T8 angle contract with Jev rank and human pick
- choose_keyword
- sentence-level, source-cited repair with splice_checked / repair_contract
- the deterministic finalizers
- the degraded registry
- the release evidence gate
- Q0 CI
- tenants always receive content

## 1. Why fixes loop (common root cause, VERIFIED in all four reviews)

1. **Policy has no single source.** It is restated in ~10 places per workflow, with 4+ meta bands. Each fix lands in one copy and contradicts another.
2. **Facts have no single source.** Writer, gates, repair and eval judge each see a different, silently cut version of the source. In T2 that source is lossy master prose with "Inclusions: None".
3. **The deciding signals are unmeasured.**
   - T9: an uncalibrated, unpinned F9 judge decides 34/99 holds and is answered by its 3rd rung.
   - T2: a source-blind brand judge drives status and retries.
   - S1: a saturated score (avg 9.99) cannot fail.
   - Writing Lab: the eval judge has kappa -0.07..0.32 on 1 human label.
4. **Repair is global or source-blind, and the detector that fired is not re-run.** One example is S1 flag_fix and revalidate (graph.py:1397-1398).
5. **Exits do not share one contract.** S1/T2 hitl goes straight to END, and T9 edits text after the last gate.
6. **Behaviour changes outside eval.** Routes, effort, env flags and writing memory all change it, and no replay is fake-proof: replays reuse stored F9 verdicts.

Every new failure therefore became one more gate or one more fixer.

## 2. Layers

```
L8 Change control   config_fp | migration lint (-- eval / -- break-glass) | eval tiers | writing-memory gating
L7 Record + replay  cassettes | manifests | findings vectors | R0a/R0b/R0c | R1 | R2 (A/A'/B, null run) | mutation suites
L6 Exit             final_contract (read-only, the one exit) -> status + typed review queue
L5 Route + repair   route_table (from policy) | repair operators | budget | stop rule | truth_cut
L4 Verify           contract_check (code) -> claim engine C2 (pinned instrument / Jev for A1) -> C3 code confirm -> C4 2nd vote
L3 Compose          slot composers (fact lines, day skeleton, inclusions, seo_fields, slug, CTA, FAQ plan) + one ordered normalizer
L2 Evidence         FactSheet (one schema, tour + route builders, persisted, fs_sha) + evidence_view renderer
L1 Policy           writing_policy.yaml -> compiler (prompts, rubrics, RulesConfig, route rows) | thresholds.yaml measurement records -> gate modes
L0 Gateway          one LLMClient + ledger | pinned instrument routes | same-model truncation retry | role-wide fallback marks | per-call family check | cassette
```

**Data flow.** raw source -> FactSheet (persisted, fs_sha) -> content plan / slots (code) -> ONE writer call, narrative only, through the gateway -> compose + normalize (code) -> contract_check + claim engine (same FactSheet) -> route table -> local repair on flagged spans -> re-verify changed units -> final_contract -> save. The tenant always receives the text; for T2/T9 the reader is protected by truth_cut of residual enforce-class promises. Last comes the record: cassette, findings vector and config_fp.

**Two kinds of judge.**
- **Verifiers** (claim engine, Jev a1_claim_supported) may hold, but only with a passing measurement record and a pinned instrument.
- **Assessors** (S1 brand_fit, T2 voice, T9 F9_brand_style / F15) are report-only. They never route, retry, select or hold until kappa >= 0.6 on labelled pairs, and they live in the Writing Lab.

## 3. Key cross-cutting rules (resolving conflicts between the four picks)

| Topic | Blog pick | S1 pick | T2 pick | Eval pick | Resolution |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Policy file | writing_policy.yaml | services/quality/writing_policy.yaml | policy rows | services/quality/policy.yaml | **one file `services/quality/writing_policy.yaml`**; taxonomy.yaml keeps class ids/definitions rendered from it |
| Calibration record | measurements.yaml | thresholds.yaml fields | taxonomy blocks | eval_judge_calibration table | **thresholds.yaml rows** for gate modes (already has the calibrated fields, 20/20 false VERIFIED); `shared.eval_judge_calibration` DB rows for instrument runs, referenced by run_id. No third file. |
| Promotion bar | P>=0.90, LB>=0.80, n>=20 | P>=0.90, LB>=0.75, n>=15 | P>=0.90, n>=15, agreement>=0.7 | claim precision>=0.70 + kappa | **Deterministic detector: P>=0.90, Wilson-95 LB>=0.75, n_pos>=15, labeller agreement>=0.7. LLM instrument (hold-capable): P>=0.90, LB>=0.80, n_pos>=20, test-retest>=0.95, hard-subset recall 10/10. Definitional classes: Q0 red-on-base proof. Eval R2 instrument: kappa>=0.6, recall_pass/fail>=0.75, mutant recall>=0.90, GATE within 0.1 of CAL.** |
| Fact source | FactPack from grounding_text_from + s1 anchoring | persisted FS from s1_facts | SourceBundle raw + master_drift | FactSheet wrapping both | **one FactSheet schema and module, two builders, one persisted row**; T2 adds BASE + master_drift; eval uses evidence_view() |
| Writer output | prose + [F:]/[R:] tags + 3/3 header | W unchanged, code appends fact lines | narrative slots JSON + 3 meta candidates | n/a | **One principle: code owns constrained slots, the LLM writes narrative only, bounded fields come as candidates.** The shape stays per workflow (tagged prose for T9, W prose for S1, slots for T2), to keep voice risk low. |
| Claim verifier | pinned t10_verify entailment on cited lines + V2a for untagged | Jev a1_claim_supported + Q-promise shadow | code verify + LLM t2_verify shadow | E1-E4 extractor + code confirm | **One claim engine module (C1-C4).** One pinned non-Claude instrument for T9/T2/eval. Jev stays C2 for A1 only (already calibrated on A1, keep-Jev rule). |
| Eval judge vs production verifier | n/a | n/a | n/a | same engine | Same engine and instrument (narrow non-Claude pool). Independence comes from claim-level human/adjudicated labels and the C4 second vote, never from the instrument agreeing with itself. INFERRED risk, accepted; recorded in the ADR. |
| Truncation retry owner | gateway | gateway | gateway | n/a | **gateway**; token_budget becomes a ceiling calculator only |
| Loop bounds | 2 repair rounds | 2 drafts, 1 repair round | writer<=2, repair<=3 | n/a | per-profile numbers in policy: writer<=2 (2nd only for structural regen), repair rounds S1=1 / T2=2 / T9=2, round 2 only on strict shrink, budget persisted across job retry |
| Product consequence | truth_cut, held = label | review queue (A1 is not tenant-facing) | needs_review shown as ready | n/a | A1: review queue blocks publish of the Master. T2/T9: tenant receives, residual enforce-class promises are truth_cut by code, held/needs_review = label only (decision D6). |

## 4. Final graph per workflow

Legend: [C] code $0, [L] LLM through the gateway (pinned/stamped), [J] Jev, [H] human. Every node writes findings + hashes to the record.

### 4.1 S1 platform tour rewrite (A1 Master)

       elephant wording over all fields -> SOURCE_HOLD (enforce only after precision read) | POLICY_HOLD flag | ok      ($0 writer spend on hold)
[C/J] N2 seo_prefetch (unchanged)

       empty cut -> same model 2x; fallback writer = DEGRADED)

[C] N6 contract_check -> classes REGENERATE | LOCAL | POLICY_HOLD | REPORT  (quality_score = report column only)
    REGENERATE and drafts<2 -> N3 with code-built feedback; exhausted -> N9

       Jev a1_claim_supported pinned version; no Jev waiver of deterministic findings; Q-promise shadow
[C->L] N8 local_fix (replaces flag_fix + _rerepair_meta): deterministic edits -> 1 grounding.repair call on enforce-flagged
       sentences with FS quotes -> code delete only for deterministic findings if field keeps >=1 sentence;
       repair_contract after each edit; re-run N6+N7 on changed units; no 2nd round

    -> PUBLISH | POLICY_HOLD | REVIEW(codes) | SOURCE_HOLD | DEGRADED

    human_edit_gate); sentence labels only for reviewer-marked sentences (blanket truth stamp removed)

### 4.2 T2 tenant tour rewrite (own linear orchestrator in services/quality + jobs, behind a profile row, then the default)

### 4.4 Writing Lab evaluation (the test half)
```
POLICY (same file) -> [C] verdict_rule(confirmed claims, struct findings) -> pass/fail + severity-weighted count (SWC)
EVIDENCE evidence_view(FactSheet, labelled output fields); over cap -> item excluded (never cut); same sha for writer, panel, judge
GROUND TRUTH shared.eval_claim_label; strata HARD/REPRESENTATIVE/MUTANTS/TRAPS; splits DEV/CAL/GATE by hash(sample_id); t9b-002 stub revoked
INSTRUMENT = claim engine E1 contract_check -> E2 pinned extraction (no verdict field) -> E3 confirm -> E4 2nd vote on unconfirmed blocking
LADDER R0a cassette rescore | R0b deterministic replay (production builder, PieceStore seam) | R0c lexicon | R1 judge-only calibration
    (writes measurement record; also measures production F9 / S1 judge / T2 voice: no record -> warn-only) |
    R2-dev (cap $3, informative) | R2-gate: $0 refusals (calibrated id, paired==planned on (sample_id,input_sha256), ledger estimate,
    pre-registered decision, no same-fingerprint rerun, 6-item drift check) -> arms A (stored finals at matching config_fp, $0) / A' / B;
    full loop dry run; HS1 = new CONFIRMED trip-promise/checkable claim absent in A and A'; decision non_inferior/improve on dSWC vs 2*SE(A'-A)
KEEP release evidence gate (API 409 + CIS 287), release 0 no-op, rollback, post-activation check, KPI soft stops, disagreement queue
```

## 5. How write / judge / test fit together
- **Write**: the generator only writes narrative inside a plan whose facts, slots and bounded fields are fixed by code. The writer's prompt is compiled from the same policy that the gates enforce. First-pass yield becomes the main writer metric, instead of repair volume.
- **Judge**:
  - Deterministic contract_check first.
  - Then one pinned claim instrument that sees exactly the FactSheet the writer saw, with code confirmation of every quote.
  - Hold power comes only from a measurement record.
  - Assessors (voice/brand) report only.
- **Test**:
  - Every change runs the cheapest tier that can falsify it, before anything paid: R0 free, then R1 cents, then R2 paid with a null run first.
  - Replay never trusts stored LLM verdicts.
  - config_fp makes every route, effort, prompt, policy or memory change visible, and the lint makes it gated.

## 6. Invariants (enforced by tests/lints)
1. One policy_sha across all rendered artefacts; 0 hand restatements (lint).
2. Every consumer reads the FactSheet by fs_sha. evidence_view parity: no silent truncation.
3. No gate in enforce mode without a passing measurement record (lint).
4. Every path to save/publish/END passes final_contract (topology test). Stored sha == gated sha.
5. A hold-capable verdict comes only from the pinned instrument rung. Any other rung is degraded.
6. No writer route contains the verifier's model family. A per-call family check runs in production.
7. Replay: a cassette miss = needs rejudge, never a pass.
8. config_fp moves on any route/effort/params/mode/policy/prompt/memory change (unit test). Gated migrations carry an eval or break-glass header.
