decisions.question: Place background: how much may the writer say about a named place that is not in the source?
decisions.context_plain: Today this rule is written 6 different ways. Some copies allow background, others punish any year or fact not in the source. This one rule is the biggest driver of disputed fidelity flags across S1, T2 and T9.
options: A: background facts about any place the fact sheet names (history, geography, culture) are allowed; never this trip's activities, services, times or views; numbers and years in background are warn-only
B: as A, but numbers and years in background are not allowed at all (hold)
C: no background beyond the source
decisions.why: It matches the standing source-fidelity rule (background OK, never promise what the source lacks). It keeps voice quality. Numbers are the one risky sub-class, and as warn they can still be measured before they ever hold.

decisions.question: Is the content brief (T8 angle text) a source of facts?
decisions.context_plain: The brief is written by an LLM from the same seed. If it counts as support, a made-up promise in the brief is then 'supported' in the article.
options: A: no; the brief is an instruction only, and support comes only from fact sheet line ids
B: yes, the brief counts as a source
decisions.why: It closes a circular path where one LLM's output certifies another's. The brief is also checked against the fact sheet by tripwires before the paid write.

decisions.question: Reflective sentences (e.g. 'a moment to slow down and take it in'): voice or embellishment?
decisions.context_plain: The eval judge fails these sentences while the product rules allow them. Four rounds of prompt edits have tried to settle this without a written rule.
options: A: voice, allowed, as long as the sentence makes no factual statement about the trip (no activity, service, time or view)
B: embellishment, flagged
decisions.why: It keeps the brand voice and moves the real risk (a hidden promise) to the code tripwires, which catch a promise whatever the sentence type.

decisions.question: Hypothetical framing ('you might spot...', 'perhaps a sunset over...')
decisions.context_plain: These sentences sit between voice and promise.
options: A: warn, unless it names a concrete trip activity/service/time/view, in which case it is treated as a promise
B: always a promise (enforce)
C: always allowed
decisions.why: The PROMISE_FRAME_RE tripwires already make the concrete cases deterministic. The vague cases stay measurable without holding pieces.

decisions.question: One meta description band and one title band for every workflow
decisions.context_plain: There are 4+ meta bands in the code today (130-148, 140-155, 145-152, 140-160). Each stage fights the others.
options: A: meta 140-155 chars, title per the existing seo title fitter band
C: keep per-workflow bands
decisions.why: 140-155 is the band of the deterministic fitter that already runs last (seo_meta_utils.py:21-22). Choosing it removes the LLM re-repair loops without changing published output for most pages.

decisions.question: What happens to tenant content (T2, T9) that still has an unsupported trip promise after the repair budget is spent?
decisions.context_plain: Today 'held' pieces still reach the tenant as ready and can be published. The paid third attempt therefore buys only an admin label.
options: A: code deletes the residual enforce-class sentence before delivery (truth_cut), if the field keeps at least one sentence and the contract still holds; 'held/needs_review' stays an admin label; no publish block
B: also block publish through content_compliance_flag
C: keep as today
decisions.why: It protects the reader without breaking 'tenant always receives content'. It costs $0. A publish block can be added later for enforce-mode classes only, if needed.

decisions.question: Which model is the single pinned claim instrument (the only one that may hold) for T9, T2 and the eval?
decisions.context_plain: Today the T9 fact judge is answered by its third fallback model, unpinned and uncalibrated. acc3 refuses GPT-6 and Claude 5.x for now.
options: A: gpt-6-luna-openai on openai-direct, single rung, no fallback (a miss = unverified); remove it from every writer route; switching to an acc3 or acc2 model later needs a new R1 calibration
B: keep a multi-rung judge route
C: use a Claude model as judge
decisions.why: It is the model that actually answers today (72/72). It differs in family from the Claude writers. Pinning it makes its error rate measurable. C breaks the judge-family rule.

decisions.question: T2 default for elephant-riding tours
decisions.context_plain: The standing policy is 'keep as-is + human review'. T2 has no path for it today, and flag_fix can rewrite the ride text.
options: A: master text verbatim + deterministic brand fields, 0 LLM calls, review row, tenant still receives
B: rewrite with the ride spans locked byte-equal
decisions.why: It is the literal reading of the policy, costs $0 and cannot alter the ride text. B can be added later if tenants ask for branded voice on these tours.

decisions.question: Take the S1 brand judge (s1_judge) off the live path?
decisions.context_plain: It has kappa 0.03, is called twice per repaired tour, decides nothing (report-only) and costs about 10% of S1 spend.
options: A: yes; move it to a Writing Lab sampler of about 20 tours/week, pinned, which returns as a gate only at kappa >= 0.6 on >= 40 labelled pairs
B: keep it live
decisions.why: It saves money and noise with no loss of protection, since it already blocks nothing.

decisions.question: Should the claim instrument used by the eval also be the production verifier?
decisions.context_plain: The pool of non-Claude models we can call is narrow. Using the same engine means the eval could partly measure agreement with itself.
options: A: same engine and instrument; independence comes from claim-level human/adjudicated labels and a second-vendor vote on unconfirmed blocking claims
B: require a different eval model
decisions.why: B is hard to staff with the current model access. A keeps one thing to calibrate. The ground truth comes from labels, not from the instrument.

decisions.question: Tech-lead labelling budget
decisions.context_plain: Today the blog golden set has 1 human label, and it is a test stub. No gate can be trusted without real labels.
options: A: about 2-3 h over 1-2 weeks: adjudicate about 60 blog claims + 10 pieces, approve the S1 L2 labels, settle the T2 disagreements; the agent panel does the first pass; then 10 new objects per workflow per month
B: agent-only labels (marked agent_only, never release evidence)
decisions.why: Hold power and release decisions need human-anchored error rates. Agent-only records can only stay informative.

decisions.question: Caps for the paid writer proofs (W5)
decisions.context_plain: Every paid run comes after free replay and cents calibration, on small fixed samples.
options: A: eval null run <= $5, T9 <= $15, S1 <= $8, T2 <= $5 (total <= $33), each started only after an explicit yes
B: a lower total of <= $15 with smaller samples (weaker statistics)
C: higher
decisions.why: It fits the 'paid runs small subsets' rule and the $25/month eval cap if spread over 2 months. The samples are the minimum that gives a noise-aware decision.

quality_targets: Policy: 1 source file; policy_sha identical in 100% of rendered prompts, rubrics and route rows; 0 hand restatements (lint); 0 of the 16 listed T9 contradictions remain; 1 meta band and 1 title band in code

Gate honesty: 0 classes in enforce/hold mode without a passing measurement record. Deterministic detectors: P >= 0.90, Wilson-95 LB >= 0.75, n_pos >= 15, labeller agreement >= 0.7. LLM instruments: P >= 0.90, LB >= 0.80, n_pos >= 20, test-retest >= 0.95, hard-subset recall 10/10 (today 20/20 thresholds calibrated:false)
Exit integrity: 100% of save/publish/END paths pass final_contract (topology test); stored text sha == gated text sha on 100% of objects; post-gate edits = 0

Contract cleanliness in stored text: 0 violations of CTA x1, FAQ 0 or 3-4, title/meta in band, slug at a word boundary, day count = source, meal/overnight lines byte-equal to the fact sheet, forbidden words 0

Fidelity: 0 unsupported trip activity/service/time/view claims in delivered text, by the verifier and in a human read of 10 pieces per writer change; S1 serious-error rate no worse than the v2 baseline of 0.0015 per sentence; day loss 0
Claim instrument: over-strict flags cleared >= 85% (today 25-26/46); <= 2 leaks per exempt type (V2a: 19); 0 hold verdicts from a non-pinned rung; degraded share < 5% while the pin is reachable

Eval instrument: item kappa >= 0.6, recall_pass and recall_fail >= 0.75, mutant recall >= 0.90 with clean originals unchanged, GATE within 0.1 of CAL; R2 paired == planned on every run (today 0/15); writer $ spent after a failed calibration = $0 (today $2.37); null run (B == A) non_inferior
First-pass yield (no enforce-class violation at the first write): T9 blog >= 30% floor, 50% target (today 4/187); T2 median writer calls 1, max 2

Bounded cost and requests: T9 median <= 5 and worst <= 8 requests per blog (today worst about 38, INFERRED), $/delivered blog <= $0.25; S1 worst <= 12 requests, $/tour <= $0.065 (today about $0.075); T2 worst <= 8 requests (today about 96), $/version median <= $0.10, hard cap $0.25; elephant policy_hold $0 LLM

Routing transparency: 0 silent model downgrades (today 3/3 Sonnet 5.5 empty cuts fell to 4.6 unmarked); 100% of calls stamped with answered model, rung and effort; 0 writer/judge same-family pairs in production; writer cut waste < 5% of writer spend (today $0.98 of $2.71)

Replayability: 100% of new-object LLM calls have a cassette with the raw reply; R0 rerun diff = 0; 0 cassette misses counted as a pass; FactSheet verify_pointers bad == 0 and every excluded fact has a reason

Change control: config_fp moves on any route/effort/params/mode/policy/prompt/memory change (unit test); 100% of gated PRs and migrations carry a matching-tier eval token or break-glass reason; 0 writing-memory activations without replay; reruns of the same candidate + fingerprint without a recorded change = 0

Ground truth: CL-1 >= 60 tech-lead-adjudicated claims + 10 pieces with a frozen 30% held-out split; L2 40-60 S1 v2 tours; t2@2 >= 12 pairs (>= 4 pass, >= 4 fail) + about 150 sentence labels; 0 internal label contradictions; 0 stub labels; >= 20 mutants per writer
Review queue (S1/T2): 100% of review rows carry a typed reason code; S1 review rate excluding POLICY_HOLD no higher than today; no item older than 7 days without an owner alert
Measurement: all metrics per workflow and per channel (blog vs LinkedIn), with every failing class per attempt; unanchored-atom share and master_drift rate reported each run
adr_needed: Root ADR 0020 (new): 'One writing-quality architecture: policy registry, FactSheet, measured gates, single exit contract'. Root level because reversing it touches CIS (all writers, Writing Lab), AA-CIS-Infra (cassette, FactSheet and claim-label tables, migration lint) and the root data standards. It covers: writing_policy.yaml as the single policy source; gate mode derived only from measurement records with the two promotion bars; verifiers vs assessors (assessors report-only); final_contract as the only exit; tenant content truth_cut while held stays a label; the shared claim engine used by both production and eval. Implements root ADR 0001 and cites ADR 0009.

Root ADR 0009 amendment (gateway): the gateway is the single owner of the same-model truncation retry; degraded marks for every role; per-call family check in production; pinned single-rung 'instrument' routes (a miss = unverified, no fallback verdict); the cassette recorder and its retention; no writer route may contain the verifier's family. Amends decision 12 (family rule) and CIS ADR 0005 decision 4 wording.

Root data-standards change (DM-10.x / DM-11.x): config_fp contents and stamping; the migration header rule '-- eval: <run_id>' or '-- break-glass: <reason>' on llm_role_config / stage_model_params / gated prompt changes; cassette and claim-label storage only in the private Dev DB (public-repo rule).

CIS ADR (new): 'Writing Lab evaluation ladder'. R0a/R0b/R0c/R1/R2 tiers, pairing on (sample_id, input_sha256), refusal at $0 before writer spend, A/A'/B with a null run first, claim-level ground truth with DEV/CAL/GATE hash splits, measurement of production LLM gates by R1. Amends CIS ADR 0010 (governed writing memory): L0 is warn-only and activation is gated by R0b + R1 (+ R2 for writer prompts).

CIS ADR (new): 'S1 control plane'. Persisted FactSheet, contract_check routing instead of quality_score, local source-aware repair replacing flag_fix / _rerepair_meta, source_gate, s1_judge off the live path, typed review queue with POLICY_HOLD, A3 atoms from the FactSheet.

CIS ADR (new): 'T2 as its own linear orchestrator'. Raw-row SourceBundle with master as voice base and master_drift marks, code-composed slots, one writer call, VersionBudget with resume-from-best, the elephant policy_hold default, one versioned T2 profile row replacing the env flags.

CIS ADR amendments for T9: CIS ADR 0011 (the t9 FAQ question filter becomes rank-only inside the code-decided answerable set; t9_faq_answer_fit removed) and CIS ADR 0009 (F17 offered moments: F17/F18 become claim-engine rules that fire only when the cited lines lack the item).
arch.summary_vi:
Kết luận chung: cả bốn workflow (S1 viết lại tour gốc, T2 viết lại tour cho đại lý, T9 blog/social, Writing Lab đo chất lượng) đều nên TÁI CẤU TRÚC tại chỗ, không viết lại từ đầu. Phần viết và nhiều mảnh code đang tốt, giữ lại: writer v2, sửa từng câu có dẫn nguồn, các bước code cố định, gateway và ledger, cổng phát hành của Writing Lab.

Vì sao sửa mãi không dứt: cả bốn workflow cùng một gốc lỗi.
- Luật viết bị chép ở nhiều nơi, mỗi nơi một kiểu.
- Mỗi bước nhìn một phiên bản "nguồn" khác nhau.
- Thứ đang quyết định giữ bài là judge LLM chưa hiệu chỉnh, hoặc một điểm số không bao giờ trượt.
- Nhiều lối ra bỏ qua bước kiểm.
- Thay route, effort, cờ env đều không qua bước đo nào.

Kiến trúc chung đề xuất, mỗi phần chỉ làm một lần, dùng cho cả bốn workflow:
1. Gateway: tự thử lại đúng model khi bị cắt ở trần token, đánh dấu mọi lần rơi xuống model dự phòng (cả judge), ghim một model duy nhất cho judge được phép giữ bài, lưu nguyên câu trả lời thô để phát lại.
2. Một file chính sách viết duy nhất. Prompt, rubric, luật regex và bảng định tuyến đều sinh ra từ file này, CI chặn khi có chỗ chép tay.
3. Một bảng sự thật (FactSheet) dựng bằng code từ dữ liệu gốc. Writer, bộ kiểm, bước sửa và judge eval cùng đọc một bản.
4. Code giữ các ô cố định: dòng bữa ăn, số ngày, meta, slug, CTA, FAQ. LLM chỉ viết phần văn.
5. Một bộ kiểm bằng code chạy trước, rồi đến một model kiểm câu đã ghim. Cổng chỉ được giữ bài khi có số đo precision đạt chuẩn, chưa đo thì chỉ cảnh báo.
6. Một lối ra duy nhất cho mọi đường. Văn bản lưu phải đúng là văn bản đã qua kiểm.
7. Bộ chạy lại nhiều tầng (miễn phí, rồi vài cent, rồi trả phí), không bao giờ dùng lại verdict cũ. Fingerprint bắt mọi thay đổi route, effort, prompt.

Thứ tự làm:
- W0: chặn lãng phí và làm lộ sự thật. Miễn phí, kèm smoke khoảng 0,75 USD.
- W1: file chính sách, FactSheet, lối ra duy nhất ở chế độ chỉ báo cáo. Miễn phí.
- W2: gán nhãn theo từng câu và hiệu chỉnh judge. Dưới 2 USD, cộng 2-3 giờ anh duyệt nhãn.
- W3: nối lại luồng cho T9, S1, T2. Đo bằng chạy lại miễn phí, smoke khoảng 1 USD.
- W4: đưa model kiểm câu đã hiệu chỉnh vào chạy thật. Dưới 0,5 USD.
- W5: thử writer trả phí, mẫu nhỏ. Tổng tối đa khoảng 33 USD, mỗi lần chạy anh đồng ý riêng.
- W6: dọn code thừa và bắt buộc kiểm soát thay đổi.

Anh cần quyết, mỗi câu đã có đề xuất trên trang bấm chọn:
- phạm vi bối cảnh địa danh;
- brief không phải là nguồn;
- câu suy ngẫm tính là giọng văn;
- một dải độ dài meta 140-155;
- với nội dung của đại lý, code cắt câu hứa hẹn sai trước khi giao, chưa chặn publish;
- ghim gpt-6-luna-openai làm judge duy nhất;
- tour cưỡi voi ở T2 giữ nguyên văn;
- bỏ judge S1 khỏi luồng chạy thật;
- thời gian anh duyệt nhãn;
- trần chi phí cho các lần chạy trả phí.

Cần một ADR gốc mới số 0020 (kiến trúc chất lượng chung), một bản sửa ADR 0009 về gateway, và vài ADR trong CIS cho từng workflow.

missing: Channels beyond blog and LinkedIn (VERIFIED). T9 writes 8 channels: CHANNEL_BARS in services/acp_shared/slate.py:115-140 lists blog, linkedin, facebook, instagram, tiktok, email, landing_page, ads. Facebook is the only social channel that is actually published: SUPPORTED_CHANNELS = ('blog','facebook') at services/acp_publish/dispatch.py:30, and the post sends content_text verbatim (dispatch.py:92). Yet channel_spec() returns a spec only for linkedin (services/acp_shared/channel_spec.py:280), and F9_CUT_NOT_HOLD_CHANNELS = {'linkedin'} (service.py:480), so Facebook holds where LinkedIn cuts. The architecture's 'SOCIAL/LinkedIn' profile, its F14 shape asserts and its per-channel metrics leave out the one social channel that reaches the public. The Writing Lab writer t9_social (insertion.py:54, :87-88) lumps all 7 social channels together.

The publish payload is built after any final_contract (VERIFIED). blog_slug() at services/acp_publish/idempotency.py:46-49 cuts the slug at character 60 (mid-word) and adds an 8-char key. The WordPress title falls back to angle_name, which is T8 LLM text, when seo_title is empty (dispatch.py:76). Markdown is rendered to HTML with the AI mark at publish and at export (dispatch.py:84, v1_content_writing.py export). Invariant 4 (stored sha == gated sha) and the 'slug at a word boundary' contract do not cover what WordPress and Facebook actually receive.

Tenant edit paths have no check (VERIFIED). The tenant piece edit PATCH /v1/content/pieces/{id} (v1_content_writing.py:157 -> service.update_piece_content_text) records a signal and an audit row only, and leaves the status unchanged. The T2 version PATCH (v1_tours.py:1342) approves, rejects or edits, and an edit inserts a new version with source 'tenant_edit' with no check. The architecture says 'human edit' passes final_contract but never decides tenant-owned edits. Open cases: a held piece fixed by the tenant stays held; an approved piece the tenant edits to add a false promise goes straight to publish. Invariant 4 is false by construction for edited objects.

Admin edits of tenant content (VERIFIED): POST /admin/.../pieces/{id}/sentences/apply (admin_content_quality.py:610) and /tour-versions/{id}/sentences/apply (:1570). These are T9/T2 exits that the final_contract exit list and the topology test do not name.

Human-authored fact sources and their lifecycle (VERIFIED). Tenant Facts Entries (v1_facts.py; kinds price/season/visa_entry/transfer_time/booking_terms, valid_until) and platform facts (admin_facts.py) are F-lines the T9 writer cites. They are unverified tenant claims and they expire. Admin place-card fact edits (admin_content_quality.py:1873) change P-lines. Admin source edits also exist: raw-tours set-active (admin_pipeline.py:2083) and the tour country PATCH (:4058). The FactSheet has no trust or provenance level per kind (tenant-asserted vs source vs LLM-derived). Nothing re-verifies delivered or published Master, T2 or T9 objects when a fact expires, a card is edited, the source changes or the Master is re-approved. The only fan-outs today are tour retirement (tour_retirement_jobs.py) and the typed 409 atom_replaced (atom_replaced.py).

Re-atomizing breaks in-flight requests (VERIFIED for the mechanism, INFERRED for the scale). W6 rebuilds A3 atoms from the FactSheet, which replaces atom ids. Every open T8/T9 request whose atom is no longer live then gets the 409 atom_replaced (atom_replaced.py:1-30; 'carrying old requests over is AA-990 proper'). The roadmap has no carry-over or migration step.

A0 ingestion is an upstream fact producer that is not measured (VERIFIED). services/ingestion/excel_parser.py:110 uses an LLM column map (build_dynamic_column_map) when the headers do not match COLUMN_MAP, so inclusions/exclusions/itinerary can be mis-mapped into raw_tours, and the FactSheet treats raw_tours as truth. jev_gates.py and near_duplicate.py run Jev decisions at ingestion. There is also a human step, upload-staging/{id}/decide (admin_pipeline.py:1984). No measurement record, cassette or fs-level guard covers these.

Other LLM-produced inputs that gates treat as context but that no measurement record covers. a3_place_card + a3_place_card_check feed the P-lines, which are the very basis of the 'place background' allowance. a3_place_days and a3_place_locate feed the route builder's walk and day mapping. a3_atomize. t8_angle_gen: angle_name becomes the slug base and the fallback title. t7_debate_judge (topic gate). segment_research (keywords). real_questions/question_topup and t9_faq_filter (FAQ question set). DataForSEO prefetch. W1 measures only the unanchored-atom share and pointer failures.

Evidence author family (VERIFIED in SAFE_DEFAULTS role_config.py:136-150; INFERRED for the live rows). a3_atomize and a3_place_card draft on gpt-6-luna, the same family as the proposed pinned instrument gpt-6-luna-openai. The instrument would then confirm writer claims against evidence its own family wrote. The family rule covers writer/judge pairs only, not evidence-author/verifier pairs.

Writing memory: tenant-scope releases (releases.py:540-595 create_draft with scope 'tenant'; insertion slots t2_block and t9_tenant). The architecture's activation gate (R0b + R1, plus R2 for writer prompts) cannot run per tenant within the caps, and no rule for tenant releases is given. Exemplars come from pieces 'approved' by the old uncalibrated F9 (exemplars.py:9-15, :156) and are not re-verified under the new policy_sha/instrument. repair_hint injection (flag_fix_node.py:576, T9 rewrite_with_feedback) loses its host when flag_fix and the rewrite are deleted, and the plan does not say where hints go in the new repair operators. The fact_filter regex (writing_memory/fact_filter.py) is itself a gate with no measurement record.

Runtime change surfaces outside the migration lint (VERIFIED). Route and model changes happen through the admin UI: admin_llm_ops.py:458 (stage model), :523 (route), :635 (switch), :681 (catalog on/off), :1509 (connection switch); admin_llm_route_control.py:118/:128/:152 (save, preset, revert route versions); admin_ai_gateway.py:580 (capacity). Other runtime inputs that change writer output: SEO config (admin_settings.py:155), the AA house style / brand identity editor, the tenant brand pack and the tenant CTA (cta_review_notice.py: exempt, published word for word). config_fp and the '-- eval:' lint see none of these.

Instrument identity is too coarse. A catalog key maps to wire_model / bedrock_profile_ids and to deployments with priorities that can change at runtime (catalog.py:158-175, llm_route_control.serving). The instrument id needs the wire model, deployment/connection row, route-control version and the provider-returned model id, or a vendor alias change silently moves the 'pinned' judge.

Other model paths that bypass the gateway or the exits (VERIFIED). (1) S1 Bedrock Batch: shared/llm_client/bedrock_batch.py, s1_batch.py and the admin POST /s1-batch/submit (admin_pipeline.py:1526) call CreateModelInvocationJob outside LLMClient.generate, so there is no cassette, pin or truncation retry. Refusing build_graph_from_generated does not remove the submit endpoint or the client. (2) A second A2 approve endpoint: /v1/pipeline/review-queue/{id}/approve (v1_pipeline.py:533, legacy SFN token -> process_export). (3) The revalidate job (revalidate_job.py, build_revalidation_graph = validate + judge + brand_audit) is the live human-edit gate of S1 and still uses the uncalibrated judge.

Exits on pause and resume (VERIFIED). A tenant budget stop or a stage switch can stop a job mid-loop: client.py:1357 _tenant_budget_gate (stopped_budget waits for staff approval), and service.py:2562-2576 waits_for_budget_approval / stage_switch / budget_counter. Two things are undefined: the verdict when a verifier call is refused for budget (it must be 'unverified', never a pass), and resume semantics after staff approval.
Jev outage path for S1 C2: jev_unavailable / jev_credit_exhausted / 402 sweep exist, but the S1 graph does not say whether an A1 tour without a Jev verdict ends DEGRADED or REVIEW.

Writers out of scope with no declaration in the ADR: supply_content_writer (AA-835, Booking hotel/service customer copy, sonnet-5-5, services/supply_content/writer.py, human review in admin_supply_content.py:101 publish with no contract check); TripPlanner narration (AA-TripPlanner-Web backend/assembly/grounding.py), which writes from the Master; AA-Partner CRM AI drafts on their own gateway; and aa_content EN/VI (human-written, locale VI). The 'one gateway' and 'one policy' claims hold only if these are named in or out.
Locale: rewrite_language en-US/en-GB (batch_prompt.py:182-185) changes the lexicon and spelling, but the policy, forbidden lists, regex detectors and mutation suites assume one locale.
wrong: The W0 route migration is incomplete against invariant 6 and the nova-lite rule (VERIFIED from the live route rows in pipeline_stats.raw). t8_angle_gen (writer) and t9_repair (writer) also carry the gpt-6-luna-openai rung, which is the proposed pinned verifier. nova-lite is also on t9_faq_filter, t9_faq_answer_fit, t10_claims, t10_adjudicate and writing_memory_mine. W0 lists only t9_write, t2_generate, t10_judge, t2_judge and the eval route.

S0 says unanchored atoms are 'framing only, never sole support for a hold'. That is inverted: an unanchored line must never be the sole support that CLEARS a claim. As written, an LLM-invented atom can certify a writer claim.

Decision D7 (gpt-6-luna-openai on openai-direct as the single rung, no fallback) makes vendor_direct the PRIMARY path for verifying tenant T2/T9 content. That conflicts with the standing vendor_last_resort data rule and the S235 'OpenAI only as last resort' guard (tests/unit/test_s235_openai_last_resort.py, data_scope.py). The decision page does not state this data-rule change, and no ADR item amends it.

W5 assumes arm A = 'stored finals at matching config_fp, $0 where possible'. W1 (FactSheet budget diff, policy compile) and W3 (graph rewire) move config_fp and input_sha256 for essentially every object. Matching controls therefore will not exist, and they need a paid regeneration that the $33 caps do not include (INFERRED).

The Exit-integrity target (stored sha == gated sha on 100%, post-gate edits = 0) is unattainable as stated: tenant edits, admin sentence apply and the publish-time slug/title/HTML transforms are legitimate post-gate changes. The invariant needs a scope ('system-written text') plus a separate rule for human-edited and publish payloads.

config_fp 'ALL route rows on the path' omits the route-control version, the catalog wire_model/deployment rows, brand pack / house style / SEO config shas and the Facts Entries snapshot. All of these change output at runtime without a migration, so the claimed 'config_fp moves on any route/effort/... change' unit test cannot hold.
fix_to_plan: W0: widen the route migration to every route with a verifier-family or nova-lite rung: t8_angle_gen, t9_repair, t9_faq_filter, t9_faq_answer_fit, t10_claims, t10_adjudicate, writing_memory_mine/eval. Add a CI lint that derives this from the live route snapshot instead of a hand list.
W0: delete or gate the S1 Bedrock Batch path (/s1-batch/submit, bedrock_batch.py) and the legacy v1_pipeline approve endpoint. Point the revalidate job at final_contract (REPORT mode first).

W0/decision page: add a decision row on the data rule for the pinned vendor_direct instrument. Option A: accept vendor primary for the verify role with allowed_scopes and an ADR 0009 amendment. Option B: pin an acc2 non-Claude model instead. Update the S235 test accordingly.
Fix S0 wording: anchored=false lines can never be the sole support that clears a claim. A claim supported only by unanchored lines is 'unsupported' (warn or enforce per class).

Add a Publish/Export contract stage after final_contract. Make slug, title and meta single-sourced from the stored gated fields: remove the angle_name title fallback and make blog_slug keep the gated slug, adding the key as a suffix only at a word boundary. Add a post-assert on the WordPress/Facebook payload, with its sha recorded in publish_log.

Add channel profiles for every channel the slate can produce. At minimum, Facebook gets its own channel_spec, shape asserts, a cut-vs-hold decision and labels, because it is auto-published. The rest are declared export-only with warn-only gates. Split t9_social metrics and Writing Lab samples per channel.

Add a decision and a design for human edits. Tenant edits are tenant-owned (BYO): contract_check + claim engine run in REPORT mode, the result is shown as a non-blocking notice, the status is re-derived (a held piece whose residual finding is gone becomes approved), and a new enforce-class promise sets content_compliance_flag. Admin sentence apply goes through final_contract. Scope invariant 4 to system-written text.

Give FactSheet lines a provenance/trust field: source_raw, human_verified, tenant_asserted, llm_derived (atom/place card/day map), external (DFS). Rule: tenant_asserted lines may support claims only about the tenant (price, terms), with valid_until enforced at compose time.

Add a source-change fan-out ($0): when raw_tours, Facts Entries, place-card facts, atoms or the Master change, re-run contract_check/claim-cache on dependent Master/T2/T9 objects by fs_sha. Results become a review row or a tenant notice. Sequence W6 re-atomize with an AA-990 carry-over (re-point open requests to the new atoms by quote match) before the atoms are replaced.

W1 input measurements: add A0 column-map accuracy (log the LLM map plus a human confirm on the upload-staging decide when llm_used), a place-card fact error rate, place_days/locate accuracy on route tours, and angle_name/title leakage. Add the evidence-author family to the family check: the instrument may not verify against llm_derived lines written by its own family, or those lines count as unanchored.

Writing memory: define tenant-release gating. Tenant releases are constraint-only (cut/ban/lexicon); exemplars must pass R0b contract replay on that tenant's last N objects plus the platform R1 record; no per-tenant R2. Re-verify existing exemplars and rules under the new policy_sha (W1) and retire failures. Decide where repair_hint rules plug into the route-table repair operators. Add a fact_filter row to thresholds.yaml.

Change control: extend config_fp and the lint to runtime surfaces. Include the route-control version id, catalog wire_model/deployment rows, brand pack / house style / SEO config / Facts snapshot shas. UI edits of llm-config, route, switch and catalog on gated stages require an eval run id or a break-glass reason in the audited body, and they are frozen during waves. The instrument id hashes the wire_model, deployment and the provider-returned model id.

Define the pause and resume semantics: a verifier refused by the tenant budget or a stage switch gives 'unverified' (never pass), the job resumes from the stored best candidate, and final_contract runs on resume. A Jev outage in S1 gives DEGRADED (no publish).
W5 caps: budget for paid regeneration of arm A controls (or re-baseline A as part of W3 smokes), since config_fp changes invalidate the stored finals.

ADR 0020: add an explicit scope section naming supply_content_writer, TripPlanner narration, CRM AI and aa_content as in or out. Recommended: supply_content_writer becomes a 5th lightweight profile (policy compile + contract_check of numbers/services vs supply facts, warn-only, with human review kept). Add locale (en-US/en-GB) as a policy dimension.
crit.still_loops_because: Even after the restructure, behaviour can still change outside the gated path, and those changes feed back without measurement. Six routes remain: runtime admin route/catalog/connection edits; brand pack, SEO config and Facts edits; tenant-scope writing-memory releases and exemplars approved under the old judge; and ungated tenant/admin edits. The other two are upstream LLM fact producers (A0 column map, place cards, atoms, day maps) that every gate treats as truth, plus publish-time transforms after the last check. So a fix verified by replay can be undone by a non-migration change or by bad evidence. Holds can also flip again whenever the uncovered upstream sources or the Facebook channel produce a failure class that has no profile or label.

missing: M1 Decision page lacks the claim classes the labels actually disagree on (VERIFIED). Decisions 1, 3 and 4 cover place background, reflection and hypotheticals. They do not cover rarity, uniqueness or superlative claims ('difficult to replicate elsewhere', 'a rare experience'), era claims ('barely changed in centuries'), suitability claims ('all suitable for swimming', 'paced to be engaging for children', 'a genuinely good place to begin with children'), or scene staging around a sourced moment ('bicycles leaned against a wall', 'guides quietly note who is comfortable'). The aa900 skeptic vote shows the fixture-1.3.0 labels contradict each other on exactly these types: t9b-004 PASS vs t9b-019 FAIL on uniqueness, t9b-017 PASS vs t9b-020 FAIL on era. The live F9 held_reason texts in pipeline_stats.raw are dominated by them. If policy v1 is frozen without these answers, CL-1 inherits the contradictions and no instrument can reach kappa 0.6.

M2 Nobody owns review capacity (VERIFIED, tour_stats.raw). raw_tours shows 891 published tours with review_status=pending_review and 1 approved, yet all 892 Masters are master_status=active. The design makes A1 REVIEW a publish block and sets the target 'S1 review rate no higher than today'. But nobody reviews today, so REVIEW in practice means blocked forever, which starves T2 and T9 for those tours. The plan does not say who reviews, at what throughput, or what happens to the 891 already-active unreviewed Masters that the W1 REPORT-mode final_contract flags (demote? keep active with a flag?).

M3 The upstream evidence (A3) is unmeasured until W6, yet it is the most expensive input (VERIFIED ledger). a3_place_card_check $9.10, a3_place_card $5.35, a3_atomize $5.21, a3_place_locate $5.07 and a3_place_days $4.35 come to about $31, more than all of t9_write ($21.29). These atoms and place cards feed the T9 route FactSheet, which W2 labels and W4/W5 decisions depend on. W1 counts unanchored atoms but measures no precision for the place-card checker or the atomizer before W2 uses that FactSheet as ground truth.

M4 Citation-tag leakage is a known live defect, but the plan has no guard for it (VERIFIED). A 2026-10-12 F9 audit text says 'the repeated inline reference markers materially disrupt the reading experience', so [R:] markers have already reached delivered blogs. The T9 plan adds [F:]/[R:] tags to all factual prose, yet its post-asserts (CTA, FAQ, bands, slug, length) have no check for 0 tag tokens in stored or delivered text. It also has no tag-coverage metric: a factual sentence the writer leaves untagged falls to extraction mode, the weaker one (recall 34-36/48), so the writer decides which check its own risky sentences get.

M5 Effort on the pinned OpenAI instrument cannot be pinned (VERIFIED). stage_params.py:15-19 and client.py:2623 say the OpenAI and Converse paths send no effort or reasoning field. The instrument therefore runs at the vendor's default effort, which the vendor can change. Yet instrument_id includes effort, and the ledger records efforts='-' for every gpt-6-luna-openai row. The plan also does not record the served wire or snapshot id from the response, so a silent alias move would invalidate the calibration unseen (INFERRED).

M6 The same-family pairs stay live after W0 (VERIFIED route rows). W0 removes gpt-6-luna-openai only from t9_write and t2_generate. It is still a fallback on the writer routes t8_angle_gen, t9_repair, s1_generate, s1_flag_fix, s1_itinerary_nudge, t2_flag_fix and t2_itinerary_nudge. When it answers t9_repair, a sentence is repaired by gpt-6-luna-openai and then verified by the same instrument, which breaks invariant 6 until W6. The evidence producers a3_atomize, a3_place_card and a3_place_dedupe have gpt-6-luna primary, the same family as the instrument. The FactSheet and the verifier then share one model's priors, which the plan does not record as a risk.

M7 writing_memory_mine and writing_memory_eval keep the gpt-5.6-luna -> gpt-6-luna -> gpt-6-luna-openai -> nova-lite chain (VERIFIED route rows). W0 removes nova-lite only from t10_judge, t2_judge and 'the eval route'. Writing memory can therefore keep mining rules from a nova-lite judge (the run 08c34cb4 judge, kappa 0.137) until W6.

M8 The stop rule has no definition of a stable key. 'A round runs only if the previous round strictly shrank the stable-key enforce set' needs a key that survives splice_checked changing sentence count and order. Without one (for example class + evidence_ids + normalized claim text, not sentence_idx), a repaired sentence counts as a new finding. The set then never shrinks strictly, or shrinks only by artefact, and the round count falls back to LLM variance.

M9 Tenant-authored text has no rule at the exit. final_contract runs on 'human edit' paths and truth_cut deletes residual enforce-class sentences. Nothing says that text a tenant wrote or edited in Content studio is report-only and never cut by code. Under the BYO / shared-responsibility rule the tenant owns its edits, so code must not delete them.

M10 There is no power or MDE calculation before any paid R2. With A' noise measured on 6-8 items and a decision rule of dSWC vs 2*SE(A'-A), a noisier instrument widens the margin and makes non_inferior easier. A 12-item null run can then hardly fail, and a real B can hardly show 'improve'. A $0 pre-check from R1 vote variance should decide whether n=12-15 can detect the effect the decision needs, before the cap is spent.

M11 Arm A will not be $0 (INFERRED from the W0 design). W0 widens config_fp to every route row, stage_model_params, mode flags, prompt shas and memory sha. W1 and W3 then change policy_sha and the normalizer. No stored final will match the new config_fp, so arm A must be regenerated at writer cost in every W5 workflow. That roughly doubles the T9, S1 and T2 caps, and the decision page does not say so.

M12 The T9 claim scope for multi-tour routes is undefined. A blog spans several tours. The plan does not say whether a trip promise is supported when ANY tour in the route has the item, or only when the tour the sentence is about has it, nor how the claim engine knows which tour a sentence is about. Without this, F17/F18 'cited lines lack the item' stays ambiguous for route content.

W2 The promotion bars cannot be met with the labels the plan budgets (VERIFIED by Wilson arithmetic). Wilson-95 LB >= 0.80 at observed precision 0.90 needs about 47 flagged items (43 TP). At n=20, only 20/20 passes (19/20 gives LB 0.764). For deterministic detectors at n=15, only 15/15 passes (14/15 fails LB 0.75). The bars also mix metrics: precision LB counts flagged items, while n_pos is a recall denominator. Rows are 'one per class x detector x writer profile', so about 60 adjudicated CL-1 claims spread over 8+ classes and 3 profiles cannot produce one passing LLM row. W4 would then flip zero classes and W5 would run with every fidelity class warn-only. The stated 'P >= 0.90' is decorative because the LB dominates.

W3 Decision 11 (2-3 h of labelling) is underestimated (VERIFIED). In the aa900 skeptic vote, the 3-judge agent panel majority agrees with the final labels at kappa 0.351 (12/17), and the voice lens alone at 0.203. If disagreement goes to the tech lead, most items will be disputed, not about 60 claims. The panel is also Claude labelling Claude-written text. Agreement among same-family lenses is correlated, so the 20% audit must be a random sample of AGREED items with the panel's error rate reported. Otherwise 'agreed' labels are not independent ground truth.

W4 W0's interim T9 'attempt 3 becomes a code truth_cut' breaks the plan's own principle that a gate without a measured record is warn-only. It deletes tenant sentences on verdicts from an uncalibrated, unpinned F9 judge. Live F9 held texts (VERIFIED, pipeline_stats.raw) show it flags place background that is probably true ('Sod Camp sits at the edge of Khövsgöl National Park', 'established in 1992'). It also flags whole sentences that carry sourced facts ('Overnight is in a standard ger ... first experience of camp life'), so a sentence-level cut deletes the sourced overnight fact along with the unsupported clause. Today 'held' is a label only, so this interim makes delivered text worse, not safer.

W5 Decision 6 (truth_cut) uses the wrong unit. Deleting whole sentences removes sourced facts that share a sentence with an unsupported clause, and can leave dangling references ('There, ...'). Clause-level repair, or reciting the FactSheet line, should be tried first. Deletion should be the fallback only when the sentence has no sourced span. Tenant-authored spans must be exempt.

W6 Decision 1 option A collides with the deterministic number detectors. S1 N7 'fail-closed novel numbers' and T9 F1_grounding (live holds: "sentence states ['12'] / ['900'] not present") cannot tell a background year or statistic (1937, 1992, 0.4%) from a trip number. Under 'numbers in background are warn-only', the same sentence is warn in F9 and enforce in F1 or N7. That is the one-rule-several-ways defect again. crit.still_loops_because: Even if the roadmap is executed as written, quality would still fail and fixes would still loop, for five reasons. (1) The policy freeze skips the claim types the labels contradict each other on: rarity/uniqueness/era, suitability and scene staging. The ground truth stays self-contradictory, so no instrument reaches kappa 0.6 and the old prompt edits continue under a new name. (2) The promotion bars need about 47 flagged items per row at P 0.90 / LB 0.80, but the budget is about 60 claims over 8+ classes and 3 profiles. Almost every fidelity class therefore stays warn-only, W4 flips little, and W5 spends money with no hold-capable verifier. (3) T9 entailment mode depends on tagged prose that arrives only in the paid W5, so the instrument that would judge it is never calibrated. Tags have already leaked into delivered blogs, and the plan has no tag-leak assert. (4) The writer prompt stays byte-equal through W4 while the gates move to the new policy, so the writer-vs-gate contradictions, and the repair churn they cause, last until the first paid run. (5) Same-family repair (t9_repair on gpt-6-luna-openai), unmeasured A3 evidence, and an OpenAI instrument whose effort cannot be pinned leave the verifier's view of 'truth' unmeasured or correlated with the writer path. On top of this, the W0 truth_cut lets an uncalibrated judge delete sourced sentences, so for a few weeks the plan makes delivered text worse before it makes it safer.
